having conquered <s>Māra</s>, attaining <s>Sambodhi</s>, one would obtain the state of <s>Buddhahood</s>.
Thus instructed by the worthy teacher, the righteous king,

body.translated_text: <s>Aśoka</s>, together with the assembled people, was delighted and awakened."

body.text: iti śrī svayambhūtpatti kathāyā śrī svayambhū bhaṭṭārakoddeśa pūjāvarṇanā nāma dvītīyo 'dhyāya samāpta /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter named 'Description of the Worship of the Blessed <s>Svayambhū</s>' in the story of <s>Śrī Svayambhūtpatti</s>.
Third chapter, named 'The Draining of the Great Lake and the Establishment of the <s>Dharmadhātu Padmagiri</s> (Lotus Mountain).'

children.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, with joined palms, having approached the city,
bowing to that worthy ascetic, entreated him thus with reverence: // SvayambhuP_3.1 //
"Venerable one, I wish to hear the sacred story of that land.

children.text: tatsamyak samupādiśya saṃbodhayituṃ no bhavān // SvayambhuP_3.2 //
children.translated_text: Having properly instructed us in it, may you enlighten us." // SvayambhuP_3.2 //
Thus entreated by the king, that worthy ascetic of great wisdom,
<s>Upagupta</s>, looking at that lord of men, instructed him thus: // SvayambhuP_3.3 //

children.text: sādhu śṛṇu mahārāja yathā me guruṇoditaṃ /
children.translated_text: "Listen well, O great king! As it was told by my teacher,
so I shall declare it to you, for the enlightenment of all beings. // SvayambhuP_3.4 //
Thereupon the great being <s>Maitreya</s>, that son of the <s>Jina</s>,
bowing again to the Blessed One, spoke thus with joined palms: // SvayambhuP_3.5 //
'O Blessed One, this great water-reservoir, this lake —

children.text: kadā bhūmi pradeśo 'tra kathaṃ jalāśrayo bhavet // SvayambhuP_3.6 //
children.translated_text: when did this region become land, and how did the lake come to be? // SvayambhuP_3.6 //
And at whose time were countries, villages, and the like established?
Please instruct us on all of this and enlighten us all.' // SvayambhuP_3.7 //

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tena maitreyena saḥ sarvavit /
children.translated_text: Thus entreated by <s>Maitreya</s>, that omniscient one,
the Blessed One, looking at that great being, instructed him thus: // SvayambhuP_3.8 //
"Listen well, O great being! What happened here on this earth —
that account I shall declare, for the enlightenment of all beings. // SvayambhuP_3.9 //
In ages past, sixty thousand years of the earth-worlds ago,
there was the Blessed Teacher named <s>Viśvabhū</s>, the omniscient one, // SvayambhuP_3.10 //
the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (king of the law), the great sage, the worthy one, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the guide,

children.text: sarva vidyādhipastāpī saṃbuddha sugato jinaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.11 //
children.translated_text: the lord of all knowledge, the ascetic, the <s>Sambuddha</s> (fully awakened), the <s>Sugata</s> (well-gone), the <s>Jina</s> (conqueror). // SvayambhuP_3.11 //
He, in a city named <s>Anupamā</s>, near the <s>Jina</s> hermitage,
dwelt for the benefit of all beings, together with his assembly. // SvayambhuP_3.12 //
I, <s>Maitreya</s>, was then a lay devotee of <s>Viśvabhū</s>,
a great being named <s>Parvata</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> bearing the welfare of others. // SvayambhuP_3.13 //
There the Blessed Teacher, speaking sweetly like nectar,
took his seat in the assembly hall to teach the true <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_3.14 //

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭā bhikṣavo sarve śrāvakāḥ brahmacāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing him, all the <s>Bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers), and <s>Brahmacārins</s> (celibate students),
and also <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Caīlakas</s> (naked ascetics), // SvayambhuP_3.15 //
<s>Bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), celibate women, ascetics and <s>Yogins</s>,
those devoted to worshipping the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), <s>Upāsakas</s> (male lay devotees) and <s>Upāsikās</s> (female lay devotees), // SvayambhuP_3.16 //
and thus other beings too, those eager for the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
devoted to the assembly of auspicious glory, eager to behold the <s>Sambuddha</s> — // SvayambhuP_3.17 //
to drink that nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, approaching the lord of sages,

children.text: yathākramaṃ samabhyarcya natvā sāñjalāya mudā // SvayambhuP_3.18 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped in due order, bowing joyfully with joined palms, // SvayambhuP_3.18 //
having circumambulated and honored him, gazing upon him with devotion,
they took their seats in that assembly, settled and composed. // SvayambhuP_3.19 //
Thus <s>Brahmā</s> and others, all the sages, the <s>Brahmacārins</s>,

children.text: tīrthikā api sarve tatsaddharmaṃ śrotumāgatāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.20 //
children.translated_text: and all the sectarian ascetics came to hear the true <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_3.20 //
<s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and other gods, and all the lords of the worlds,

children.text: grahāstārāgaṇāḥ siddhāḥ sādhyā vidyādharā api // SvayambhuP_3.21 //
children.translated_text: the planets, hosts of stars, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, and <s>Vidyādharas</s> too — // SvayambhuP_3.21 //
all of them, having assembled and worshipped the Blessed One in due order,

children.text: samabhyarcya praṇatvā tata sabhāyāṃ samupāśrayat // SvayambhuP_3.22 //
children.translated_text: having bowed, took their seats in the assembly. // SvayambhuP_3.22 //

children.text: evaṃ ca brāhmaṇā vijñā rājāna kṣatriyā api /
children.translated_text: And thus learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, kings, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,
<s>Vaiśyas</s>, counselors, ministers, householders, and great people, // SvayambhuP_3.23 //
artisans, merchants, caravan leaders, and city-dwellers,

children.text: grāmyā jānapadāścāpi tathā nye deśavāsinaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.24 //
children.translated_text: villagers, country-folk, and inhabitants of other lands — // SvayambhuP_3.24 //
all of them, having approached and worshipped the Blessed One in due order,

children.text: samabhyarcya praṇatvā ca kṛtvā pradakṣiṇānyapi // SvayambhuP_3.25 //
children.translated_text: having bowed and also made circumambulations, // SvayambhuP_3.25 //
having honored the teacher, surrounded him on all sides,
and stood composed, ready to drink that nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_3.26 //
Seeing them all seated, the Blessed <s>Viśvabhū</s>, the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: ādi madhyānta kalyāṇaṃ saddharma samupādiśat // SvayambhuP_3.27 //
children.translated_text: taught the true <s>Dharma</s>, good in the beginning, middle, and end. // SvayambhuP_3.27 //
Having drunk that nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, all the beings in the assembly,
having understood the distinction of the <s>Dharma</s>, were enlightened and attained bliss. // SvayambhuP_3.28 //

children.text: tasminkṣaṇe mahī sarvā ca cāraddhi saparvatāḥ /
children.translated_text: At that moment, the entire earth with its mountains shone with splendor;

children.text: suprasannā diśaḥ sarvā rejuravīndra vahnyaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.29 //
children.translated_text: all the directions became perfectly clear, and the fires of the lords of the gods shone. // SvayambhuP_3.29 //
Divine kettledrums resounded, showers of flowers fell,
and a great portent-free celebration commenced everywhere. // SvayambhuP_3.30 //

children.text: tad vilokya sabhālokāḥ sarve te vismayānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing that, all the assembly, filled with wonder,
stood eager, gazing at the Omniscient One to hear the cause. // SvayambhuP_3.31 //
Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Gaganagañja</s> (Treasury of the Sky) arose,
drew aside his upper robe and came forward. // SvayambhuP_3.32 //
Bowing to that Omniscient One of great supernatural knowledge, the <s>Dharmarāja</s>, the Guide,
<s>Viśvabhū</s> the Sage, he spoke thus with joined palms: // SvayambhuP_3.33 //
"O Blessed One, this portent — for whom does it arise now?
May you, O Guru, instruct us on that and enlighten us." // SvayambhuP_3.34 //
Thus entreated by him, that Blessed Lord, the great sage,
looking at <s>Gaganagañja</s> and that assembly, spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_3.35 //
"Son of good family, a greatly auspicious portent has occurred.
I shall declare it; listen, all of you, with devotion. // SvayambhuP_3.36 //
The one of threefold supernatural knowledge, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the son of the <s>Sugata</s>,
dwells in the north, in great <s>Cīna</s> (China), in a mountain hermitage. // SvayambhuP_3.37 //
His two beloved wives are <s>Keśinī</s> and <s>Śrīvarapradā</s>;

children.text: vidyā sadguṇa saṃbhartrī dvitīyāḥ copakeśinī // SvayambhuP_3.38 //
children.translated_text: the bearer of knowledge and good qualities, the second is <s>Upakeśinī</s>. // SvayambhuP_3.38 //
Once, there, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that ocean of good qualities,

children.text: lokaṃ saṃdarśana nāma samādhiṃ vidadhe mudā // SvayambhuP_3.39 //
children.translated_text: joyfully entered the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called 'Beholding the World.' // SvayambhuP_3.39 //
With his meditation-vision, he beheld here, in the lotus of the great lake,
the self-arisen <s>Dharmadhātu</s> <s>Jina</s> shrine, made of jewels. // SvayambhuP_3.40 //
Having beheld that <s>Svayambhū</s>, <s>Mañjudeva</s> of excellent intellect,
delighted, meditating again, reflected thus in his mind: // SvayambhuP_3.41 //
'Ah! A self-arisen <s>Dharmadhātu</s> <s>Jina</s> shrine,

children.text: nirjane jalamaye jyotirūpaḥ saṃbhāṣayan sthitaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.42 //
children.translated_text: standing in the form of light in the uninhabited, water-filled place, shining forth! // SvayambhuP_3.42 //

children.text: tat tathāhaṃ kariṣyāmi gatvā tatra mahāhrade /
children.translated_text: Therefore, I shall do thus: going there to the great lake,
having dried up its waters, so that it may become dry land — // SvayambhuP_3.43 //
then, on that great expanse of earth, well-established and waterless,
I shall establish it upon a rock-hill and worship that Lord. // SvayambhuP_3.44 //
Then, when that land comes into being, villages and other habitations shall arise;

children.text: tadā sarve 'pi lokāśyaḥ bhajeyustaṃ jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_3.45 //
children.translated_text: then all beings shall worship that <s>Jina</s> shrine. // SvayambhuP_3.45 //

children.text: tathā tat puṇya bhāvena sarvadā tatra maṃgalaṃ /
children.translated_text: And by the power of that merit, there shall always be auspiciousness there,

children.text: nirutpātaṃ bhavennūnaṃ lokāśca syūḥ subhāvinaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.46 //
children.translated_text: free from calamity, and the beings shall be of virtuous disposition. // SvayambhuP_3.46 //
Then all those people, having taken refuge in him,

children.text: yathāśakti mahotsāhaiḥ prabhajeyuḥ sadā mudā // SvayambhuP_3.47 //
children.translated_text: shall always worship joyfully with great celebration according to their ability. // SvayambhuP_3.47 //
Then they, purified by that merit, eager for the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
becoming great <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, shall observe the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s> (Bodhisattva vow). // SvayambhuP_3.48 //
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
having attained the threefold method, shall reach the state of <s>Nirvṛti</s> (cessation). // SvayambhuP_3.49 //
Thus, having accumulated great merit, even in the three worlds,
having made it the essence of <s>Dharma</s>, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, I shall reach the state of <s>Nirvṛti</s>.' // SvayambhuP_3.50 //
Having thus meditated and resolved, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that son of the <s>Jina</s>,
assuming the form of the teacher called <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the one of great supernatural power, // SvayambhuP_3.51 //
<s>Keśinī</s> becoming <s>Varadā</s> by name, and <s>Upakeśinī</s> becoming <s>Mokṣadā</s>,
together with many great beings, they all set forth. // SvayambhuP_3.52 //
Then, traveling with his wives, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, together with his assembly,

children.text: sarvatra bhadratāṃ kṛtvā mahotsārhaiḥ samācarat // SvayambhuP_3.53 //
children.translated_text: bestowing blessings everywhere, proceeded with great celebration. // SvayambhuP_3.53 //
Arriving there, they saw from afar, shining brilliantly,
the <s>Jina</s> shrine standing in the midst of the lotus of the great lake. // SvayambhuP_3.54 //

children.text: tatra te taṃ samālokya jyotirūpaṃ samujvalaṃ /
children.translated_text: Beholding it there, in the form of light, resplendent,

children.text: praṇatvā sahasopetyaḥ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇāni ca // SvayambhuP_3.55 //
children.translated_text: they bowed, quickly approached, and made circumambulations. // SvayambhuP_3.55 //

children.text: tattīre parvate ramye sarve 'pi te samāśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: On the shore, upon a beautiful mountain, they all settled,

children.text: taṃ caityameva saṃvīkṣya nyavasanta pramoditāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.56 //
children.translated_text: and gazing upon that <s>Caitya</s> (sacred monument), they dwelt in delight. // SvayambhuP_3.56 //

children.text: tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya mañjudevaḥ sa ṛddhimān /
children.translated_text: Then, rising at dawn, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the one of great power,
with supreme devotion, praised the self-arisen <s>Jina</s> shrine: // SvayambhuP_3.57 //
"Homage to the one in the form of light, in the form of consciousness!
To the one without beginning or end, the bestower of <s>Śrī</s> (auspiciousness), in the form of <s>Praṇava</s> (the syllable Oṃ)! // SvayambhuP_3.58 //
To the one whose form faces all directions, in the form of <s>Svāhā</s> and <s>Svadhā</s>!
To the creator of the elements beginning with earth, in the form of the great festival! // SvayambhuP_3.59 //

children.text: jagatsraṣṭe jagatpātre jagad dhartre namo namaḥ /
children.translated_text: To the creator of the world, the protector of the world, the sustainer of the world — homage, homage!

children.text: jagat vaṃdyāya jagatamārādhāya ca te namaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.60 //
children.translated_text: To the one venerated by the world, the one who is the delight of the world — homage to you! // SvayambhuP_3.60 //
To the exceedingly gross, to the subtle, to transformation, to the transformer,
to you, the formless yet form-assuming, whose essence is <s>Saccidānanda</s> (being-consciousness-bliss)! // SvayambhuP_3.61 //
To the one in the form of the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation), to the fire that receives offerings, homage!

children.text: hotre havana rūpāya homadravyāya te namaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.62 //
children.translated_text: To the sacrificer, to the one in the form of oblation, to the offering substance — homage to you! // SvayambhuP_3.62 //
To the one attainable through devotion, the gentle one, the one tender toward devotees — homage to you!
To the one attainable through meditation, the object of meditation, the bestower of the four aims of life! // SvayambhuP_3.63 //
To the foremost jewel, to the one of limitless glory — homage always!

children.text: guṇātītāya yogāya yogine ca sadā namaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.64 //
children.translated_text: To the one beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), to <s>Yoga</s>, and to the <s>Yogin</s> — homage always! // SvayambhuP_3.64 //

children.text: evaṃ stutvā mañjudevaḥ punaḥ kṣamārthatāṃ vyadhāt /
children.translated_text: Having praised thus, <s>Mañjudeva</s> then made a prayer for forgiveness:

children.text: prasīda bhagavan yadahaṃ hadaṃ saṃśoṣituṃ yate // SvayambhuP_3.65 //
children.translated_text: "Be gracious, O Blessed One, for I endeavor to dry up this lake." // SvayambhuP_3.65 //

children.text: ityuktvā candrahāsaṃ sa sajjīkṛtya samaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having said this, he readied his <s>Candrahāsa</s> (moon-laughing sword) and then,
having circumambulated thrice, he looked about in all directions. // SvayambhuP_3.66 //

children.text: vilokya sa mahāsattvo yāmya diśāvṛtaṃ nagaṃ /
children.translated_text: Looking, that great being saw a mountain blocking the southern direction,

children.text: candrahāsena khaḍgena chitvā jalāśrayaṃ vyadhāt // SvayambhuP_3.67 //
children.translated_text: and with the <s>Candrahāsa</s> sword he cut it open, making a channel for the water. // SvayambhuP_3.67 //
Through that cut mountain passage, all the waters from all around
flowed out swiftly and reached the confluence with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. // SvayambhuP_3.68 //
From that time, rivers and streams came into being on the earth's surface, and lakes too,
filled in all directions with muddy waters and islands. // SvayambhuP_3.69 //

children.text: tatra nirudhya ye 'mvuni yatra ye śilāḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the waters were obstructed and where rocks stood,

children.text: tatra tatra satānsarvāśchitvā svūnica cārayet // SvayambhuP_3.70 //
children.translated_text: there, cutting through all of them, he made the water flow downward. // SvayambhuP_3.70 //

children.text: evaṃ sa sarvataḥ chitvā kṛtvā tajjalanirgamaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having cut through on all sides and created an outlet for that water,

children.text: trirātreṇāpi na jalāni sarvāṇi niracārayet // SvayambhuP_3.71 //
children.translated_text: even in three nights he could not drain out all the waters.
The remaining water of that lake, called <s>Dhanādaha</s>,
he established as the abode of the <s>Nāga</s> <s>Karkoṭaka</s>.
Just as a great elephant, harassed by a lion, bewildered with fear,

children.text: mahārāvai rudanto vai vidravanto diśo daśaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.73 //
children.translated_text: crying out with great roars, fled in the ten directions—
thus the mass of that water, from the cutting of the <s>Candrahāsa</s> sword,
flowed out through other channels, leaving only mud behind.
The remaining water of that lake, called <s>Dharādaha</s>,
he established as the refuge of the <s>Nāga</s> <s>Karkoṭaka</s>.
Then, when that water dried up, the lotus that had been its support
became a mountain, and the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> remained established upon it.
By the power of <s>Mañjudeva</s>, that foremost of all mountains,

children.text: abhedyā vajravaktena vajrakūṭa iti smṛtaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.77 //
children.translated_text: impenetrable by the <s>Vajra</s> weapon, is known as <s>Vajrakūṭa</s>.
At that time, that beautiful land was surrounded by mountains on all sides,
called <s>Upachandoha</s>, and is also referred to as <s>Himālaya</s>.
The invincible <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), in her own form, illuminating knowledge,
having taken the form of a <s>Heruka</s> <s>maṇḍala</s>, remained established.

children.text: tatrāpi ca pradhānā śrī mahādevī khagānanā /
children.translated_text: And there the supreme glorious great goddess, bird-faced (<s>Khagānanā</s>),
called <s>Dharmodayā</s>, abides for the welfare of the world.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa mahācaryā mañjudevo maharddhimāna /
children.translated_text: Seeing her, that great teacher <s>Mañjudeva</s> of great supernatural power,
the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, was exceedingly delighted.

children.text: tataḥ sa tāṃ mahādevī samālokya pramoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, beholding that great goddess with joy,

children.text: urasā śirasā dṛṣṭayā vacasā manasā tathā // SvayambhuP_3.82 //
children.translated_text: with his chest, head, eyes, speech, mind,

children.text: padbhyāṃ karābhyāṃ jānubhyāṃ aṣṭāṃgo 'pi iti smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: feet, hands, and knees—this is known as the eightfold (<s>aṣṭāṅga</s>) prostration.

children.text: aṣṭāṃgai praṇītā kṛtvā sāṃjaliḥ samupāśrayan // SvayambhuP_3.83 //
children.translated_text: Having made the eightfold prostration, with palms joined, he approached her.
With a supremely serene lotus-face, fully awakened, with lotus-like eyes,
gazing upon that great goddess, he worshipped her with hymns of praise thus joyfully:
"O Blessed One, O Great Goddess, I take refuge in you;

children.text: vande pādāmvuje nityaṃ bhajāmi tanprasīdatu // SvayambhuP_3.85 //
children.translated_text: I always bow to your lotus feet, I worship you—may you be pleased.
You are the mother of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the bestower of <s>Bodhi</s> (enlightenment),
the mother of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the protector of their welfare.
Devoted to the welfare of all, the purifier of all sins,
the dispeller of the agitation of wicked hosts of <s>Māra</s>, the bestower of great bliss and happiness,
the giver of strength, valor, and virtuous qualities for the enthusiastic practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
the bestower of the happiness of meditation and <s>samādhi</s>, free from affliction and tranquil,
the giver of the great jewel of wisdom-virtue, prosperity, and glory.

children.text: tad bhaktyāḥ padāmbhoja śaraṇastho bhajāmyaham // SvayambhuP_3.89 //
children.translated_text: With devotion to your lotus feet, having taken refuge, I worship you."

children.text: iti saṃprārthya sa prājño mañjudeva sa samvarī /
children.translated_text: Having thus prayed, that wise <s>Mañjudeva</s>, keeper of vows (<s>saṃvarī</s>),
with a soul pleased by devotion to her, wished to worship her.

children.text: atha tatra sa ācāryaḥ sagaṇaḥ saṃpramoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that teacher, together with his assembly, filled with joy,

children.text: mārga śīrṣaiśitaiḥ pakṣai navamyāṃ ravivāsare // SvayambhuP_3.91 //
children.translated_text: on the ninth day of the bright fortnight of the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, on a Sunday,
having bathed in the morning, pure in soul, clad in clean garments, that wise one,
having taken the <s>poṣadha</s> vow (<s>saṃvara</s>), stood worshipping the goddess.
Having kept vigil at night with recitation of <s>dhāraṇī</s> mantras,
he worshipped and served that queen of the <s>Jinas</s> with hymns of praise.

children.text: tataḥ prātaḥ daśamyāṃ sa snātvā gandhodakairmudā /
children.translated_text: Then, on the morning of the tenth day, having bathed with fragrant water joyfully,
having given charity as desired, purified in the three spheres,
having worshipped that goddess, the supreme sovereign, according to the proper rites,

children.text: mahotsāhaiḥ stutiṃ kṛtvā tridhā pradakṣiṇāni ca // SvayambhuP_3.95 //
children.translated_text: with great enthusiasm making praises and performing circumambulation thrice,
with a supremely serene lotus-face, his mind set on the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
again making the eightfold prostration, he prayed with the <s>añjali mudrā</s> (gesture of reverence) thus:
"Be pleased, O Mother of the world! Having taken refuge in you,

children.text: saṃbodhi sādhanotsau bhajāmi sarvadā mudāṃ // SvayambhuP_3.97 //
children.translated_text: with enthusiasm for the practice of perfect enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), I worship you always with joy."

children.text: iti saṃprārthya saṃprājñau natvāṣṭāṃgairmudā ca tāṃ /
children.translated_text: Having thus prayed and bowed with the eightfold prostration joyfully to her,
he took the nectar from that lotus and drank it thrice with cupped hands.
Having drunk that nectar, purified in the three spheres,
freed from the eight unfavorable states (<s>aṣṭākṣaṇa</s>), he attained the moment of full awakening (<s>saṃbuddhakṣaṇa</s>).

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā sa ācārya devyā bhaktiparāyaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus done, that teacher, devoted to the worship of the goddess,
attaining the moment of full awakening, became the lord of all <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: tataḥ śrīmān sa ācāryo bodhisattva jagaddhite /
children.translated_text: Then that glorious teacher, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the welfare of the world,
dwelt there with his <s>Saṅgha</s> at the hermitages near the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>.
Because of his consecration there, that region, beautiful and glorious,
became renowned everywhere as <s>Mañjuśrīparvata</s> (the Mountain of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>).
Dwelling there always, a devotee of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,
that son of the <s>Jina</s> served for the benefit of all beings.
Seeing that, all the pure ones beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>,
and all the lords of the worlds came there with joy.

children.text: tatraivo poṣaḍhaṃ dhṛtvā kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ niśi /
children.translated_text: There, having taken the <s>poṣadha</s> vow and keeping vigil at night,

children.text: uṣitvā dhāraṇī mantraḥ dhyātvā tāṃ śrī jineśvarīṃ // SvayambhuP_3.105 //
children.translated_text: having recited <s>dhāraṇī</s> mantras and meditated upon that glorious queen of the <s>Jinas</s>,
having worshipped according to the proper rites and performed circumambulations,

children.text: kṛtvāṣṭāṃga praṇāmāni stutibhiścā bhajaṃ mudā // SvayambhuP_3.106 //
children.translated_text: having made eightfold prostrations and worshipped with hymns of praise joyfully—
thus all who took refuge in that great goddess
attained the wealth of the glory and virtues of <s>Dharma</s>, great supernatural power and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment).
Then all those immortals, lords headed by <s>Indra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: vajrakūṭaṃ nagāvjaṃ taṃ samīkṣyante jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_3.108 //
children.translated_text: beholding <s>Vajrakūṭa</s>, the mountain-lotus, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
rejoicing and delighting, having gone to its refuge,
worshipped with great enthusiasm and served with reverence.
Then all the immortals and all the lords of the worlds
of this <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the <s>Vajrācārya</s>, the true <s>Guru</s>,
having approached his refuge, with divine worship-offerings,
worshipped with great enthusiasm and served with delight.
Thus all beginning with <s>Manu</s>, human great sages,
renunciants, yogins, monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>), and <s>brahmacārins</s>,
the cloth-clad ones (<s>cailakas</s>), <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, sons of the <s>Jina</s>—

children.text: te sarve samupāgatya tasyā devyā upāsakāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.113 //
children.translated_text: all of them, having come near, devotees of that goddess,
worshipped according to the proper rites and served with delight.
Then, all of them, having taken refuge in the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> as well,
worshipped with great enthusiasm, bowed, and performed circumambulation.
With supremely serene lotus-faces, they were delighted in mind.
Then those great beings worshipped <s>Mañjudeva</s> of great supernatural power,
the teacher, with enthusiasm and delight.
<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> also, all came there,

children.text: tāṃ devī dharmmadhātuṃ tamācāryaṃ ca samārcayaṃ // SvayambhuP_3.117 //
children.translated_text: and worshipped that goddess, the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, and that teacher.
All the <s>Tathāgatas</s> also, with clouds of offerings,

children.text: tāṃ devīṃ dharmadhātuṃ tamācāryaṃ ca samācaryaṃ // SvayambhuP_3.118 //
children.translated_text: worshipped that goddess, the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, and that teacher.
Thus other people too, having arrived with devotion,

children.text: tāṃ devīṃ dharmadhātuṃ ca tamācāryaṃ ca prābhajan // SvayambhuP_3.119 //
children.translated_text: worshipped that goddess, the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, and that teacher.
By the power of that merit, the earth with its mountains trembled,
and a rain of flowers and auspicious celebration spread in all directions.
Thus was this instruction given by the lord of sages <s>Viśvabhū</s> heard.

children.text: sarve samāśritā lokā vismayaṃ samupāyayuḥ // SvayambhuP_3.121 //
children.translated_text: All the assembled people were filled with wonder.

children.text: tataḥ sarve 'pi te lokāstāṃ devīṃ śrīmaheśvarī /
children.translated_text: Then all those people wished to behold that goddess, the glorious <s>Maheśvarī</s>,
the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, and that teacher.
Knowing that intention, <s>Gaganagañja</s> arose
and looking at the Blessed One, spoke thus:
"O Blessed One, all wish to see that queen of the <s>Sugatas</s>,

children.text: dharmmadhātuṃ tamācāryaṃ tadanujñāṃ dadātu naḥ // SvayambhuP_3.124 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, and that teacher—please grant us permission."
Thus entreated by him, the Blessed One, that lord of sages,
looking at <s>Gaganagañja</s>, the knower of the Self, instructed thus:
"Well done! If you wish to see that great goddess, the bird-faced queen of the <s>Jinas</s>,
the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, and that teacher,

children.text: tatra himālaye gatvā tāṃ śrī devīṃ khagānanāṃ /
children.translated_text: go to the <s>Himālaya</s> there and worship that glorious goddess, the bird-faced one,

children.text: dharmadhātuṃ tamācāryaṃ saṃbhajadhvaṃ yathā vidhi // SvayambhuP_3.127 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, and that teacher according to the proper rites."
Hearing this instruction given by the lord of sages <s>Viśvabhū</s>,

children.text: sarve lokā mahotsāhai ratrāyayuḥ pramoditāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.128 //
children.translated_text: all the people went there with great enthusiasm and delight.
I too, having received the permission of the lord of sages, delighted,
set out with them and, seeing this from afar, came here.
Arriving here and beholding this <s>Dharmadhātu</s> with joy,

children.text: samabhyarcya mahotsāhaistai lokaiḥ prābhajaṃ saha // SvayambhuP_3.130 //
children.translated_text: I worshipped with great enthusiasm together with those people.

children.text: śraddhayā śaraṇaṃ gatvā kṛtvā cainaṃ pradakṣiṇāṃ /
children.translated_text: Going to it as refuge with faith, performing circumambulation,

children.text: stutvāṣṭāṃgaiḥ praṇatvā ca prārthayaṃ bodhisamvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_3.131 //
children.translated_text: praising it, making the eightfold prostration, I prayed for the <s>Bodhi</s> vow (<s>saṃvara</s>).
Then I beheld that teacher called <s>Mañjudeva</s>,
and worshipped him with great enthusiasm together with his disciples.
Then, by his instruction, I worshipped that glorious goddess, the bird-faced one,
according to the proper rites and with great enthusiasm.
Having performed circumambulation and made the eightfold prostration with delight,

children.text: stutvā dhyātvā ca saṃbodhiṃ saṃprārthaya jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_3.134 //
children.translated_text: having praised and meditated upon perfect enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), I prayed for the welfare of the world.
By the power of that merit, purified in the three spheres,

children.text: aṣṭākṣaṇa vinirmukto bodhisattvo bhavaṃ kṛtī // SvayambhuP_3.135 //
children.translated_text: freed from the eight unfavorable states, I became a accomplished <s>Bodhisattva</s>.
Then, having fulfilled the accumulations for perfect enlightenment in proper order,

children.text: jitvā māragaṇān arhan kalāvapi jinobhave // SvayambhuP_3.136 //
children.translated_text: having conquered the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, as an <s>Arhat</s>, I became a <s>Jina</s> (Victor) even in the age of <s>Kali</s>.

children.text: evamasyā mahādevyāḥ ye ye śaraṇa āśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, whoever takes refuge in this great goddess
and worships according to the proper rites with minds set on <s>Bodhi</s>—

children.text: te te sarve mahāsattvāḥ pariśuddha trimaṇḍalāḥ /
children.translated_text: they all, great beings, purified in the three spheres,
become <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great supernatural knowledge, lords of the three virtues.
They never go anywhere to a bad destiny, not ever;
always born in good destinies, they become repositories of glorious virtues.
Having given desired goods to supplicants with reverence,
enjoying happiness as desired, they should practice for the welfare of the world.
Then, those of pure conduct, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes),
having taken the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vow (<s>saṃvara</s>), should always practice what is auspicious.
Then they become great beings, devoted to the happiness of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
engaged in the vow of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), which sustains the welfare of both self and others.
Then they become the foundation of good qualities, energetic, discerning,
devoted to the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>, they become lords of the three qualities.
Then they become wise, steadfast, free from afflictions, with conquered senses,
endowed with the qualities of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration), they become yogis of <s>Bodhi</s>.
Then they become pure of soul, lords of all knowledge and virtues,

children.text: prajñāśrī ratna saṃprāpto bhaveyuḥ sugatātmajāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.145 //
children.translated_text: having attained the jewel of the glory of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), they become sons of the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: tataśca te sahāsattvāḥ sarve sattvā hitotsukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then those great beings, all eager for the welfare of beings,
wise in the methods of removing all misfortunes, become lords of the three qualities.
Then they become oceans of the jewel of aspiration for the accumulations of <s>Bodhi</s>,
having done what benefits all beings, they would always conduct themselves in auspiciousness.
Then they, possessing great supernatural knowledge, endowed with auspicious glory and good qualities,

children.text: valiṣṭhā duṣṭa jetāro bhaveyu stribhaveśvarāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.148 //
children.translated_text: strong, conquerors of the wicked, become lords of the three realms of existence.
Then they, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, practitioners of auspicious conduct,
enriched with the jewel of the knowledge of perfect awakening (<s>Sambodhi</s>), become lords of sages.
Then they become <s>Sugatas</s>, <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Jinas</s> who are lords of the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),
having established all on the path of <s>Bodhi</s>, they make all righteous.
Thus, having made everything pervaded by <s>Dharma</s> in all worlds,
having attained the excellent state of <s>Nirvṛti</s> (cessation), they proceed to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.
Thus, the supreme and excellent worship of this great goddess,
the greater merit accomplished, is the means to the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.

children.text: iti satyaṃ samākhyātaṃ sarvai rapi munīśvaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus this truth has been proclaimed by all the lords of sages;

children.text: vijñāyāsyā mahādevyā bhajadhvaṃ śaraṇe sthitā // SvayambhuP_3.153 //
children.translated_text: knowing this, worship the great goddess, standing in her refuge.
Also from worship at this <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the supreme and excellent
greater merit accomplished is the means to the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.
Also from worship of this <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the supreme and excellent
greater merit accomplished is the means to the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.

children.text: matveti yadi vo vāṃcchā vidyate saugate pade /
children.translated_text: Understanding thus, if you have the desire for the state of a <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: sarve yūyaṃ samādhāya bhajatāntra jinālaye // SvayambhuP_3.156 //
children.translated_text: all of you, having composed yourselves, worship here at the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.
Having taken refuge in this bird-faced great goddess,

children.text: dhyātvā smṛtvā samuccārya nāmāpi bhajatābhavaṃ // SvayambhuP_3.157 //
children.translated_text: meditating, remembering, and uttering even the name, worship until the end of existence.

children.text: ya eṣāṃ śaraṇe sthitvā dhyātvā smṛtvā samāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, standing in their refuge, meditating, remembering, with concentration,
even uttering the name, worship always throughout existence—

children.text: te sabhadrā nagacchanti durggatiṃ ca kadācana /
children.translated_text: they, the auspicious ones, never go to a bad destiny, not ever.

children.text: sadā sadgati saṃjātā bhaveyuḥ śrī guṇāśrayāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.159 //
children.translated_text: Always born in good destinies, they become the abode of glory and virtues.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, practitioners of the true <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Bodhi</s>,
devoted to the welfare of all beings, they become sons of the <s>Sugata</s>.
Thus, their great happiness, endowed with auspicious glory and good qualities,
always free from calamity, proceeds with concentration.
Fear from divine calamities does not exist for them anywhere;
for seeing them thus devoted, all the gods led by <s>Indra</s> joyfully protect them.
Fear from fire calamities never exists for them,

children.text: yat tāndṛṣṭvā prasīdanto rakṣeyurvahnayaḥ sadā // SvayambhuP_3.163 //
children.translated_text: for seeing them, the fires, being pleased, would always protect them.
Fear of untimely death does not exist for them anywhere,

children.text: yadyamopi samalokya rakṣati tāṃ prasāditaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.164 //
children.translated_text: for even <s>Yama</s>, looking upon them, protects them, being pleased.
Fear from <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons) does not exist for them anywhere,

children.text: yad vāyavo 'pi tā vījya rakṣeyuḥ sarvadānugāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.165 //
children.translated_text: for even the winds, fanning them, would always protect them as followers.

children.text: yakṣasyāpi bhayaṃ teṣāṃ vidyate na sadā kvacit /
children.translated_text: Fear from <s>Yakṣas</s> does not exist for them ever, anywhere,

children.text: yakṣā samīkṣya rakṣeyuḥ sarve yakṣādhipā api // SvayambhuP_3.166 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Yakṣas</s>, observing them, would protect them—all the lords of <s>Yakṣas</s> too.
Fear from <s>Bhūtas</s> (spirits) does not exist for them anywhere,
for even <s>Īśāna</s>, seeing them, would protect them, being delighted.
Fear from <s>Gandharva</s> disturbances does not exist for them anywhere,
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> too, seeing them, would protect them, being pleased.
Fear from <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s> likewise never exists for them;
<s>Virūḍhaka</s>, seeing them with favor, protects them out of grace.

children.text: nāgebhyo 'pi bhayanteṣāṃ vidyate na sadā kvacita /
children.translated_text: Fear from <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent beings) does not exist for them ever, anywhere;
<s>Virūpākṣa</s>, looking upon them rightly, protects them, being pleased.

children.text: yakṣebhyo 'pi sadā teṣāṃ vidyate na bhayaṃ kvacita /
children.translated_text: Fear from <s>Yakṣas</s> does not exist for them always, ever, anywhere;

children.text: kuvero hi samālokya saṃrakṣastān prasāditaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.171 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kuvera</s>, looking upon them, protects them, being pleased.
Fear from <s>Kinnaras</s> does not exist for them at any time;

children.text: drumo hitān mahāsattvā saṃvīkṣavat prasāditaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.172 //
children.translated_text: <s>Druma</s>, the great being, looking upon them with favor, is pleased.
Fear from <s>Guhyakas</s> (secret beings) does not exist for these righteous ones;
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, seeing them with favor, would always be pleased.
Likewise, fear from <s>Vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-holders) does not exist for them,
for <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> too, looking upon them rightly, would always be so.
Fear from planetary disturbances does not exist for them ever;
all the lords of the planets, observing them, would always be so.
Likewise, fear from stellar disturbances does not exist for them;

children.text: sarvāstā rāhi tānvīkṣya sarvatrā veyurābhavaṃ // SvayambhuP_3.176 //
children.translated_text: all the stars, looking upon them, would protect them throughout existence.
<s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, and <s>Rudras</s>, looking upon them, would always protect them;

children.text: tattebhyopi bhayaṃ kvāpi teṣāṃ nāsti kadācana // SvayambhuP_3.177 //
children.translated_text: thus, fear from them also does not exist for them anywhere, ever.

children.text: tathā ca mātṛkotpātaṃ bhayaṃ nāsti kadācana /
children.translated_text: Likewise, fear from <s>Mātṛkā</s> (mother goddess) disturbances never exists;

children.text: sarvāhi mātṛkān dṛṣṭvā rakṣeyu stāṃ prasāditāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.178 //
children.translated_text: all the <s>Mātṛkās</s>, seeing them, would protect them, being pleased.
<s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, and the <s>Bhairavas</s> too,
always looking upon them, would protect them, being pleased.
<s>Pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), <s>Vetālas</s> (vampiric beings), and hosts of <s>Ḍākinīs</s>,
even they, always seeing them, would protect them, being pleased.
Fear from them also does not exist for these ones, ever;

children.text: sarve 'pi rtesahāyāḥ syu saṃvodhi dharmmasādhane // SvayambhuP_3.181 //
children.translated_text: all of them become their helpers in the practice of <s>Dharma</s> for awakening.
From lions and all animals, from birds too, on all sides,

children.text: sarpādi kṛmikīṭebhyo bhayanteṣāṃ sadāpi na // SvayambhuP_3.182 //
children.translated_text: from serpents, worms, and insects—fear does not exist for them, ever.
Even from wicked adversaries and from thieves on all sides,

children.text: śatrubhyo 'pi bhayanteṣāṃ vidyate na samantataḥ // SvayambhuP_3.183 //
children.translated_text: from enemies too—fear does not exist for them anywhere.
For they, anointed with merit, seeing them, are pleased;

children.text: sarve maitrī kṛpā sneha nivaddhāḥ syuhitārthinaḥ // SvayambhuP_3.184 //
children.translated_text: all become bound by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), compassion, and affection, seeking their welfare.
Thus all beings too, seeing them, are pleased,
with affectionate minds and serene faces, they would look upon them with loving-kindness.
Kings too, seeing them, imbued with loving-kindness and affection,

children.text: suprasannāśayāḥ prītā mānayeyuḥ sadā mudā // SvayambhuP_3.186 //
children.translated_text: with supremely clear dispositions, pleased, would always honor them joyfully.
Ministers too would always speak to them with loving-kindness and affection,
honoring as they wish their practice of the true <s>Dharma</s> and vows.

children.text: brāmhaṇā api sarve ca teṣāṃ saddharmma sādhanaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> too, all of them, seeing their practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
with rejoicing minds, would always give auspicious blessings.

children.text: ṛṣayo 'pi tathā sarve tāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃprasāditāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣis</s> (seers) too, all of them, seeing them, being pleased,

children.text: paśyantaḥ kṛpayā dṛṣṭvā modayeyuḥ subhāśiṣā // SvayambhuP_3.189 //
children.translated_text: looking upon them with compassion, would delight them with auspicious blessings.

children.text: evaṃ ca yoginaḥ siddhā yatayo bramhacāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus also <s>yogins</s>, <s>siddhas</s> (perfected ones), ascetics, <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibate students),
<s>tīrthikas</s> (religious wanderers), <s>tāpasas</s> (ascetics), and also those observing vows and lay devotees,
wanderers, <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), and also female lay devotees—

children.text: api tāṃ sudṛśālokya nandayeyuḥ śubhāśiṣāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.191 //
children.translated_text: even they, seeing them clearly, would make them happy with auspicious blessings.

children.text: evaṃ ca śrāvakāḥ sarve pratyeka sugatā api /
children.translated_text: Thus also all <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples), <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) too,

children.text: bodhisatvāśca sarve 'pi tān dṛṣṭvā saṃprasāditāḥ // SvayambhuP_3.192 //
children.translated_text: and all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, seeing them, are pleased.
Looking upon them with compassion, with loving-kindness, affection, and goodwill,

children.text: rakṣitvā bodhimārgeṣu niyājeyuḥ sadā bhavaṃ // SvayambhuP_3.193 //
children.translated_text: having protected them, they would always guide them on the paths of <s>Bodhi</s> throughout existence.

children.text: evaṃ sarve 'pi saṃbuddhā dṛṣṭvā tāṃ saṃprasāditāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus all the fully awakened <s>Sambuddhas</s> too, seeing them, are pleased;
always with compassion they would protect and guide them for the welfare of the world.
Thus, the great merit of those ones, the means to the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>,
bestowing prosperity, accomplishment, and the wealth of auspicious glory and good qualities—
thus, you too, having understood, always taking refuge,
having worshipped according to your ability, serve these Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>).

children.text: smṛtvā dhyātvāpi nāmāpi samuccārya sadā mudā /
children.translated_text: Remembering, meditating, and even uttering the names always with joy,

children.text: eṣāmeva triratnānāṃ bhajadhvaṃ śaraṇe sthitā // SvayambhuP_3.197 //
children.translated_text: worship these very Three Jewels, standing in their refuge.
Those anointed with this merit, purified in the three spheres,
endowed with auspicious glory and good qualities, they become those of auspicious disposition.

children.text: durgatiṃ te na gaccheyuḥ sadā sadgatisaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: They never go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies;
they become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, practitioners of auspicious conduct.
Then they, striving for the welfare of all beings,
steadfast and wise, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
then, having conquered the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, free from afflictions, with conquered senses,

children.text: arhanta trividhāṃ bodhiṃprāpya yāyu jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_3.201 //
children.translated_text: attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s> of an <s>Arhat</s>, they go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.
All this has been proclaimed by me and by all the lords of sages;
having heard and rejoiced, always conduct yourselves in auspiciousness.
Having heard this instruction given by the lord of sages, those assembled in the court,
all, rejoicing likewise, having attained delight, were awakened.

body.text: iti śrī svayambhūtpattisamuddeśa mahāhrada śoṣaṇa dharmmadhātu padmagirisaṃprasthāpano nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, named 'The Drying of the Great Lake, the Establishment of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> <s>Padmagiri</s>,' in the glorious <s>Svayambhū</s> Origin.
Fourth Chapter: named 'The Story of the Origin of the Glorious <s>Svayambhū Caitya</s>, the Establishment of the <s>Vītarāga Tīrtha</s> Kingdom.'

children.translated_text: Then that great being <s>Maitreya</s>, son of the <s>Sugata</s>,
having bowed to that Lord, spoke thus with palms joined in <s>añjali mudrā</s>:
"When, O Lord, were villages, rows of cities, and the like
established here as great kingdoms? Please instruct on this."

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tena maitreyena niśasya sa /
children.translated_text: Having heard this request made by <s>Maitreya</s>,
the Lord, looking upon that one of great supernatural knowledge, instructed thus:

children.text: sādhu śṛṇu mahāsattva maitreya tvaṃ samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Well done! Listen, O great being <s>Maitreya</s>, with concentration.
I shall tell of that time when habitation came to be here.
When the lifespan of humans was forty thousand years,
<s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Dharma), lord of the world, <s>Krakucchanda</s>, lord of sages,
lord of all knowledge, the Teacher, the guide of the three realms,
the Omniscient One, of great supernatural knowledge, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Jina</s>—he arose.
That fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>, together with his assembly, for the welfare of the world—
In the delightful monastery near the great city of <s>Kṣemāvatī</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.7 //
in the Buddhist dwelling, he taught the true <s>dharma</s>,
excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, he resided, illuminating. // SvayambhuP_4.8 //
At that time I was a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a wise one named <s>Jyotipāla</s>,
having worshipped the teacher <s>Krakucchanda</s>, I always served him. // SvayambhuP_4.9 //
Then that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the teacher <s>Krakucchanda</s>, for the welfare of the world,
wished to teach the true <s>dharma</s> in the regions. // SvayambhuP_4.10 //

children.text: tataḥ sa bhagavān śāstā sarvasaṃghaiḥ samanvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the teacher, accompanied by all the <s>saṃgha</s>,
having brought auspiciousness everywhere, conversing, went forth. // SvayambhuP_4.11 //
Thus that teacher, wandering, taught the <s>dharma</s> everywhere,
and gradually coming here, he beheld all around. // SvayambhuP_4.12 //
Having seen this <s>dharmadhātu</s> (essence of reality), the blazing abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
he, together with the <s>saṃgha</s>, having approached, worshipped it with proper rites, joyfully. // SvayambhuP_4.13 //
Then he proceeded right here to the rocky mountain called <s>Śaṅkha</s>,

children.text: mahachuddhaśilāyāṃ ca vijahāra sa sāṃdhikaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.14 //
children.translated_text: and on a great, pure rock, he resided with his followers. // SvayambhuP_4.14 //
There, seeing that lord of the world, <s>Krakucchanda</s>, the lord of sages,
seated on the throne in the midst of the assembly, attended by the community of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), // SvayambhuP_4.15 //
the great beings, sons of the <s>Jina</s>,
came together, delighted, to drink that nectar of the true <s>dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.16 //
<s>Bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) such as <s>Suśīlā</s> and others, ascetics and lay devotees,

children.text: cailakā vratinaścāpi sarve upāsikā api // SvayambhuP_4.17 //
children.translated_text: female ascetics, those observing vows, and all female lay devotees as well, // SvayambhuP_4.17 //
<s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, longing for the qualities of the true <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: tatsaddharmmāmṛtaṃ pātuṃ sarve te samupāgatāḥ // SvayambhuP_4.18 //
children.translated_text: all of them came together to drink that nectar of the true <s>dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.18 //
Having worshipped that <s>Bhagavān</s> and performed circumambulations,
bowing with joined palms, gazing at him, they took their seats. // SvayambhuP_4.19 //
Likewise, <s>Brahmā</s> and others, great sages and ascetics,
renunciants, yogins, sages, and celibate practitioners, // SvayambhuP_4.20 //

children.text: evaṃ śakrādayo davāḥ sarve lokādhipā api /
children.translated_text: thus <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and other <s>devas</s> (gods), all the lords of the worlds as well,
planets, hosts of stars, <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings), <s>sādhyas</s>, and <s>vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-bearers) as well, // SvayambhuP_4.21 //

children.text: gandharvā kinnarā yakṣā guhyakā rākṣasā api /
children.translated_text: <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>kinnaras</s> (mythical beings), <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>guhyakas</s> (secret beings), and <s>rākṣasas</s> (night-wanderers) as well,
<s>dānavas</s> (demons), <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), and others came here. // SvayambhuP_4.22 //
Having worshipped that <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>saṃgha</s>, delighted,
bowing, they stood concentrated, ready to drink the nectar of <s>dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.23 //

children.text: evaṃ ca brāhmaṇā vijñā rājānaḥ kṣatriyā api /
children.translated_text: Thus also wise <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, kings, <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors),

children.text: vaiśyāśca mantriṇo 'mātyāḥ sainyā bhṛtyā janānyapi // SvayambhuP_4.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>vaiśyas</s> (merchants), ministers, counselors, soldiers, servants, and other people, // SvayambhuP_4.24 //
wealthy householders, the eminent, virtuous ones, and great people,
artisans, traders, caravan leaders, and townsfolk, // SvayambhuP_4.25 //
subjects, villagers, forest-dwellers, wandering ascetics, and mountain-dwellers,
thus other people too came from all directions. // SvayambhuP_4.26 //
Having seen that <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowing, they approached,
having worshipped in due order and performed circumambulations, // SvayambhuP_4.27 //
having performed the eightfold prostration, with cupped palms, in joy,
to drink that nectar of the true <s>dharma</s>, in that assembly on all sides, // SvayambhuP_4.28 //
surrounding and attending him, they took their seats with concentration,
revering the lord of sages as their <s>guru</s>, gazing up at him, they sat down. // SvayambhuP_4.29 //
Then that <s>Bhagavān</s>, seeing all those present,
contemplating the <s>Āryasatya</s> (Noble Truths), taught the true <s>dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.30 //
Having drunk that nectar of the true <s>dharma</s>, all of them were awakened,

children.text: bodhicaryā vrataṃ dhartuṃ samecchanta prasāditāḥ // SvayambhuP_4.31 //
children.translated_text: and wished to undertake the vow of <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct toward enlightenment), with minds made serene. // SvayambhuP_4.31 //
Having perceived their intentions, that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the lord of sages,
looking at <s>Maitreya</s>, the essence of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, instructed thus: // SvayambhuP_4.32 //
"Sons of good family, those who with joy and faith, in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>,
wish to go forth — let them go forth with reverence. // SvayambhuP_4.32 //
Those here who desire — I grant it — for the accomplishment of all <s>dharma</s> and its purpose:

children.text: pravrajyā śāsane bauddhe caranti bodhisaṃvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_4.34 //
children.translated_text: having gone forth in the Buddhist teaching, they shall practice the <s>bodhisaṃvara</s> (vow of enlightenment). // SvayambhuP_4.34 //

children.text: te sarve pātakā muktāḥ pariśuddha trimaṇḍalāḥ /
children.translated_text: All of them, freed from sins, with the three spheres completely purified,
free from defilements, of spotless souls, <s>bodhisattvas</s> with senses conquered, // SvayambhuP_4.35 //
having conquered the wicked hosts of <s>Māra</s>, destroyers of evil, celibate practitioners,
having attained the threefold <s>bodhi</s>, they shall reach the state of a <s>Saṃbuddha</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.36 //

children.text: iti matvātra saṃsāre ye vāṃchanti sunirvṛtiṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having understood, those in this <s>saṃsāra</s> who desire supreme <s>nirvṛti</s> (liberation),

children.text: tatra pravrajyā sānbauddhaṃ carantu śraddhayā vrataṃ // SvayambhuP_4.37 //
children.translated_text: let them go forth there and practice the Buddhist vow with faith." // SvayambhuP_4.37 //
Having heard this instruction of the lord of sages, those who were awakened,
the great beings seated in the assembly wished to go forth. // SvayambhuP_4.38 //
Then four hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s> headed by <s>Guṇadhvaja</s> and others,
and likewise three hundred <s>kṣatriyas</s> named <s>Bhayadada</s> and others, // SvayambhuP_4.39 //
and many other great beings, <s>vaiśyas</s>, <s>śūdras</s>, and virtuous people,
all of them, with serene minds, wished to go forth. // SvayambhuP_4.40 //
Then all of them, rising up, with joined palms, came forward,
bowing to that <s>Bhagavān</s>, they requested thus with reverence: // SvayambhuP_4.41 //
"O <s>Bhagavān</s>, lord, omniscient one, having received your command, we
wish to go forth in the Buddhist teaching and practice the vow. // SvayambhuP_4.42 //

children.text: bhagavansta bhavānasmān sarvān paśyan kṛpā dṛśā /
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavān</s>, may you, looking upon us all with compassionate eyes,
having taken us in, deign to establish us in the true <s>dharma</s>." // SvayambhuP_4.43 //
Thus requested by all of them, that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the lord of sages,
looking at all of them with righteous minds, addressed them and instructed thus: // SvayambhuP_4.44 //
"If here in the <s>Sugata</s>'s <s>dharma</s> you wish to go forth,

children.text: etat pravrajya sarvatra caradhvaṃ saugataṃ vrataṃ // SvayambhuP_4.45 //
children.translated_text: having gone forth, practice everywhere the vow of the <s>Sugata</s>." // SvayambhuP_4.45 //
Having thus instructed, that <s>Saṃbuddha</s>, touching their heads with his hand,
took all of them into the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Sugata</s> with respect. // SvayambhuP_4.46 //

children.text: tato 'vatārya te keśān rakta cīvara prāvṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having shaved their hair, clothed in saffron robes,

children.text: khikhirī pātramādhāya sarve 'pi bhikṣuvo bhavan // SvayambhuP_4.47 //
children.translated_text: carrying alms bowls, they all became <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). // SvayambhuP_4.47 //

children.text: tataḥ sa bhagavāntebhyoḥ yatibhyo saṃmyak saṃbodhipākṣikān /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Bhagavān</s>, to those ascetics, taught the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s>,
and having taught the true <s>dharma</s>, he bestowed the <s>bodhisaṃvara</s> (vow of enlightenment). // SvayambhuP_4.48 //
Then those, of spotless souls, free from defilements, with pure senses,

children.text: satkāraṃ lābha niḥkāṃkṣā vītasaṃgā niraṃjanāḥ // SvayambhuP_4.49 //
children.translated_text: without desire for honor and gain, free from attachment, without blemish, // SvayambhuP_4.49 //
practicing conduct beneficial to self and others, without longing for the ways of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
unattached to the ways of <s>Māra</s>, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, // SvayambhuP_4.50 //
free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), of spotless souls, with the three spheres completely purified,

children.text: arhanta bhadrakā cārā babhubu brahmacāriṇaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.51 //
children.translated_text: they became <s>arhats</s>, of auspicious conduct, celibate practitioners. // SvayambhuP_4.51 //
Then all those Buddhist ascetics, practitioners of the path to <s>bodhi</s>,
having worked for the welfare of all beings, always wandered in the auspicious. // SvayambhuP_4.52 //
Then, those of completely purified souls, possessing the five <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), of great powers,

children.text: vandyāḥ pūjyāḥ sadevānāṃ lokānāṃ guravo bhavan // SvayambhuP_4.53 //
children.translated_text: became venerable, worshipful, teachers of the worlds including the <s>devas</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.53 //

children.text: tasmiṃśca samaye tatra gireḥ śaṃkhasya mūrddhani /
children.translated_text: At that time, there on the summit of <s>Śaṅkha</s> mountain,
from the thumb of <s>Vajrasattva</s>'s hand, pure water flowed forth. // SvayambhuP_4.54 //
That became a marvelous, wondrous, holy pilgrimage place — a great river,
which bestowed the fruits of the four aims of life upon all beings. // SvayambhuP_4.55 //
Moreover, it became even more sanctified by the words

children.text: saddharmma deśanā vākyāvabhūvā ti pavitratā // SvayambhuP_4.56 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Krakucchanda</s>'s <s>dharma</s> teaching — it became supremely pure. // SvayambhuP_4.56 //
Therefore it became renowned as the foremost of all <s>tīrthas</s> (holy waters), called <s>Vāgmatī</s>,

children.text: bhadraśrī guṇa saṃbhartrī sarvapāpa viśodhanī // SvayambhuP_4.57 //
children.translated_text: a bearer of auspicious glory and good qualities, a purifier of all sins. // SvayambhuP_4.57 //

children.text: ye tatra vidhinā snātvā pitṛ devāditarpaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Those who bathe there according to proper rites, perform <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libations) to ancestors and gods,

children.text: kṛtvā dānādikaṃ datvā vrataṃ cāpi prakurvate // SvayambhuP_4.58 //
children.translated_text: give gifts and charity, and also undertake vows — // SvayambhuP_4.58 //
they, of spotless souls through the <s>saṃgha</s>, endowed with auspicious glory and good qualities,

children.text: yathākāmaṃ sukhaṃ bhutvā saṃprayānti jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_4.59 //
children.translated_text: having enjoyed happiness as they desire, proceed to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.59 //

children.text: iti matvā sadā tatra snātvā pitrāditarppaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having understood, one should always bathe there, perform libations to ancestors,

children.text: dānādi saṃvaraṃ kṛtvā sacarantāṃ jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_4.60 //
children.translated_text: perform charity and restraint, and wander for the welfare of the world. // SvayambhuP_4.60 //
By the mere sight of it, by drinking its water even a little,
and even by touching it, all sins are destroyed. // SvayambhuP_4.61 //

children.text: prakṣālyāpi ca tatrāsyaṃ gaṃgā snāna phalaṃ labheta /
children.translated_text: Even by washing one's face there, one obtains the fruit of bathing in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: śilasiṃ ca mātreṇa śuddhānte indriyāni ṣaṭ // SvayambhuP_4.62 //
children.translated_text: and by mere contact with the rock, the six senses are purified. // SvayambhuP_4.62 //
Thus, the exceedingly great merit arising from devotion to <s>Vāgmatī</s>,

children.text: sarve tīrthottamākhyātaṃ te nāsau vāgmatī jinaiḥ // SvayambhuP_4.63 //
children.translated_text: proclaimed as the foremost of all <s>tīrthas</s> — she is called <s>Vāgmatī</s> by the <s>Jinas</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.63 //

children.text: iti matvātra saṃsāre icchanti ye sadāśubhaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having understood, those who desire perpetual auspiciousness in this <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: vāgmatī śrī sukhādhārāṃ bhajantu sarvadāpi te // SvayambhuP_4.64 //
children.translated_text: let them always worship <s>Vāgmatī</s>, the glorious support of happiness. // SvayambhuP_4.64 //
Moreover, another river arose, born from that very hand;

children.text: sāpi pavitritā bhūtā krakuchandasya vākyataḥ // SvayambhuP_4.65 //
children.translated_text: she too became sanctified by the words of <s>Krakucchanda</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.65 //
There, the beards, hair, and nails of those who went forth

children.text: kṛtvā bhāgadvayaṃ tatra bhāgamekaṃ pracikṣipuḥ // SvayambhuP_4.66 //
children.translated_text: were divided into two portions; one portion they cast in there. // SvayambhuP_4.66 //
Then that great river became renowned as <s>Keśāvatī</s> (the hair-bearing one),

children.text: eka bhāgantu tatraiva saṃsthāpitaṃ śilātale // SvayambhuP_4.67 //
children.translated_text: and one portion was placed right there on a stone slab. // SvayambhuP_4.67 //
As many beards and hairs as there were, that many <s>caityas</s>

children.text: prādurbhūtāni caityāni tāṃnyadyāpi vasaṃti hi // SvayambhuP_4.68 //
children.translated_text: manifested on the stone slab — they remain even to this day. // SvayambhuP_4.68 //

children.text: sāpi nadī mahātīrtha vāgmatī va prasīddhatā /
children.translated_text: That river too became a great holy <s>tīrtha</s>, renowned like <s>Vāgmatī</s>,
through the great power of merit of those who went forth. // SvayambhuP_4.69 //
The fame and glory of the great merit of those who went forth,

children.text: tadāpuṇya mahākīrti śabda sarvatra prāsarat // SvayambhuP_4.70 //
children.translated_text: those <s>bhikṣus</s>, celibate practitioners, spread everywhere at that time. // SvayambhuP_4.70 //
Thereafter, eight dispassionate, unsupported ones,
luminous in form, formless, manifested for the welfare of the world. // SvayambhuP_4.71 //
One on the side of <s>Śaṅkha</s> mountain, near the hermitage of <s>Maṇicūḍā</s>,

children.text: maṇiliṃga iti khyātaḥ so 'dyāpi saṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.72 //
children.translated_text: known as <s>Maṇiliṅga</s> — he remains established even today. // SvayambhuP_4.72 //
The second at the site of <s>Gokarṇa</s> on earth, in the form of a luminous sage,
the third on <s>Cārugiri</s>, and the fourth at <s>Kumbhatīrtha</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.73 //
The fifth on <s>Phaṇiśaila</s> (Serpent Mountain), the sixth at the site of <s>Gartaka</s>,

children.text: saptamo gandhavatyāṃ ca aṣṭamo vikramasthale // SvayambhuP_4.74 //
children.translated_text: the seventh at <s>Gandhavatī</s>, and the eighth at the site of <s>Vikrama</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.74 //
These eight great <s>devas</s>, dispassionate, without blemish,
luminous in form, formless, manifested for the welfare of the world. // SvayambhuP_4.75 //
Here, through the power of these dispassionate ones, on all sides,
the land became delightful — the foremost of all <s>pīṭhas</s> (sacred seats) on earth. // SvayambhuP_4.76 //
At that time, there was a great lord, born of the lineage of <s>Mahāsammata</s>,
of compassionate, merciful, and auspicious soul — a <s>bodhisattva</s> king. // SvayambhuP_4.77 //

children.text: tatra sa nṛpa rājendraḥ krakuchandena tāyinā /
children.translated_text: There that king, lord of kings, by the protector <s>Krakucchanda</s>
came here together to behold <s>Svayambhū</s> and <s>Khagānanā</s> (the Bird-faced Goddess). // SvayambhuP_4.78 //
Seeing from afar <s>Svayambhū</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
having bowed and approached, he performed three circumambulations. // SvayambhuP_4.79 //

body.translated_text: Then, with great celebrations, he worshipped that one who embodies the five <s>Jinas</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.80 //

children.translated_text: Having prostrated with the eight limbs and having taken refuge, he worshipped;

children.text: tatastathā ca rājendro mañjudevaṃ ca saṅguruṃ // SvayambhuP_4.81 //
children.translated_text: then likewise, the great king worshipped <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the true <s>Guru</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.81 //
according to the proper rites, and worshipped with great joy.

children.text: tatastathā sa rājendraḥ khagānanāṃ jineśvarīṃ // SvayambhuP_4.82 //
children.translated_text: Then likewise, that great king worshipped <s>Khagānanā</s>, the queen of <s>Jinas</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.82 //
according to the proper rites, and with great celebrations worshipped her joyfully.
Then, seeing all eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> (passionless ones) of <s>Svayambhū</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.83 //
the king, being delighted, likewise worshipped them with great celebrations.
By the power of this merit, he, of great meritorious disposition, accomplished, // SvayambhuP_4.84 //
became the foremost king of all <s>Dharma</s>, the lord of all worlds.

children.text: sarva vidyādhipo rājā bhadraśrī sadguṇāśrayaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.85 //
children.translated_text: The king, lord of all knowledge, <s>Bhadraśrī</s>, abode of good qualities, // SvayambhuP_4.85 //
became famous and renowned by the name <s>Dharmākara</s> (Mine of Dharma).

children.text: tataḥ so 'tra mahārājaḥ saṃsthāstuṃ kāma ātmanā // SvayambhuP_4.86 //
children.translated_text: Then, that great king, desiring to dwell here himself, // SvayambhuP_4.86 //
bowed to <s>Krakucchanda</s>, the foremost lord of sages, and petitioned thus:
"Lord, I have a desire; may you know my wish. // SvayambhuP_4.87 //
Granting that permission, you are worthy of bestowing your grace."

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tena bhagavānsa munīśvaraḥ // SvayambhuP_4.88 //
children.translated_text: When thus entreated by him, the Lord, that supreme sage, // SvayambhuP_4.88 //
looking at that king <s>Dharmākara</s>, instructed thus:

children.text: sādhu rājan mahāsattva yadevaṃ tvaṃ samīcchasi // SvayambhuP_4.89 //
children.translated_text: "Well done, O king, great being, that you desire thus! // SvayambhuP_4.89 //

children.text: tathātvamiha san sthitvā pālayaṃ bodhayan prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Accordingly, dwell here and protect and awaken the people.
And here, having established all the people and awakening them, // SvayambhuP_4.90 //
establishing them on the path of enlightenment, always guide them in auspiciousness.

children.text: dharmmeṇa pālayan sarvāllokān svayaṃ samācaran // SvayambhuP_4.91 //
children.translated_text: Protecting all people through <s>Dharma</s>, practicing it yourself, // SvayambhuP_4.91 //
live happily as you wish for the welfare of the world.

children.text: dharmmanītyā samādhāya kṛtvā lokahitaṃ sadā // SvayambhuP_4.92 //
children.translated_text: Having established the policy of <s>Dharma</s>, always working for the welfare of the world, // SvayambhuP_4.92 //
accomplishing the accumulation for enlightenment, dwell here in this body.

children.text: sadāsya śaraṇe sthitvā dharmmadhātoḥ svayambhuvaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.93 //
children.translated_text: Always standing in the refuge of this <s>Dharmadhātu Svayambhū</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.93 //
having worshipped with faith, act for the welfare of the world.

children.text: asyāḥ khagānanāyāśca devyāḥ śaraṇa āśritaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.94 //
children.translated_text: Having taken refuge in this <s>Khagānanā</s>, the goddess, // SvayambhuP_4.94 //
always worshipping, practice the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s> (vow of enlightenment).
And having attended upon this <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the true <s>Guru</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.95 //
holding the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>, practice the true <s>Dharma</s>.
And of these eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> (passionless ones), always // SvayambhuP_4.96 //
having worshipped with faith, accomplish the supreme <s>Dharma</s>.
And by resorting to the <s>Tīrthas</s> (sacred fords) headed by <s>Vāgmatī</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.97 //
performing bathing, charity, and the like, pleasing the ancestors and gods,

children.text: labdhā trikāya saṃśuddhiṃ dhṛtvā saṃbodhimānasaṃ // SvayambhuP_4.98 //
children.translated_text: having attained purification of the three bodies, holding a mind set on <s>Saṃbodhi</s> (perfect enlightenment), // SvayambhuP_4.98 //
having worked for the welfare of all beings, dwell happily.

children.text: evaṃ rājendra lokāṃśca sarvānapi pravodhayaṃ // SvayambhuP_4.99 //
children.translated_text: Thus, O king, awakening all the people also, // SvayambhuP_4.99 //
always establishing all these in refuge,

children.text: pūjā bhakti mahotsāhaiḥ cārayitvā samādarāt // SvayambhuP_4.100 //
children.translated_text: having guided them with reverence through worship, devotion, and great celebrations, // SvayambhuP_4.100 //
establishing them on the path of enlightenment, always guide them in auspiciousness.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā mahārāja saṃbodhi nihitāśrayaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.101 //
children.translated_text: Having done thus, O great king, with your mind set on <s>Saṃbodhi</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.101 //
holding the vow of <s>Bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of enlightenment), act for the welfare of the world.
Anointed with this merit, you shall become a son of the <s>Jina</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.102 //
a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of great supernatural knowledge, <s>Bhadraśrī</s>, abode of good qualities.

children.text: kadācidapi naivatvaṃ durgatau ca kvacitsareḥ // SvayambhuP_4.103 //
children.translated_text: Never shall you go to evil destinies anywhere; // SvayambhuP_4.103 //
always born in good destinies, endowed with prosperity and accomplishment, wise,
glorious, lord of all qualities, ruler of all worlds, accomplished. // SvayambhuP_4.104 //
Having gradually fulfilled the accumulation for enlightenment with concentration,
always in the great bliss and happiness of devotion to the Three Jewels, // SvayambhuP_4.105 //
enjoying with pure conduct, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes),
free from afflictions, conquering all the <s>Māras</s>, having attained <s>Arhatship</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.106 //
attaining the threefold enlightenment, you shall reach the state of a <s>Sambuddha</s> (fully awakened one).
All the people too, with their three spheres purified, // SvayambhuP_4.107 //
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, always born in good destinies,

children.text: bodhicaryā vrataṃ dhṛtvā saṃcaranto jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_4.108 //
children.translated_text: holding the vow of <s>Bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of enlightenment), acting for the welfare of the world, // SvayambhuP_4.108 //
having conquered all the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
free from afflictions, with pure selves, without craving for the courses of <s>Saṃsāra</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.109 //
as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Saṃbodhi</s>, they shall reach <s>Buddhahood</s>.

children.text: eṣāṃ ca vītarāgānāṃ aṣṭānāmapi sāmprataṃ // SvayambhuP_4.110 //
children.translated_text: Now, of these eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> also, // SvayambhuP_4.110 //

children.text: pūjāphala viśeṣatvaṃ va kṣyāmi śṛṇu tannṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: I shall speak of the special fruits of worship; listen, O king!

children.text: vāgmatisalile yastu snātvā nityaṃ samāhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.111 //
children.translated_text: He who, having bathed in the waters of <s>Vāgmatī</s>, always with concentration, // SvayambhuP_4.111 //
always worships these eight great lords, the <s>Vītarāgas</s>,

children.text: yatatpuṇya viśuddhātmā śrī samṛddhi sukhānvitaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.112 //
children.translated_text: by that merit, with purified self, endowed with auspicious prosperity and happiness, // SvayambhuP_4.112 //
having always enjoyed happiness in <s>Saṃsāra</s>, he shall go to the abode of <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious One).

children.text: ghṛtena snāpayet yastu vītarāgān svayaṃbhūvaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.113 //
children.translated_text: He who bathes the <s>Vītarāgas</s> of <s>Svayambhū</s> with ghee, // SvayambhuP_4.113 //
he too shall go to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>, the sweet realm of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: dadhnā yaḥ snāpayed devān vītarāgān svayaṃbhuvaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.114 //
children.translated_text: He who bathes the <s>Vītarāga</s> deities of <s>Svayambhū</s> with yogurt, // SvayambhuP_4.114 //

children.text: sa yāyād vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ śrī samṛddhi sukhāśrayaṃ /
children.translated_text: he shall go to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the abode of auspicious prosperity and happiness.
Even by bathing with sugarcane juice, one shall reach the realm of <s>Vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-bearers); // SvayambhuP_4.115 //
with perfumed water, the realm of <s>Gandharvas</s>; with milk, the abode of the Moon.
With cool water, the pure-souled one becomes sinless, with purified senses. // SvayambhuP_4.116 //

children.text: eṣāṃ pūjāṃ ca yaḥ kuryānnānāpuṣpaiḥ sugandhitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: He who performs worship of these with various fragrant flowers,

children.text: sarva kāma sukhaṃ bhuktvā modate manujādhipaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.117 //
children.translated_text: having enjoyed all desired pleasures, rejoices as a lord of men. // SvayambhuP_4.117 //
He who diligently offers excellent <s>Bilva</s> (wood-apple) leaves,

children.text: śivaṃ sarvatra prāpnoti yajñānāṃ ca sahasrakaṃ // SvayambhuP_4.118 //
children.translated_text: attains auspiciousness everywhere and the fruit of a thousand <s>Yajñas</s> (sacrifices). // SvayambhuP_4.118 //

children.text: naivedyaṃ ḍhokayedyaḥ sa dīrdhāyuḥ syād vali nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who offers <s>Naivedya</s> (food offering) shall have long life and be a mighty king;

children.text: dīpamālāṃ ca yo dadyāttejasvī syātsudṛṣṭimān // SvayambhuP_4.119 //
children.translated_text: and he who gives a garland of lamps shall be radiant and clear-sighted. // SvayambhuP_4.119 //
He who burns <s>Gugguru</s> (bdellium incense)—all his sins are destroyed;

children.text: tilapātraṃ ca yodadyādurggati sa vrajennahi // SvayambhuP_4.120 //
children.translated_text: he who gives a vessel of sesame shall never go to evil destinies. // SvayambhuP_4.120 //

children.text: suvarṇaṃ ye pradadyācca sa yāyāt saṅgatau sadā /
children.translated_text: He who gives gold shall always go to good company;

children.text: tiladhenuṃ pradadyādyoḥ sa saṃ yāyācchivālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_4.121 //
children.translated_text: he who gives a sesame-cow shall go to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.121 //

children.text: raupyakhurāṃ hema śṛṃgī raṇad ghaṇṭhāvalaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: With silver hooves, golden horns, adorned with tinkling bells,

children.text: savatsāṃ kapilāṃ dadyādyaḥ sa yajñaphalaṃ labhet // SvayambhuP_4.122 //
children.translated_text: he who gives a tawny cow with her calf shall obtain the fruit of sacrifice. // SvayambhuP_4.122 //

children.text: yo ratnakaṃcukaṃ dadyāt sa bhaved bahuratnavān /
children.translated_text: He who gives a jeweled garment shall become possessor of many jewels;
through the gift of cloth one becomes wealthy in cloth; through the gift of land, wealthy in land. // SvayambhuP_4.123 //
He who arranges great celebrations of music, singing, dancing, and the like,

children.text: yaḥ sadivya śrutiprāptaḥ śivapārśvacaro bhavet // SvayambhuP_4.124 //
children.translated_text: shall attain divine hearing and become an attendant of <s>Śiva</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.124 //

children.text: nīlotpalārkapadmāni yo dadyāt sa śriyaṃ labhet /
children.translated_text: He who offers blue lotuses, sun-lotuses, and other lotuses shall obtain prosperity;

children.text: yo 'rcayed vilvapatreṇa sa baliṣṭho bhavet kṛtī // SvayambhuP_4.125 //
children.translated_text: he who worships with <s>Bilva</s> leaves shall become strong and accomplished. // SvayambhuP_4.125 //

children.text: dhatturakena nirvārya kena vīreṇa sad vano /
children.translated_text: With <s>Dhattūra</s> (thorn-apple), with bold offerings, with noble intent,
he who worships with all kinds of fragrant flowers, even the eight, // SvayambhuP_4.126 //
he shall become prosperous, fortunate, and wise, dwelling in fragrance,
divinely beautiful, handsome, <s>Bhadraśrī</s>, rich in good qualities. // SvayambhuP_4.127 //
He who worships the auspicious ones with flowers, leaves, fruits, roots, or hymns,

children.text: sa devālayamāsādya bhuktvā divyasukhaṃ caret // SvayambhuP_4.128 //
children.translated_text: reaching the abode of the gods, shall enjoy divine happiness. // SvayambhuP_4.128 //
He who, having performed circumambulation, always worships with reverence,
shall become beautiful in form and in the end shall go to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.129 //
He who, with a clear mind, worships these great lords with hymns,

children.text: sa tu pitrālayaṃ gatvā mahānanda sukhaṃ labhet // SvayambhuP_4.130 //
children.translated_text: going to the realm of the ancestors, shall obtain great bliss and happiness. // SvayambhuP_4.130 //
He who, uttering and chanting their names with concentration,

children.text: so 'pi śrīmān mahābhijñaḥ prānte yāyācchivālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_4.131 //
children.translated_text: he too, prosperous and of great supernatural knowledge, shall in the end go to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>. // SvayambhuP_4.131 //

children.text: aṣṭāṃgaiḥ praṇatiṃ kṛtvā yo bhajet tān maheśvarān /
children.translated_text: He who, prostrating with the eight limbs, worships those great lords,

children.text: sa yāyāt saṅgatāveva durgatiṃ na kadācan // SvayambhuP_4.132 //
children.translated_text: he shall go to good company and never to evil destinies. // SvayambhuP_4.132 //

children.text: smṛtvā dhyātvā samuccārya nāmapi yo bhajat sadā /
children.translated_text: He who always worships by remembering, meditating, and uttering even the name,

children.text: sa divyāmṛtabhuṃjāno ramed divi yathāsukhaṃ // SvayambhuP_4.133 //
children.translated_text: he, partaking of divine nectar, shall rejoice in heaven as he wishes. // SvayambhuP_4.133 //
He who, having seen them, with a clear mind, joyfully bows with joined palms,

children.text: so 'pi divyāmṛtaṃ bhuktvā ramet svarge suraiḥ saha // SvayambhuP_4.134 //
children.translated_text: he too, having partaken of divine nectar, shall rejoice in heaven with the gods. // SvayambhuP_4.134 //
Thus, by the worship of these eight <s>Vītarāgas</s>, assuredly
knowing the special fruits, worship them as you desire. // SvayambhuP_4.135 //
Therefore, on this earth, having purified and established a city here,
establishing all people, always protecting them, dwell here. // SvayambhuP_4.136 //
Then, from all directions, all the people, delighted,

children.text: āgatya saṃsthiti kṛtvāni vaseyuḥ sadā mudā // SvayambhuP_4.137 //
children.translated_text: having come and settled, shall always dwell here joyfully. // SvayambhuP_4.137 //
Then, the countryside here, the villages, and cities too,

children.text: nirgama paktanaṃ cāpi pravarkteyuḥ samantataḥ // SvayambhuP_4.138 //
children.translated_text: and the markets and shops shall flourish on all sides. // SvayambhuP_4.138 //

children.text: tathā devā surendrāścaṃ sarve lokādhipā api /
children.translated_text: Likewise, gods, lords of gods, and all the rulers of the worlds,
having come here and beheld the <s>Dharmadhātu Svayambhū</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.139 //

children.text: gandharvā guhyakā yakṣāḥ kinnarā rākṣasā api /
children.translated_text: <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s> also,

children.text: kumbhāṇḍā garuḍā nāgāḥ siddhā vidyādharā api // SvayambhuP_4.140 //
