children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s> also, // SvayambhuP_4.140 //

children.text: sādhyāśca mātṛkā ścāpi sa bhairavagaṇā api /
children.translated_text: <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Mātṛkās</s> (mother goddesses), together with hosts of <s>Bhairavas</s>,

children.text: ṛṣayo yoginaścāpi yataya stīrthikā api // SvayambhuP_4.141 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣis</s> (seers), <s>Yogins</s>, ascetics, <s>Tīrthikas</s> also, // SvayambhuP_4.141 //
<s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples), <s>Bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Cailakas</s> (Jain monks), and <s>Upāsakas</s> (lay devotees),

children.text: bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ śaiva kaulāśca vaiṣṇavāḥ // SvayambhuP_4.142 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, <s>Śaivas</s>, <s>Kaulas</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.142 //
having come here and beheld the <s>Dharmadhātu Svayambhū</s>,
the goddess <s>Khagānanā</s>, and <s>Mañjudeva</s> the true <s>Guru</s>, // SvayambhuP_4.143 //
and these <s>Vītarāgas</s>, and the power of the <s>Tīrthas</s>,

children.text: prasāditāḥ samāśritya bhajeyuḥ sarvadā mudā // SvayambhuP_4.144 //
children.translated_text: being pleased, having taken refuge, shall always worship with joy. // SvayambhuP_4.144 //
Then, here, always, by the merit of all these,
there shall surely be abundance, auspicious festivities, and freedom from calamity. // SvayambhuP_4.145 //
Thus instructed by the lord of sages, <s>Krakucchanda</s>, at that time,
<s>Dharmākara</s>, having listened, acknowledged 'so be it' and was awakened. // SvayambhuP_4.146 //
Then that king, rising and with palms joined, to that lord of sages,

children.text: krakucchanda sa saṃghaṃ ya praṇatvevaṃ nyavedayata // SvayambhuP_4.147 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Krakucchanda</s> and his <s>Saṅgha</s> (community), having bowed, petitioned thus: // SvayambhuP_4.147 //
"Lord, having held your command, I shall here always

children.text: puraṃ vidhāya lokānāṃ hitārthe nivase khalu // SvayambhuP_4.148 //
children.translated_text: having established a city, you should dwell for the welfare of the people."
"May you, looking with compassion, always here in the <s>Himālaya</s>,
together with your assembly, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, dwell for the welfare of the world."

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tena bhagavān sa munīśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus entreated by him, the Blessed One, that lord of sages,
looking at <s>Dharmākara</s>, the great being, spoke thus:

children.text: nāhaṃ sadātra tiṣṭheyaṃ careyaṃ sarva bhūtale /
children.translated_text: "I shall not always remain here; I shall wander over the entire earth,

children.text: sarvasattva hitārtha hi bhavāmi dharmmadikṣiṇaḥ // SvayambhuP_4.151 //
children.translated_text: for I exist for the welfare of all beings, generous in <s>Dharma</s>."
Having thus instructed, the lord of sages <s>Krakucchanda</s>, together with his assembly,

children.text: tataḥ saṃprasthito 'nyatra deśeṃ saṃbhāṣayan yayau // SvayambhuP_4.152 //
children.translated_text: then set out and departed to another land, teaching as he went.

children.text: tato dharmākaraḥ so 'tra vidhāya nagaraṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Dharmākara</s>, having established a city there,
having set up the organs of government and established a kingdom, resided there.
Then all came there, and in the dwellings on all sides,

children.text: āśritya saṃsthitiṃ kṛtvā nivasanto mudā caran // SvayambhuP_4.154 //
children.translated_text: having taken up residence and settled, they dwelt joyfully.

body.translated_text: Then others also arrived from all directions, everywhere;

body.text: jānapade purenekaṃ grāmeṣu nyavasan mudā // SvayambhuP_4.155 //
body.translated_text: they dwelt joyfully in the countryside, in more than one city, and in villages.

children.text: tathā devā surādyāśca sarve lokādhipā api /
children.translated_text: Likewise the gods, celestials, and all the lords of the worlds,

children.text: svasvaparijanaiḥ sārddhaṃ āgatyātra mudā vasan // SvayambhuP_4.156 //
children.translated_text: together with their respective retinues, came and dwelt there joyfully.
Likewise the great sages, renunciants, and <s>brahmacārins</s>,
<s>yogins</s>, monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>), <s>Arhats</s>, those observing vows, and lay devotees (<s>upāsakas</s>),
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, cloth-clad ones (<s>cailakas</s>), and <s>Śrāvakas</s> also,

children.text: yathābhilaṣite deśe kṛtvā śramaṃ samāśrayan // SvayambhuP_4.158 //
children.translated_text: having established hermitages in their desired places, took up residence.

children.text: tathānya tīrthikāḥ śaivā vaiṣṇavāḥ kaulikā api /
children.translated_text: Likewise other sectarians (<s>tīrthikas</s>)—<s>Śaivas</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, and <s>Kaulikas</s> too—
having established hermitages in their desired places, took up residence.
<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) also, coming from all directions,

children.text: vivikte āśrame ramye samāśritya mudā vasan // SvayambhuP_4.160 //
children.translated_text: dwelling in secluded and pleasant hermitages, lived there joyfully.
Lords of sages also, having come and stayed here with their assemblies,

children.text: prārya sambodhi saddharmmaṃ samādeśyan tvarāgatāḥ // SvayambhuP_4.161 //
children.translated_text: having proclaimed the noble true <s>Dharma</s> of perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>), they had come.
Thus this most sacred land, called <s>Himālaya</s>,
beautiful like <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Pure Land), is the abode of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.
And here are many <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred bathing sites) that remove all sins,

children.text: jātāni santi sarvārtha samṛddhi siddhidāṇyapi // SvayambhuP_4.163 //
children.translated_text: which have arisen and exist, bestowing the fulfillment of all purposes and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment).

children.text: tadeteṣu ca tīrtheṣu snātvā carata sadvrataṃ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, at these <s>tīrthas</s>, having bathed, practice the good vow,

children.text: pāpaṃ hantuṃ śubhaṃ prāptuṃ samīchantyatra ye narāḥ // SvayambhuP_4.164 //
children.translated_text: those people who here wish to destroy sin and attain auspiciousness.

children.text: ye 'tra tīrtheṣu sarveṣu snātvā nityaṃ samāhita /
children.translated_text: Those who at all these <s>tīrthas</s>, having bathed, always concentrated,

children.text: japa yajñādi karmmāṇi kṛtvā caranti samvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_4.165 //
children.translated_text: performing <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), and other rites, practice the vow (<s>saṃvara</s>),
and worship the ancestors and the gods with faith and reverence,

children.text: datvā dānaṃ samādhāya dhyātvāpīśaṃ bhajanti ca // SvayambhuP_4.166 //
children.translated_text: giving charity, practicing concentration, meditating upon the Lord, and worshipping—
they too, all freed from impurity, purified in the three spheres,

children.text: śrīmantaḥ siddhi mantaśca bhaveyuḥ sadguṇāśrayāḥ // SvayambhuP_4.167 //
children.translated_text: glorious and possessed of <s>siddhi</s>, become repositories of good qualities.

children.text: tataste sarva sattvānāṃ hitārthe dharma sādhakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then they, practitioners of <s>Dharma</s> for the welfare of all beings,
become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, sons of the <s>Sugata</s>.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
having performed devotion to the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), should practice for the welfare of the world.
Then they, pure in soul, free from affliction, with conquered senses,

children.text: arhanta strividhāṃ bodhiṃ prāpyeyuḥ saugataṃ padaṃ // SvayambhuP_4.170 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, reach the state of the <s>Sugata</s>.
Thus, understanding this, at all these <s>tīrthas</s>, by those who desire <s>Bodhi</s>,

children.text: nātvā dānādi karma karttavya sarvadā bhave // SvayambhuP_4.171 //
children.translated_text: bathing, charity, and other rites should always be performed in every existence.
Having heard this instruction given by the lord of sages,

children.text: sarva sabhāśritā lokāḥ prābhyanandan pravodhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_4.172 //
children.translated_text: all the assembled people rejoiced and were awakened.

body.text: iti śrī svayaṃbhū caitya samutpatti kathā vītarāgatīrtha rāṣṭra pravarttano nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, named 'The Story of the Origin of the Glorious <s>Svayambhū Caitya</s>, the Establishment of the <s>Vītarāga Tīrtha</s> Kingdom.'
Fifth Chapter, named 'Description of the Great Merit Born from the Many <s>Tīrthas</s> Arising from the Origin of <s>Svayambhū</s>.'

children.translated_text: Then that great being <s>Maitreya</s>, with palms joined in joy,
entreated the Blessed One with reverence, saying thus:

children.text: bhagavan tatra tīrthānāṃ snātvā dānādi karmmajaṃ /
children.translated_text: "O Blessed One, please now instruct upon the special distinction of the merit
born from bathing, charity, and other rites at those <s>tīrthas</s>."
Thus entreated by him, the Blessed One, that lord of sages,
looking at that great being <s>Maitreya</s>, instructed thus:

children.text: sādhu śṛṇu mahāsattva tīrtha sevā phalodbhavaṃ /
children.translated_text: "Well done! Listen, O great being, to the fruit that arises from the service of <s>tīrthas</s>;

children.text: puṇyaṃ tad viśeṣatvaṃ vakṣāmi sarva bodhane // SvayambhuP_5.4 //
children.translated_text: I shall declare the special distinction of that merit for the awakening of all.
Now, the root <s>tīrthas</s> are said to be twelve here,

children.text: mahāpuṇyāni sarveṣāṃ tīrthānāṃ yāni bhūtale // SvayambhuP_5.5 //
children.translated_text: the most meritorious of all <s>tīrthas</s> on the earth.
Where the <s>Vāgmatī</s> river, the bestower of unfailing fruit, has its confluence,
that <s>tīrtha</s> is known as <s>Śodhana</s> (Purification), because it purifies the ten sins.
There the chief of <s>Nāgas</s>, passionate, named <s>Takṣaka</s>, of beautiful radiance,
is adorned with a blazing great jeweled, glorious hood.
Those people who at that holy <s>tīrtha</s>, with faith, according to the proper rites,

children.text: snānaṃ kuryumudā yāvadeka viṃśati vāsaraṃ // SvayambhuP_5.8 //
children.translated_text: perform bathing joyfully for up to twenty-one days,
and perform <s>japa</s>, <s>yajña</s>, and other rites for seven days,

children.text: pitṛn devāñca saṃpūjya kuryuḥ saṃtṛptamoditān // SvayambhuP_5.9 //
children.translated_text: and worship the ancestors and gods, making them satisfied and pleased,
and give gifts to supplicants as desired, with reverence,
of pure conduct, practicing concentration, and performing vows likewise—
they, purified by this merit, free from affliction, with pure senses,

children.text: bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhaveyuḥ śrī guṇāśrayāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.11 //
children.translated_text: become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, repositories of glorious virtues.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.
And then, where the <s>Māradāyinī</s> river has its confluence with the <s>Vāgmatī</s>,
that is known as the <s>Śānta Tīrtha</s> (Peaceful Sacred Site), which purifies the faults of affliction (<s>kleśa</s>).
There the chief of <s>Nāgas</s>, white, is renowned as <s>Somaśikhin</s>,
adorned with a hood-circle blazing with the glory of sparkling jewels.

children.text: tatrāpi śānta tīrtha ca ye kleśa duḥṣitā narāḥ /
children.translated_text: At that <s>Śānta Tīrtha</s>, those people who are afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)

children.text: kuryu snānaṃ sadā yāvadekaviṃśati vāsaraṃ // SvayambhuP_5.15 //
children.translated_text: should perform bathing always for up to twenty-one days,
and perform <s>japa</s>, <s>yajña</s>, and other rites, and observe the <s>poṣadha</s> vow,

children.text: pitṛn devāñca saṃpūjya kuryuḥ saṃtuṣṭananditān // SvayambhuP_5.16 //
children.translated_text: and worship the ancestors and gods, making them satisfied and delighted,
and give gifts to supplicants as desired, with joy,
of pure conduct and practice, meditating and worshipping the Lord.
They, anointed with this merit, purified in the three spheres,
become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, abodes of glorious virtues.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,

children.text: arhanta strividhāmbodhi prāpyeyuḥ saugataṃ padaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.19 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, reach the state of the <s>Sugata</s>.
And then, where the <s>Maṇirohiṇī</s> has its confluence with the <s>Vāgmatī</s>,
there, issuing forth from above, pure, resembling crystal and mirror,

children.text: rudradhārā mṛtākhyātā tayā ca tatra saṃgame /
children.translated_text: is the stream called <s>Rudrādhārā</s> (Stream of <s>Rudra</s>), and at that confluence,

children.text: triveṇī saṃgame tena śaṃkara tīrtha mucyate // SvayambhuP_5.21 //
children.translated_text: at the triple confluence (<s>Triveṇī Saṃgama</s>), it is called the <s>Śaṃkara Tīrtha</s>.
There the chief of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, white and exceedingly beautiful,
is adorned with a glorious hood blazing with the radiance of jewels.

children.text: tatra śaṃkara tīrthe ye mānavāśca yathāvidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: At that <s>Śaṃkara Tīrtha</s>, those people who according to the proper rites
perform bathing joyfully for up to twenty-one days,
and perform <s>japa</s>, <s>yajña</s>, and other rites for seven days,
and worship the ancestors and gods, satisfying them according to the proper rites,
and give gifts to supplicants with faith, with minds set on <s>Bodhi</s>,
meditating and worshipping the Lord, and observing the <s>poṣadha</s> vow—
they, purified in soul by this merit, free from affliction, with pure senses,

children.text: labheyuḥ śrī mahāpuṣṭiśānti guṇā ca śāntyapi // SvayambhuP_5.26 //
children.translated_text: shall obtain glorious great prosperity, peace, and virtues of pacification.

children.text: durggati tena yāyuśca saṃjātāḥ saṅgatau sadā /
children.translated_text: They shall not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies;
they become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, practitioners of auspicious conduct.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,

children.text: arhanta strividhāṃ bodhi prāpyeyuḥ saugataṃ padaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.28 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, reach the state of the <s>Sugata</s>.
And then, where the <s>Rājamañcarī</s> has its confluence with the <s>Vāgmatī</s>,
that is known as the <s>Rāja Tīrtha</s> (Royal Sacred Site), the place of kingship, health, and happiness.
There the chief of <s>Nāgas</s>, white, named <s>Surūpa</s>, exceedingly beautiful,
has his abode adorned with the great brilliance and glorious radiance of jewels.
There, those people who for twenty-one days

children.text: snāna dāna japa dhyānaṃ kuryu dadyuśca saṃvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_5.31 //
children.translated_text: perform bathing, charity, <s>japa</s>, and meditation, and give the vow (<s>saṃvara</s>)—
they, purified by this merit, faultless, with pure senses,

children.text: rājyaśvarya sadārogya bhadra saukhyama vāpnuyuḥ // SvayambhuP_5.32 //
children.translated_text: shall obtain kingship, sovereignty, constant health, auspicious happiness.

children.text: te 'pi na durggati yāyuḥ sadāsadgati saṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: They too shall not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies;
they become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, repositories of glorious virtues.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,

children.text: arhanta strividhāṃ bodhi prāpyayāyu jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.34 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.
Likewise here, at the confluence of the <s>Vimalāvatī</s> and the <s>Keśāvatī</s>,
that is known as <s>Manoratha</s> (Heart's Desire), bestowing ornaments as one wishes.
There the chief of <s>Nāgas</s>, fearsome, named <s>Kulika</s>, very dark,
has his abode adorned with the glorious radiance blazing from the jewels of his hood.

children.text: tatra manorathe tīrthe manujā ye yathāvidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: At that <s>Manoratha Tīrtha</s>, those people who according to the proper rites
perform bathing, charity, and other rites for twenty-one days—

children.text: te 'pi na durgatiṃ yāyuḥ sadā sadgatisaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: they too shall not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies;
they become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, repositories of auspicious glory and good qualities,
adorned with silk, fine garments, jewels, and ornaments as desired,
established in the welfare of all beings, they should practice the <s>Bodhi</s> vow (<s>saṃvara</s>).
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.
And then, at the confluence of the <s>Kusumāvatī</s> and the <s>Keśāvatī</s>,
that is known as the <s>Nirmala Tīrtha</s> (Pure Sacred Site), which destroys the obstacles of false conceptualization.
There the <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Palāla</s>, yellow in color, of great form,
is adorned with a glorious hood blazing with the radiance of divine jewels.
There, those people who for twenty-one days
perform bathing, charity, and other rites, and everything else as before—

children.text: te 'pi na durgatiṃ yāyuḥ sadā saṅgatisaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: they too shall not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies;
they become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, endowed with auspicious glory and good qualities,

children.text: kali vighna mala kleśa nirmukta bhadracāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: freed from the impurities and afflictions of the <s>Kali</s> age and its obstacles, practitioners of auspicious conduct.
devoted to the welfare of all beings, they become practitioners of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate conduct).
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.

children.text: tataḥ suvarṇṇavatyā ca bāgamatyā yatra saṃgame /
children.translated_text: Then, where the <s>Suvarṇavatī</s> and the <s>Bāgamatī</s> meet at their confluence,
the <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford) called <s>Nidhāna</s> (Treasury) is proclaimed, bestowing all prosperity.
There dwell two <s>Nāgas</s> of green color, <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>,

children.text: nānā ratna prabhāddīptiḥ śrī matphaṇāvibhūṣitau // SvayambhuP_5.48 //
children.translated_text: adorned with the splendor of various jewels, their glorious hoods beautifully decorated.
There, those humans who for twenty-one days
perform all rites such as bathing and the rest as before, according to the prescribed method—

children.text: te 'pi na durggatiṃ yāyuḥ sadā saṅgatisaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good company.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, the abode of auspicious glory and good qualities,
endowed with the welfare of all beings, they become practitioners of <s>Dharma</s>.
They too, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a <s>Sugata</s>.
Then, where the sin-destroying <s>Keśavatī</s> meets at the confluence,
the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Jñāna</s> (Knowledge) was proclaimed, bestowing divine enjoyment and happiness.

children.text: tatra nāgādhipaḥ śukla vāśukirnāma bhīṣaṇaḥ // SvayambhuP_5.53 //
children.translated_text: There the lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, white, named <s>Vāsuki</s>, fearsome,
adorned with the ornament of hoods radiant with the splendor of divine jewels.
There, those humans who for twenty-one days

children.text: snāna dānādi karmmāṇi kuryuḥ sarvāṇi purvavat /
children.translated_text: perform all rites of bathing, charity, and the rest as before—

children.text: te 'pi na durggati yāyurjātāḥ sadāpi saṅgatau // SvayambhuP_5.55 //
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good company.
Endowed with all enjoyments, great prosperity, happiness, free from illness,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes),
the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, they become practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: tathā te bodhisaṃbhāraṃ pūrayitvā yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.57 //
children.translated_text: Likewise they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of the Omniscient.
The foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, achievers of the qualities of a <s>Sambuddha</s>.

children.text: tataśca yatra vāgmatyāḥ keśāvatyā ca saṃgameḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, where the <s>Vāgmatī</s> and the <s>Keśāvatī</s> meet at their confluence,
that is proclaimed as <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (Wish-fulfilling Jewel), the wealth of all desired goals.

children.text: gaṃgā ca yamunācāpi tathā devī sarasvatī /
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>, and also the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: parva pratyāgatā tatra tena pañca samāgamā // SvayambhuP_5.60 //
children.translated_text: come there on festivals; thus there are five confluences.

children.text: tatra nāgādhipaḥ śuklo varuṇā sarva nāgarāt /
children.translated_text: There the lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, the white <s>Varuṇa</s>, king of all <s>Nāgas</s>,
adorned with the circle of hoods resplendent with the glory of divine jewels.
There, those humans who for twenty-one days
perform all rites of bathing, charity, and the rest as before, with respect—

children.text: te 'pi na durggatiṃ yāyuḥ sadā sadgatisaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
Of full and supreme lifespan, lords of knowledge, discerning,
of good progeny, great enjoyments, enjoyers of <s>Dharma</s>, wealth, and pleasure,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, they become practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.

children.text: tataśca yatra vāgmatyā ratnāvatyāḥ samāgame // SvayambhuP_5.66 //
children.translated_text: Then, where the <s>Vāgmatī</s> and the <s>Ratnāvatī</s> meet at their confluence,
the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Pramoda</s> (Delight) is proclaimed, bestowing love, affection, and wealth.

children.text: tatra nāgādhipaḥ padmo dhavaladivya sundaraḥ // SvayambhuP_5.67 //
children.translated_text: There the lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Padma</s> (Lotus), white, divine, and beautiful,
adorned with the circle of hoods of great brilliance of divine jewels.
There, those humans who for twenty-one days

children.text: snāna dānāni sarvāṇi kuryuḥ karmmāṇi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: perform all rites of bathing, charity, and the rest as before—

children.text: te 'pi nadurgatīṃ yāyuḥ sadā sadgati saṃbhavāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.69 //
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
Endowed with love, affection, delight, joy, and great happiness,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, purified in the three spheres,
the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, they become achievers of <s>Bodhi</s>.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, they go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.
Then, where the <s>Vāgmatī</s> and the <s>Cārumatī</s> meet at their confluence,
that is proclaimed as <s>Sulakṣaṇa</s> (Auspicious Sign), the wealth of glory, radiance, and fortune.

children.text: tatra nāgo mahāpadmo 'ti dhavalo 'ti sundaraḥ // SvayambhuP_5.73 //
children.translated_text: There the <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Mahāpadma</s> (Great Lotus), extremely white and most beautiful,
adorned with the circle of hoods resplendent with the glory of divine jewels.
There, those humans who for twenty-one days

children.text: snāna dānaṃ japa dhyānaṃ kuryuryajñaṃ ca pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: perform bathing, charity, <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and sacrifice as before—

children.text: te 'pina durgatiṃ yāyuḥ sadā sadgati saṃbhavāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.75 //
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
Endowed with glory, radiance, and objects of enjoyment, possessing beautiful form and auspicious marks,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, the abode of auspicious glory and good qualities,
devoted to the welfare of all beings, they become practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,

children.text: arhanta trividhāṃ bodhi prāpyeyuḥ saugataṃ padaṃ /
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: tataśca yatra vāgmatyā prabhāmatyā samāgameḥ // SvayambhuP_5.78 //
children.translated_text: Then, where the <s>Vāgmatī</s> and the <s>Prabhāmatī</s> meet at their confluence,
the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Jaya</s> (Victory) is proclaimed, the destroyer of fear from all enemies.

children.text: tatra nāgādhipaḥ śukraḥ śrīkānti divya sundaraḥ // SvayambhuP_5.79 //
children.translated_text: There the lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, of glorious beauty, divine and handsome,
adorned with the circle of hoods resplendent with the glory of divine jewels.

children.text: tatra ye mānavā yāvadeka viṃśativāsaraṃ // SvayambhuP_5.80 //
children.translated_text: There, those humans who for twenty-one days,

children.text: snātvā yajñādi karmmāṇi kuryuḥ sarvāṇi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: having bathed, perform sacrifice and other rites, all as before—

children.text: te 'pi na durggatīṃ yāyuḥ sadā sadgati saṃbhavāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.81 //
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
Fearless, endowed with the energy of the three qualities, victorious, having conquered enemies,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
of auspicious glory and good virtuous conduct, they become practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: dvādaśaitāni nāmāni tīrthāni mahāntyatra himālaye // SvayambhuP_5.84 //
children.translated_text: These twelve are the great <s>tīrthas</s> named here in the <s>Himālaya</s>;

children.text: anyānyapi ca saṃtyatra tāni vakṣyāmyahaṃ śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: there are others here too—I shall describe them; listen.
Then, near the <s>Vāgmatī</s>, in the vicinity of <s>Śrotasiddha</s> stream,
the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Saundarya</s> (Beauty) is proclaimed, bestowing the wealth of beauty and good qualities.
There, those humans who for twenty-one days

children.text: snāna dānāni karmmāṇi kuryuḥ sarvāṇi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: perform all rites of bathing, charity, and the rest as before—

children.text: te 'pina durggatiṃ yāyuḥ sadā sadgatisaṃbhavāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.87 //
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
Beautiful of form, endowed with auspicious marks, glorious, possessed of good qualities,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
they would practice the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s> (Bodhisattva vow), giving for the welfare of all beings.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, would proceed to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.
Above that, the <s>tīrtha</s> where the great sage <s>Agastya</s>

children.text: nityasnānaṃ japa dhyānaṃ kṛtvā yajñaṃ ca sevitaṃ /
children.translated_text: performed daily bathing, <s>japa</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and sacrifice,

children.text: tenāgastyaṃ mahattīrtha tadā khyāntaṃ munīśvaraiḥ // SvayambhuP_5.91 //
children.translated_text: and therefore that great <s>tīrtha</s> was proclaimed by the lords of sages as <s>Agastya</s> <s>tīrtha</s>.

children.text: tatra ye manujā snāyūste yāyuḥ paramāṃ gatiṃ /
children.translated_text: Those humans who bathe there would go to the supreme destination.

children.text: dāna yajña japādiśca kuryu dhyātvāyi ceśvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_5.92 //
children.translated_text: They should perform charity, sacrifice, <s>japa</s>, and the rest, meditating upon the Lord,
and also satisfy the ancestors and give charity as desired.
They all, of pure soul, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, become the abode of glory and good qualities.

children.text: tathā te bodhisaṃbhāraṃ pūrayitvā yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.94 //
children.translated_text: Likewise they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, would attain <s>Buddhahood</s>.
There, in the great lake where the <s>Nāga</s> <s>Ananta</s> (the Infinite) dwelt,
therefore that lake was proclaimed as <s>Ananta Tīrtha</s>, bestowing wealth.
There, those humans who for twenty-one days

children.text: snāna dāna japa dhyānaṃ kuryuryajñaṃca pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: perform bathing, charity, <s>japa</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and sacrifice as before—

children.text: te 'pi na durgatiṃ yāyuḥsadā sadgatisambhavāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.97 //
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, they become the abode of glory and good qualities.

children.text: tathā te bodhisambhāraṃ pūrayitvā yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.98 //
children.translated_text: Likewise they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of the Omniscient.
There too is the great <s>tīrtha</s> frequented by the noble <s>Tārā</s>,
and therefore it was celebrated as the <s>Āryatārā Tīrtha</s>, bestowing good fortune.
There too, those humans who for twenty-one days
perform bathing, charity, <s>japa</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and sacrifice according to the prescribed method—

children.text: te 'pi na durgatiṃ yāyuḥ saṃjātāḥ sadgatau sadā // SvayambhuP_5.101 //
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, purified in the three spheres,
endowed with good fortune, steadfast, the abode of auspicious glory and good qualities,
eager for the welfare of all beings, they become practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: tathā te bodhisaṃbhāraṃ pūrayitvā yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.103 //
children.translated_text: Likewise they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a <s>Sugata</s>.
Above the upper half of the <s>Vāgmatī</s> is the supreme <s>Prabha Tīrtha</s> (Radiance Ford),
proclaimed as the chief and foremost of all <s>tīrthas</s>.

children.text: tatraikasnāna mātreṇa gaṃgā snāna śatādhikaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.105 //
children.translated_text: There, by a single bathing alone, merit greater than a hundred bathings in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>
is accomplished, a greater merit bestowing desired goals and happiness.
There, those humans who for twenty-one days

children.text: snāna dāna japa dhyānaṃ yajñaṃ kuryuryuyathāvidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: perform bathing, charity, <s>japa</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and sacrifice according to the prescribed method—

children.text: śuviśuddha trikāyāste yathākāma sukhāśina ca // SvayambhuP_5.107 //
children.translated_text: they, well-purified in the three bodies (<s>trikāya</s>), enjoying happiness as they wish,
prosperous in <s>Dharma</s>, wealth, and glory, become those abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>.

children.text: kvacinna durggatiṃ yāyuḥ saṃjātā sadgato sadā // SvayambhuP_5.108 //
children.translated_text: They would never go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
Having done what benefits self and others, they would always conduct themselves in auspiciousness.
Then they, of pure soul, with well-purified senses and dispositions,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, become mines of good qualities.

children.text: tathā te bodhisaṃbhāraṃ pūrayitvā yathāvidhiḥ // SvayambhuP_5.110 //
children.translated_text: Likewise they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> according to the prescribed method,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: taṃ śaṃkhaparvata nāma sarva śiloccayottamaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.111 //
children.translated_text: The mountain named <s>Śaṅkha</s> (Conch), the finest among all rocky peaks—

children.text: samārohaṇa mātreṇa niṣṇā yeḥ siddhimān bhavet /
children.translated_text: by merely ascending it with devotion, one would become accomplished.

children.text: tatrāpi ye samāśritya snātvā dhyātvā samāhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_5.112 //
children.translated_text: There too, those who take refuge, having bathed and meditated with concentration,

children.text: japa yajñādi dānaṃ ca kuryuḥ saṃbodhimānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: perform <s>japa</s>, sacrifice, charity, and the rest, with minds set on <s>Sambodhi</s>—

children.text: te 'pi na durgatiṃ yāyuḥ sadāsadgati saṃbhavāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.113 //
children.translated_text: they too would not go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, purified in the three spheres,

children.text: niḥkleśā vimalātmānaḥ sarva sattva hitāśayāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.114 //
children.translated_text: free from afflictions, of pure soul, with dispositions directed to the welfare of all beings,
the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, they become practitioners of <s>brahmacarya</s>.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.

children.text: vahūni copa tīrthāni vidyante 'tra himālaye // SvayambhuP_5.116 //
children.translated_text: And many sacred <s>tīrthas</s> (pilgrimage sites) are found here in the <s>Himālayas</s>. // SvayambhuP_5.116 //

children.text: tāni tīrthāni sarvāṇi bhukti mukti pradānyapi /
children.translated_text: All those <s>tīrthas</s> bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation;

children.text: yatra yatra śravantīnāma nyeṣāṃ ca samāgame // SvayambhuP_5.117 //
children.translated_text: wherever the flowing rivers converge with others, // SvayambhuP_5.117 //

children.text: tatra tatrāpi tīrthāni puṇya phala pradāni hi /
children.translated_text: there too are <s>tīrthas</s> that grant the fruits of merit.

children.text: teṣāṃ cāpyupa tīrthānāṃ pṛthakpṛthatphalaṃ mahat // SvayambhuP_5.118 //
children.translated_text: And each of those subsidiary <s>tīrthas</s> also has its own great fruit, // SvayambhuP_5.118 //

body.translated_text: purifying sins, bestowing merit, the means to the happiness of the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: teṣvapi ye narāḥ snātvā careyu poṣaḍhaṃ vrataṃ // SvayambhuP_5.119 //
body.translated_text: Those people who, having bathed at these, observe the <s>Poṣadha</s> (Uposatha) vow, // SvayambhuP_5.119 //

children.text: dadyurdānāni cārthibhyaṃ kuryuryajñāni ca ye mudā /
children.translated_text: who give gifts to supplicants, and who joyfully perform sacrifices,
and who satisfy the ancestors and worship the gods, // SvayambhuP_5.120 //
remembering and meditating upon the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), worshipping with fire offerings,

children.text: evaṃ lokādhipānāṃ ca smṛtvā dhyātvā samāhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.121 //
children.translated_text: and likewise, remembering and meditating upon the lords of the worlds with concentration, // SvayambhuP_5.121 //
having chanted the <s>nāma-mantras</s>, they accomplish them according to the prescribed method.

children.text: tāni sarvāni sidhyeyuḥ sādhitāni jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_5.122 //
children.translated_text: All those accomplishments, performed for the welfare of the world, are fulfilled. // SvayambhuP_5.122 //
They grant auspicious celebration in this world, and in the next, the state of <s>Nirvṛti</s> (cessation).

children.text: te 'pi na durgatiṃ yāyuḥ sadā sadgatisaṃbhavāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.123 //
children.translated_text: They too shall never go to bad destinies, always born in good destinies, // SvayambhuP_5.123 //
free from afflictions, of pure souls, purified in the three spheres,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, dwelling in the four <s>Brahma-vihāras</s> (divine abodes), // SvayambhuP_5.124 //
endowed with auspicious glory and good qualities, they become practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulation of <s>Bodhi</s> in due order, // SvayambhuP_5.125 //
having attained <s>Arhat Bodhi</s>, they go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.
Having understood as one the true fruit of all the <s>tīrthas</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.126 //
the enthusiasm for auspicious glory and good qualities, the means to happiness and <s>Saṃbodhi</s> —
at all these <s>tīrthas</s>, with aspirations for the virtues of auspicious glory, // SvayambhuP_5.127 //

children.text: snāna dānādikaṃ karma karttavyaṃ bodhi prāptaye /
children.translated_text: bathing, giving, and other such acts should be performed for the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: ye ye eteṣu tīrtheṣu snātvā nityaṃ yathāvidhiḥ // SvayambhuP_5.128 //
children.translated_text: Those who, having bathed at these <s>tīrthas</s> always according to the prescribed method, // SvayambhuP_5.128 //

children.text: datvā dāna vrataṃ dhṛtvā dhyātvā bhajeyurīśvaraṃ /
children.translated_text: having given gifts, held vows, meditated, and worshipped the Lord —

children.text: te te sarve vikalmāṣāḥ pariśuddha trimaṇḍalāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.129 //
children.translated_text: all of them, freed from blemish, purified in the three spheres, // SvayambhuP_5.129 //
free from afflictions, of pure souls, shall become partakers of <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: iti lokādhipaiḥ sarve rbrahmendra pramukhairapi // SvayambhuP_5.130 //
children.translated_text: Thus all the lords of the worlds, led by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.130 //
have always frequented all these <s>tīrthas</s>.

children.text: tathā ca munibhiḥ sarvestāpa sairbrahmacāribhiḥ // SvayambhuP_5.131 //
children.translated_text: And likewise, all the sages, ascetics, <s>Brahmacārins</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.131 //
ascetics, <s>Yogins</s>, sectarian wanderers, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers),

children.text: brāhmaṇai vaiṣṇavaiḥ śaivaiḥ kaulikairapi śaktikairapi // SvayambhuP_5.132 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, <s>Śaivas</s>, <s>Kaulikas</s>, and <s>Śāktas</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.132 //
gods and <s>Dānavas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>,

children.text: guhyaka siddhasādhyai śca grahaiḥ vidyādharairapi // SvayambhuP_5.133 //
children.translated_text: <s>Guhyakas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, planets, and <s>Vidyādharas</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.133 //
and all the <s>Apsarases</s> have always frequented them.
Lords of <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.134 //
and thus others too, even the spirits, have frequented them seeking auspiciousness.
Planets and their attendants, those observing vows, and lay devotees, // SvayambhuP_5.135 //
<s>Bodhisattvas</s> and great sages have frequented them for the welfare of the world.
I too, likewise, approaching those <s>tīrthas</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.136 //

children.text: snātvā dānāni datvā ca kṛtvā yajñaṃ yathāvidhi /
children.translated_text: having bathed and given gifts, having performed sacrifice according to the prescribed method,
having also satisfied the ancestors and worshipped the gods, // SvayambhuP_5.137 //
having performed worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), I observed the <s>Poṣadha</s> vow,

children.text: dharmmadhātuṃ samārādhya smṛtvā dhyātvā samāhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_5.138 //
children.translated_text: having propitiated the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, remembering and meditating with concentration, // SvayambhuP_5.138 //
having chanted <s>dhāraṇī</s> mantras, practicing the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s> (Bodhisattva vow).
By the power of that merit, purified in the three spheres, // SvayambhuP_5.139 //
free from afflictions, of pure soul, dwelling in the four <s>Brahma-vihāras</s>,
a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a great being, endowed with the wealth of auspicious glory and good qualities, // SvayambhuP_5.140 //
having swiftly fulfilled the accumulation for <s>Saṃbodhi</s> in due order,
having conquered all the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, even in the <s>Kali</s> age, for the welfare of the world, // SvayambhuP_5.141 //
having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, I became the <s>Sambuddha</s>, the <s>Dharmarāja</s>, on earth.
You too, knowing this, free from obstacles, for the attainment of <s>Bodhi</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.142 //
practice according to the prescribed method at all those <s>tīrthas</s>.

children.text: dharmmadhātuṃ sadābhyarcya smṛtvā dhyātvā samāhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.143 //
children.translated_text: Always worshipping the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, remembering and meditating with concentration, // SvayambhuP_5.143 //
having chanted <s>dhāraṇī</s> mantras, worship for the welfare of the world.
By the power of that merit, purified in the three spheres, // SvayambhuP_5.144 //
you shall never go to bad destinies; be born always in good destinies.

children.text: tatra sadā triratnāno śaraṇe samupasthitāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.145 //
children.translated_text: There, always established in the refuge of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), // SvayambhuP_5.145 //
having performed worship with honors, conduct yourselves for the welfare of the world.
They indeed, of pure souls, dwelling in the four <s>Brahma-vihāras</s>, // SvayambhuP_5.146 //
shall become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, practitioners of auspicious conduct.
Then, endowed with the foundation of glorious good qualities, skilled in all knowledge, // SvayambhuP_5.147 //
conduct yourselves for the welfare of the world, bearing the welfare of all beings.

children.text: tataḥ saṃbodhiṃ saṃbhāraṃ pūrayitvā yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_5.148 //
children.translated_text: Then, having fulfilled the accumulation for <s>Saṃbodhi</s> in due order, // SvayambhuP_5.148 //
swiftly attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, you shall reach the state of the <s>Sugata</s>."

children.text: ityādiṣṭaṃ munīndreṇa śrutvā sarve pravodhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_5.149 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction of the great sage, all were enlightened; // SvayambhuP_5.149 //

body.translated_text: the assembly, led by <s>Maitreya</s>, attaining bliss, were awakened.

body.text: iti śrī svayaṃbhū samutpatti kathāyāṃ aneka tīrtha saṃjāta puṇya mahātmya varṇano nāma pañcamo 'dhyāya /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, named 'Description of the Great Merit Born from the Many <s>Tīrthas</s>,' in the story of <s>Śrī Svayambhū</s> Origin.
Sixth chapter, named 'The Establishment of the Well-Known Name <s>Svayambhū Dharmadhātu Vāgīśvara</s>.'

children.translated_text: Then that great being <s>Maitreya</s>, son of the <s>Sugata</s>,
bowing to the great sage <s>Śrīghana</s>, spoke thus with joined palms: // SvayambhuP_6.1 //
"O Blessed One, regarding this name '<s>Dharmadhātu Vāgīśvara</s>' —
by what cause did it become well-known? Please instruct us on that." // SvayambhuP_6.2 //

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tenaḥ maitreyeṇa sa sarvavit /
children.translated_text: Thus entreated by <s>Maitreya</s>, that omniscient one,
the Blessed One, looking at that great being, instructed thus: // SvayambhuP_6.3 //
"The cause by which this name '<s>Dharmadhātu Vāgīśvara</s>'

children.text: prasiddhiṃ tatpravakṣāmi śṛṇu maitreya sādaraṃ // SvayambhuP_6.4 //
children.translated_text: became well-known — that I shall declare. Listen, O <s>Maitreya</s>, with devotion. // SvayambhuP_6.4 //
When the lifespan of humans was thirty thousand years,
in the great city of <s>Śobhāvatī</s>, there arose a <s>Jina</s>: // SvayambhuP_6.5 //
the fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>, the worthy one, the teacher of the world, the <s>Dharmarāja</s>, the lord of sages,
named <s>Kanakamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the guide. // SvayambhuP_6.6 //
At that time, I was a son of good family named <s>Sudharma</s>, a knower of the self,
a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a great being, <s>Dharmaśrī</s>, bearing good qualities. // SvayambhuP_6.7 //
He, having taken refuge in the teaching of the teacher <s>Kanakamuni</s>,
performing worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), practiced the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s> (Bodhisattva vow). // SvayambhuP_6.8 //
When the Blessed Teacher, in the hermitage near <s>Śobhāvatī</s>,

children.text: vihāre śobhitārāme vijahāra sa sāṃghikaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.9 //
children.translated_text: dwelt in the beautiful garden-monastery together with his <s>Saṅgha</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.9 //

children.text: tadā tatra sabhāloke brahmendra pramukhāḥ surāḥ /
children.translated_text: then, there in the assembly, the gods led by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>,
and all the lords of the worlds came to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.10 //

children.text: sarve grahāśca tārāśca sarvā vidyādharā api /
children.translated_text: All the planets and stars, all the <s>Vidyādharas</s>,

children.text: siddhāḥ sādhyāśca rudrāśca munayo 'pi maharṣayaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, sages, and great seers, // SvayambhuP_6.11 //

children.text: gandharvāḥ kinnarā yakṣā guhyakā rākṣasā api /
children.translated_text: <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: kumbhāṇḍā garuḍā nāgā daityāścāpi samāgatāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Daityas</s> too assembled. // SvayambhuP_6.12 //
Ascetics, <s>Yogins</s>, sectarian wanderers, and practitioners of austerities,
heretics, wandering mendicants, <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jain monks), and <s>Brahmacārins</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.13 //
<s>Śramaṇas</s> (ascetics), <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers), those observing vows, and lay devotees —
they all came with devotion to drink the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.14 //
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, counselors, and common people,

children.text: gṛhādhipāśca śreṣṭāścaḥ bhṛtyāḥ sainyādhipā api // SvayambhuP_6.15 //
children.translated_text: householders, the eminent, servants, and military commanders, // SvayambhuP_6.15 //
artisans, merchants, caravan leaders, and great people,

children.text: paurā jānapadā grāmyāḥ kārpaṭikāśca śairikāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.16 //
children.translated_text: city-dwellers, country-folk, villagers, mendicant ascetics, and servants — // SvayambhuP_6.16 //
and others dwelling elsewhere too, all beings, pleased,
came with devotion to drink the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.17 //
Seeing all of them assembled, the Blessed One joyfully
sat upon his seat in the midst of the assembly, meditating and shining forth. // SvayambhuP_6.18 //

children.text: taṃ munīndraṃ prabhākāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve 'pi sāṃdhikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing that great sage, radiant with splendor, all the assembly members,

children.text: śravaṇāḥ śrāvakāḥ sarve bhikṣavo brahmacāriṇaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.19 //
children.translated_text: the listeners, all the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Bhikṣus</s>, and <s>Brahmacārins</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.19 //
<s>Bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), celibate women, <s>Upāsikās</s> (female lay devotees), and <s>Caīlakas</s> (naked ascetics),
naked ascetics, those observing vows, and lay devotees desiring the <s>Dharma</s> — // SvayambhuP_6.20 //

children.text: sarve 'pi te samāgatya praṇatvā taṃ munīśvaraṃ /
children.translated_text: all of them, having assembled and bowed to that lord of sages,
having circumambulated and honored him, took their seats to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.21 //

children.text: tato brahmadayo devāḥ sarve lokādhipā api /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> and other gods, and all the lords of the worlds,

children.text: taṃ munīndraṃ samabhyarcya praṇatvā ca yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.22 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped that great sage and bowed in due order, // SvayambhuP_6.22 //
having circumambulated and honored him, on all sides of that assembly,

children.text: saṃpaśyantaṃ munīndraṃ taṃ upatasthuḥ samāhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.23 //
children.translated_text: they stood composed, gazing upon that great sage. // SvayambhuP_6.23 //
Then all those people — sages, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, kings, and others —

children.text: taṃ munīndraṃ samabhyarcya saṃpraṇatvā yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.24 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped that great sage and bowed in due order, // SvayambhuP_6.24 //
having taken their seats in the assembly, surrounding him on all sides,
honoring and gazing upon him, they stood composed. // SvayambhuP_6.25 //

children.text: tatastān samupāsīnān dṛṣṭvā sa bhagavān mudā /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing them all seated, the Blessed One joyfully
beginning with the <s>Āryasatya</s> (Noble Truths), taught the true <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.26 //
Progressively teaching the practice of <s>Bodhi</s> and the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>Āryāṣṭāṅga Satpatha</s>),

children.text: ādiśya bodhimārge tān sarvāllokān yojayet // SvayambhuP_6.27 //
children.translated_text: instructing in the path to <s>Bodhi</s>, he set all beings upon it. // SvayambhuP_6.27 //
Having drunk that nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, all the beings were enlightened,

children.text: saddharmma sādhanā yuktā babhūvu rbodhimānasāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.28 //
children.translated_text: and became devoted to the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>, with minds set on <s>Bodhi</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.28 //
At that time, in a monastery called <s>Vikramaśīla</s>, there was a self-knowing <s>Bhikṣu</s>,
dwelling with his <s>Saṅgha</s>, the wise ascetic named <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.29 //
He, having taken his place there for the welfare of all beings,
together with his <s>Saṅgha</s>, wished to expound the <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s> (Chanting of Names). // SvayambhuP_6.30 //

children.text: tataḥ sa satmatiḥ sarvān saṃghā nāma prasādaraṃ /
children.translated_text: Then that one of true wisdom, together with all the <s>Saṅgha</s>, with grace,
sat upon his seat in the midst of the assembly, absorbed in meditation. // SvayambhuP_6.31 //

children.text: taṃ sabhāsana āsīnaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve 'pi sāṃghikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing him seated upon the assembly seat, all the <s>Saṅgha</s> members,
desiring to drink the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, assembled with devotion. // SvayambhuP_6.32 //

children.text: tatra ye yatiṃ natvā parivṛtya samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: There, those who had bowed to the ascetic, surrounding him on all sides,
honoring and gazing upon him, stood composed. // SvayambhuP_6.33 //
There, others too arrived — beings, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, kings, and others,

children.text: vaiśyāśca mantrino 'mātyāḥ bhṛtyā sainyādhipā api // SvayambhuP_6.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiśyas</s>, counselors, ministers, servants, and military commanders, // SvayambhuP_6.34 //
artisans, merchants, caravan leaders, and great people —
Townsfolk, villagers, country-dwellers, and inhabitants of other lands, // SvayambhuP_6.35 //

children.text: sarve te samupāgatya praṇatvā taṃ yatiṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: all of them, having come and bowed to that ascetic with joy,
surrounding and attending him, gazing at him, took their seats. // SvayambhuP_6.36 //
Then that ascetic, seeing all of them assembled,
narrated the <s>Mañjuśrī-nāma-saṃgīti</s> (Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī) in proper order. // SvayambhuP_6.37 //
Having heard that instruction, all the people assembled,
understanding the glory of the qualities of the <s>Saṃbuddha</s>, were awakened with joy. // SvayambhuP_6.38 //
Then all those people, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, kings and others,

children.text: natvā taṃ yatimāmantrya svasvālayaṃ mudāyayuḥ // SvayambhuP_6.39 //
children.translated_text: bowing to that ascetic, having taken leave, went joyfully to their respective abodes. // SvayambhuP_6.39 //
Then those wise <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), ascetics, celibate practitioners,
wished to properly hear the secret meaning of the twelve syllables. // SvayambhuP_6.40 //

children.text: tataste yoginaḥ sarve kṛtāñjali puṭā mudā /
children.translated_text: Then all those yogins, with cupped palms, in joy,

children.text: śāstāraṃ taṃ yatiṃ natvā samāmatryaivamavruvan // SvayambhuP_6.41 //
children.translated_text: bowing to that teacher, the ascetic, addressed him and spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_6.41 //
"Venerable one, the purification of the twelve syllables in particular —
we wish to hear about it; please instruct about that." // SvayambhuP_6.42 //

children.text: iti tai rprārthitaṃ dharmmaśrī mitraḥ sasudhīrapi /
children.translated_text: Thus requested by them, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, though wise,

children.text: dvādaśākṣara guhyārthaṃ viśuddhiṃ na samādiśat // SvayambhuP_6.43 //
children.translated_text: could not instruct on the secret meaning of the purification of the twelve syllables. // SvayambhuP_6.43 //

children.text: taṃ viśuddhā nabhijñātā viṣaṇṇātmā sa utthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Unable to know that purification, his spirit dejected, he arose,
and seated in his meditation chamber, meditating, he pondered thus: // SvayambhuP_6.44 //
"The purification of the secret meaning of these syllables is not known to me;

children.text: tatkathaṃ upadekṣyāmi hāhā kutra bhrameyahi // SvayambhuP_6.45 //
children.translated_text: then how shall I instruct? Alas, where shall I wander?" // SvayambhuP_6.45 //
Thus dejected in spirit with such thoughts, his mind confounded with shame,

children.text: smṛtvā ratnatrayaṃ dhyātvā tasthau dhairyasamāhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.46 //
children.translated_text: remembering the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels) and meditating, he stood firm with composure. // SvayambhuP_6.46 //
At that very moment, through the power of merit from remembering the <s>Triratna</s>,
he obtained this resolve: great energy and great zeal. // SvayambhuP_6.47 //
Then that one, bold in intellect, meditating again with concentration,

children.text: manasā sarva lokeṣu vicārayan vyalokayan // SvayambhuP_6.48 //
children.translated_text: surveyed and examined all the worlds with his mind. // SvayambhuP_6.48 //
Then he saw in <s>Mahācīna</s> (Great China), in the north, on the supreme mountain,
<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the one of great supernatural knowledge, the supreme lord of all <s>vidyās</s> (knowledge), // SvayambhuP_6.49 //
the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the great being, the master and lord of all <s>dharmas</s>,
the giver of understanding and knowledge of all secret purified meanings. // SvayambhuP_6.50 //

children.text: taṃ paśyan manasā dharmmaśrī mitraḥ samutsukaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing him with his mind, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, filled with longing,
quickly rose and addressed those communities assembled, speaking thus: // SvayambhuP_6.51 //
"O venerable ones, I shall go to <s>Mahācīna</s>, to the supreme mountain;
I wish to see <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the great being, right now. // SvayambhuP_6.52 //
The detailed secret purification of this <s>Nāma-saṃgīti</s> —

children.text: pṛṣṭā samyak vijñāya āgamiṣyāmyahaṃ drutaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.53 //
children.translated_text: having asked and properly understood it, I shall return quickly. // SvayambhuP_6.53 //
Until I come back here, all of you, with concentration,

children.text: triratna bhajanaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhata mā viṣīdata // SvayambhuP_6.54 //
children.translated_text: performing worship of the <s>Triratna</s>, remain — do not be disheartened." // SvayambhuP_6.54 //
Having spoken thus, that one of great supernatural knowledge then set forth quickly,
and wandering, arrived here in the land of <s>Nepāla</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.55 //

children.text: tamāyātaṃ yatiṃ natvā mañjudevaḥ sa sarvavit /
children.translated_text: Bowing to that arriving ascetic, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the all-knowing,
wished to approach him and test him, displaying supernatural powers. // SvayambhuP_6.56 //
Then <s>Mañjudeva</s>, having himself become a farmer,
was plowing the earth with a plow drawn by a tiger and a deer-king. // SvayambhuP_6.57 //
Seeing him from afar, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s> was extremely astonished:
"What is this great wonder?" — and he went to see it. // SvayambhuP_6.58 //
Then, having approached and seen that great marvel,
he addressed that farmer and asked, looking at him: // SvayambhuP_6.59 //
"O good man, from this land, the supreme mountain of <s>Mahācīna</s>,
<s>Pañcaśīrṣa</s> (Five-Peaked) — how far is it? Please tell me." // SvayambhuP_6.60 //

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ tena śrutvā sa halavāhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this request, that plowman
looked at that ascetic for a long time and spoke thus with respect: // SvayambhuP_6.61 //
"From where have you come here, and for what purpose on this northern path

children.text: mahācīnasya dūrato gantuṃ tvaṃ paripṛccha se // SvayambhuP_6.62 //
children.translated_text: do you ask about going to the distant <s>Mahācīna</s>? // SvayambhuP_6.62 //

children.text: adya pravartate sāyaṃ tad vihāre mamāśrame /
children.translated_text: The evening is now approaching; therefore, in my hermitage monastery,

children.text: uṣitvā prāta rutthāya gaccha maddeśitātpathaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.63 //
children.translated_text: having stayed the night, rise in the morning and go by the path I shall show you." // SvayambhuP_6.63 //

children.text: iti tenoditaṃ dharmaśrī mitro niśaṃmya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard what was spoken by him, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>

children.text: tathetyanumataṃ dhṛtvā tūṣṇīṃ bhūtvā vyatiṣṭhataḥ // SvayambhuP_6.64 //
children.translated_text: accepted it saying 'so be it,' and remained in silence. // SvayambhuP_6.64 //

children.text: tataḥ saṃbodhitaṃ bhikṣu matvā sa halavāhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, considering the <s>bhikṣu</s> to be awakened, that plowman
made those two, the tiger and the deer-king, disappear right there. // SvayambhuP_6.65 //
The plow, however, for the purpose of awakening all beings,

children.text: tatraivocca sthala kṣetre yūpa vadavaropayat // SvayambhuP_6.66 //
children.translated_text: he planted there in a high field like a sacrificial post. // SvayambhuP_6.66 //
Even today that place of earth is renowned as <s>Mañjuśrībhū</s> (Land of Mañjuśrī),

children.text: sāvāceti prasiddhā ca yatrāvaropitaṃ halaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.67 //
children.translated_text: and that where the plow was planted is known as <s>Sāvācā</s>. // SvayambhuP_6.67 //
Then, having called that ascetic, that plowman in the evening,

children.text: tatra praviśya dharmaśrīmitra saṃprati vismitaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.68 //
children.translated_text: entering there, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s> was at that moment amazed. // SvayambhuP_6.68 //
Then, having respectfully offered roots, fruits, leaves and other provisions

children.text: datvā tasmai svayaṃ bhuktvā tasthau sa halavāhakaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.69 //
children.translated_text: to him, and having eaten himself, that plowman remained. // SvayambhuP_6.69 //
Then <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, having spoken various night-time tales,

children.text: bhāṣitvā taṃ mahābhijñaṃ kṛṣikaraṃ vyanodayan // SvayambhuP_6.70 //
children.translated_text: entertained that one of great supernatural knowledge, the farmer. // SvayambhuP_6.70 //

children.text: tataḥ sa mañjudevastaṃ yati chātrālaye niśi /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjudeva</s>, having sent that ascetic to the guest quarters for the night,

children.text: preṣayitvā svayaṃ gahvāgāre śayyāṃ samāśrayat // SvayambhuP_6.71 //
children.translated_text: himself went to the inner chamber and retired to bed. // SvayambhuP_6.71 //

children.text: tatra praviśya dharmmaśrī mitra saṃprati vismitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Entering there, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, amazed at that moment,
having slept briefly, rose and pondered thus in his mind: // SvayambhuP_6.72 //
"No sleeping arrangements were made here today; this man is of great powers;

children.text: bhāryāyā sahasākathyaṃ kiṃkiṃ kuryād vinodayaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.73 //
children.translated_text: speaking to his wife in secret — what kind of entertainment might he be doing?" // SvayambhuP_6.73 //
Thus meditating, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, the ascetic, rose
and, keeping his vows discreetly, approached the base of the door. // SvayambhuP_6.74 //

children.text: tatkṣaṇe mañjudevaṃ taṃ keśinī supriyā satī /
children.translated_text: At that moment, <s>Keśinī</s>, the beloved, virtuous wife,
seated on the bed, spoke thus to her husband <s>Mañjudeva</s>: // SvayambhuP_6.75 //
"My lord, who is this wise ascetic, and for what purpose has he come to our hermitage?
From where has he come here? Please instruct about that." // SvayambhuP_6.76 //

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ devyā mañjudevo niśamya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this request of the goddess, <s>Mañjudeva</s>,

children.text: keśinīṃ tāṃ priyāṃ bhāryāṃ sampaśyannevamavravīt // SvayambhuP_6.77 //
children.translated_text: looking at <s>Keśinī</s>, his beloved wife, spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_6.77 //

children.text: sādhu śṛṇu priye devī yadartha yamimihāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Well said! Listen, O beloved goddess, for what purpose this one has come here;

children.text: tadartha hi mahaddhetuṃ vakṣyāmi te vicārayat // SvayambhuP_6.78 //
children.translated_text: I shall tell you the great reason for that purpose — consider it. // SvayambhuP_6.78 //
This <s>bhikṣu</s> of great supernatural knowledge, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of great wisdom,
is the renowned one known as the great <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, the ascetic. // SvayambhuP_6.79 //
He dwells in the monastery called <s>Vikramaśīla</s>,

children.text: nāmasaṃgīti vyākhyānaṃ śikṣebhyo vistaraṃ vyadhāt // SvayambhuP_6.80 //
children.translated_text: and expounded the commentary on the <s>Nāma-saṃgīti</s> in detail to his disciples. // SvayambhuP_6.80 //
The detailed knowledge of the purification of the secret meaning of the twelve syllables —

children.text: nāma samyagupākhyātuṃ śaknoti na sudhīrapi // SvayambhuP_6.81 //
children.translated_text: even that wise one is unable to properly explain the name. // SvayambhuP_6.81 //
Then he, dejected in spirit, seated in his meditation chamber,

children.text: dhyātvā lokeṣu sarvatra vilokyaivaṃ vyacintayan // SvayambhuP_6.82 //
children.translated_text: meditating, surveying everywhere in the worlds, pondered thus: // SvayambhuP_6.82 //
'Only <s>Mañjuśrī</s> would know — the knower of all secret purification;
he would instruct on the purification of the secret meaning of the twelve syllables.' // SvayambhuP_6.83 //

children.text: iti dhyātvā samutthāya sarvān śiṣyānsa sāṃghikān /
children.translated_text: Thus meditating, having risen, having awakened all his disciples and companions,
with great zeal and energy, he set forth from there. // SvayambhuP_6.84 //
To the north, in <s>Mahācīna</s>, to <s>Pañcaśīrṣa</s>, to my hermitage —
traveling by this path, he has come here. // SvayambhuP_6.85 //
Having seen him arrive here, through the power of supernatural vision,
having awakened him, I have invited him thus — I shall lead him to our hermitage now. // SvayambhuP_6.86 //

children.text: iti bhaktā samādiṣṭaṃ śrutvā sā keśinī priyā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction to his devoted wife, that beloved <s>Keśinī</s>,

children.text: svāminaṃ taṃ samālokya papracchaivaṃ samādarāt // SvayambhuP_6.87 //
children.translated_text: looking at her husband, asked thus with respect: // SvayambhuP_6.87 //

children.text: svāminahaṃ na jānāmi śṛṇomi na kadācana /
children.translated_text: "My lord, I do not know, I have never heard —
for the purpose of this purification, instruct me now." // SvayambhuP_6.88 //

children.text: iti saṃprāthitaṃ devyā mañjudevo niśamya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this request of the goddess, <s>Mañjudeva</s>,

children.text: keśinīṃ tāṃ priyāṃ bhāryā sampaśyannevamavravīt // SvayambhuP_6.89 //
children.translated_text: looking at <s>Keśinī</s>, his beloved wife, spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_6.89 //
"Well said, O goddess! For your delight, it shall now be instructed;
this great secret teaching must be carefully guarded." // SvayambhuP_6.90 //
Having spoken thus, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, to that goddess, according to proper method,
instructed the purification of the secret meaning of the twelve syllables. // SvayambhuP_6.91 //
Having heard all this narrated in detail, that great-minded one,
<s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, was awakened with supreme joy. // SvayambhuP_6.92 //

children.text: tata samudito dharmmaśrī mitra utthite mudā /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, elated, rising with joy,
arrived at the certainty: 'This is indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>!' // SvayambhuP_6.93 //
Then, with a supremely serene mind, at the base of the door, with cupped palms,

children.text: aṣṭāṃga praṇatiṃ kṛtvā tasthau tadgata mānasaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.94 //
children.translated_text: having performed the eightfold prostration, he stood with his mind absorbed in him. // SvayambhuP_6.94 //
Then in the morning, having risen, <s>Keśinī</s>, the giver of liberation,
opened the door and began to go outside. // SvayambhuP_6.95 //
There, seeing that ascetic standing at the base of the door,

children.text: bhītā sā keśinī devī drutamupācaratprabhoḥ // SvayambhuP_6.96 //
children.translated_text: that goddess <s>Keśinī</s>, frightened, quickly went to her lord. // SvayambhuP_6.96 //

children.text: tāṃ pratyāgatāṃ dṛṣṭvā mañjudevaḥ sa sarvavit /
children.translated_text: Seeing her return, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the all-knowing,
looking at her troubled face, asked thus with concern: // SvayambhuP_6.97 //
"Goddess, why have you opened the door and come back so hastily?

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kiṃ tatra bhītāsi tatsatyaṃ vada me puraḥ // SvayambhuP_6.98 //
children.translated_text: What did you see there that frightened you? Tell me the truth now." // SvayambhuP_6.98 //

children.text: iti pṛṣṭe jagacchāstā bharktā sā keśinī virāt /
children.translated_text: Thus asked, <s>Keśinī</s>, the wife of the teacher of the world,
looking at her husband, gently reported thus: // SvayambhuP_6.99 //
"My lord, that ascetic, having bowed, has fallen at the base of the door;

children.text: jīvito vā mṛtau vāsau mayā na jñāyate khalu // SvayambhuP_6.100 //
children.translated_text: whether he is alive or dead, I truly do not know." // SvayambhuP_6.100 //

children.text: ityuktaṃ bhāryayā śrutvā mañjudevaḥ sa utthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard what his wife said, <s>Mañjudeva</s> arose,

children.text: upetya dvāramūle taṃ saṃdadarśa nipātitaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.101 //
children.translated_text: and going to the base of the door, he saw him fallen there. // SvayambhuP_6.101 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sa mañjudevastaṃ yatiṃ dhyātvā jitendriyaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having seen him, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, meditating upon that ascetic of conquered senses,
grasping his hand, raising him up, looking at him, spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_6.102 //
"O ascetic, for what purpose have you stood here thus, meditating at the door?

children.text: tatmamapurataḥ sabhyaṃ vadaya te samāhitaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.103 //
children.translated_text: Tell me properly, in my presence, what you have in your concentrated mind." // SvayambhuP_6.103 //
Thus addressed by <s>Mañjudeva</s>, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, with an exalted mind,
bowed to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> with the eightfold prostration and requested thus with joy: // SvayambhuP_6.104 //
"O <s>Bhagavān</s>, lord, omniscient one, supreme master of all <s>vidyās</s>,
at your lotus feet, with devotion, I take refuge. // SvayambhuP_6.105 //
You alone are the teacher of the world, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>;

children.text: jñāyate dṛśyate hyatra jñānaratnanidhi rmayā // SvayambhuP_6.106 //
children.translated_text: for here I perceive and behold a treasury of the jewel of knowledge. // SvayambhuP_6.106 //
You, Lord, know the purpose for which I have come here;
may the Teacher be worthy of fulfilling my desire. // SvayambhuP_6.107 //

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ tena mañjudeva niśamya sa /
children.translated_text: Having heard this entreaty by him, <s>Mañjudeva</s>,
recognizing that one of great supernatural knowledge, looking at him, spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_6.108 //

body.text: kathaṃ vinā abhiṣekaṃ te mantrārthamupadeśyate // SvayambhuP_6.109 //
body.translated_text: "How can the meaning of the <s>mantras</s> be taught to you without <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration)? // SvayambhuP_6.109 //

children.translated_text: Therefore, first receive the <s>abhiṣeka</s> here, if you so desire."

children.text: ityuktaṃ mañjudevena niśamya sa yatiḥ sudhīḥ // SvayambhuP_6.110 //
children.translated_text: Having heard what was spoken by <s>Mañjudeva</s>, that wise ascetic, // SvayambhuP_6.110 //
bowing to <s>Mañjudeva</s>, spoke thus with palms joined:
"Omniscient Lord, O Teacher, I am without wealth, possessing nothing. // SvayambhuP_6.111 //

children.text: kiṃ dāsye bhavataṃ śāstre dakṣiṇāṃ guru bhaktimān /
children.translated_text: What shall I give as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) to you, the Teacher, being devoted to the <s>Guru</s>?"

children.text: iti tenoditaṃ śrutvāḥ mañjudevaḥ sasanmatiḥ // SvayambhuP_6.112 //
children.translated_text: Having heard what was spoken by him, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the one of true wisdom, // SvayambhuP_6.112 //
looking at that ascetic <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, spoke thus:

children.text: yataḥ kiṃ dhanasaṃpatyā śraddhā te yadi vidyate // SvayambhuP_6.113 //
children.translated_text: "What need is there of wealth? If you have faith, // SvayambhuP_6.113 //
<s>Gurus</s> are satisfied by devotion alone, not by wealth here."
Hearing this spoken by <s>Mañjudeva</s>, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, overjoyed, // SvayambhuP_6.114 //
bowing to that <s>Guru</s> with the eight-limbed prostration, entreated with reverence thus:

children.text: bhagavanyadi bhaktyaiva tuṣyate 'tra bhavān mama // SvayambhuP_6.115 //
children.translated_text: "Lord, if you are indeed satisfied here by my devotion alone, // SvayambhuP_6.115 //
I shall render devoted service to you.

children.text: iti me kṛpayā śāsta abhiṣeka yathāvidhiḥ // SvayambhuP_6.116 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, O Teacher, with compassion, granting me the <s>abhiṣeka</s> according to the proper rites, // SvayambhuP_6.116 //
you are worthy of giving the purification of the meaning of the twelve <s>mantras</s>."

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ tena mañjudevaṃ sa sarvavit // SvayambhuP_6.117 //
children.translated_text: When thus entreated by him, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the all-knowing one, // SvayambhuP_6.117 //
seeing him as devoted, spoke thus:

children.text: dāsyāmi te mahābhāga bhakti śraddhāsti te yadi // SvayambhuP_6.118 //
children.translated_text: "I shall give it to you, O fortunate one, if you have devotion and faith. // SvayambhuP_6.118 //
With a clear mind, receive the <s>abhiṣeka</s> with concentration."

children.text: tataḥsa mañjudevaḥ śrī vajrācārya yathāvidhi // SvayambhuP_6.119 //
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Mañjudeva</s>, the glorious <s>Vajrācārya</s> (vajra-master), according to the proper rites, // SvayambhuP_6.119 //
established the <s>maṇḍala</s> called <s>Dharmadhātu Vāgīśvara</s>,
and having worshipped and venerated that <s>maṇḍala</s> according to the proper rites, // SvayambhuP_6.120 //

children.text: abhiṣekaṃ prasannāya tasmai dadau sa vajradhṛk /
children.translated_text: that <s>vajra</s>-holder bestowed the <s>abhiṣeka</s> upon that one whose mind was clear.

children.text: tatastān maṇḍale devān saṃdarśayaṃ yathākramāt // SvayambhuP_6.121 //
children.translated_text: Then, showing to him the deities in the <s>maṇḍala</s> in proper order, // SvayambhuP_6.121 //
having worshipped according to ability, he joined him to the refuge.
Then, to that one whose mind was clear, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, according to the proper rites, // SvayambhuP_6.122 //
instructed the purification of the secret meaning of the twelve syllables.
Then, having received the <s>abhiṣeka</s>, that <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, with great joy, // SvayambhuP_6.123 //
attained the knowledge of the purification of the secret meaning of the twelve <s>bhūmis</s> (stages).

children.text: tasmai śāstre sabhāryāya svamātmānaṃ sa dakṣiṇāṃ // SvayambhuP_6.124 //
children.translated_text: To that Teacher, together with his wife, he offered himself as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee), // SvayambhuP_6.124 //

children.text: saṃkalpya śraddhayā bhaktyā natvaivaṃ prārthayan mudā /
children.translated_text: resolving with faith and devotion, bowing, he entreated joyfully thus:

children.text: bhagavan nātha sarvajña bhavat kṛpā prasādataḥ // SvayambhuP_6.125 //
children.translated_text: "Lord, Protector, Omniscient One, by the grace of your compassion, // SvayambhuP_6.125 //
my purpose is fully accomplished; I become a bearer of auspicious glory and good qualities.
Therefore, I, always having taken refuge at your feet, // SvayambhuP_6.126 //
shall conduct myself in existence just as you have instructed.
Therefore, granting me permission, the means to the knowledge of <s>Saṃbodhi</s> (perfect enlightenment), // SvayambhuP_6.127 //
I shall practice the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s> (vow of enlightenment) for the welfare of all beings."

children.text: iti saṃprārthya dharmaśrī mitra sa samupāśritaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.128 //
children.translated_text: Having thus entreated, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, having taken refuge, // SvayambhuP_6.128 //
with a mind clear through faith and devotion, became supreme in service to the <s>Guru</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sa mañjudevastaṃ mahāsattvaṃ vicakṣaṇaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.129 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjudeva</s>, considering that great being as discerning, // SvayambhuP_6.129 //
urged and encouraged him to engage in the practice of <s>Saṃbodhi</s>:

children.text: sādhu sādhu mahābhāgaḥ saṃcaratvaṃ jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_6.130 //
children.translated_text: "Well done! Well done! O fortunate one! Conduct yourself for the welfare of the world! // SvayambhuP_6.130 //

children.text: saṃbodhi sādhanaṃ bodhicaryā vrata sadā bhava /
children.translated_text: Always be in the vow of <s>Bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of enlightenment), the means to <s>Saṃbodhi</s>.
Anointed with this merit, with the three spheres purified, // SvayambhuP_6.131 //
<s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great supernatural knowledge, you shall become the abode of auspicious glory and good qualities.
Then, having fulfilled the accumulation for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order, // SvayambhuP_6.132 //
free from afflictions, having attained enlightenment, you shall reach the state of a <s>Sambuddha</s>.

children.text: iti me śāsanaṃ dhṛtvā smṛtvā dhyātvā samāhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.133 //
children.translated_text: Thus, holding my teaching, remembering and meditating with concentration, // SvayambhuP_6.133 //
having taken refuge in the Three Jewels, conduct yourself for the welfare of the world.

children.text: yadi jagaddhitaṃ kartuṃ saṃbodhiṃ prāpnumicchasi // SvayambhuP_6.134 //
children.translated_text: If you wish to work for the welfare of the world and attain <s>Saṃbodhi</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.134 //

body.translated_text: teach the true <s>Dharma</s> and awaken all beings.

body.text: tatastān bodhitān sarvān kamena bodhisādhanaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.135 //
body.translated_text: Then, having gradually awakened them all, as a means to enlightenment, // SvayambhuP_6.135 //

children.translated_text: establishing them on the path of enlightenment, guide them for the welfare of the world.

children.text: tatasteṣāṃ samālokya cittaṃ saṃbodhi niścitaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.136 //
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that their minds are resolved upon <s>Saṃbodhi</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.136 //
teach the Three Vehicles and engage them in the ultimate truth.
Having thus accomplished the great <s>Dharma</s>, the swift means to <s>Saṃbodhi</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.137 //
endowed with auspicious glory and good qualities, you shall attain auspiciousness for the world.
Thereby, with a swiftly purified self, having attained the state of a <s>Sambuddha</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.138 //
having made the world into <s>Dharma</s>, you shall reach the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: iti bhadravrataṃ dhṛtvā gatvā tvaṃ svāśrame punaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.139 //
children.translated_text: Thus, holding the auspicious vow, returning to your own hermitage, // SvayambhuP_6.139 //
expounding the <s>Nāmasaṅgīti</s> (Chanting of Names), spread the true <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: ahamapi mahāsattva śrotuṃ tvad dharmmadeśanāṃ // SvayambhuP_6.140 //
children.translated_text: I too, O great being, to hear your teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.140 //
and to see your <s>Saṅgha</s> (community), shall come to your hermitage."

children.text: iti śāstā samādiṣṭaṃ niśaṃmya sa mahāmatiḥ // SvayambhuP_6.141 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction given by the Teacher, that one of great wisdom, // SvayambhuP_6.141 //
<s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, looking at that <s>Guru</s>, spoke thus:

children.text: maharddhiko bhagavāñchāsta vijñāsya te kathaṃ mayā // SvayambhuP_6.142 //
children.translated_text: "O mighty Lord Teacher, how shall I recognize you? // SvayambhuP_6.142 //
Please establish a sign and come here accordingly."

children.text: iti tenoditaṃ śrutvā mañjudevaḥ sa sanmati // SvayambhuP_6.143 //
children.translated_text: Having heard what was spoken by him, <s>Mañjudeva</s>, of true wisdom, // SvayambhuP_6.143 //
looking at <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, spoke again thus:

children.text: vatsāhamutpalaṃ dhṛtvā samāyāsyāmi te sabhāṃ // SvayambhuP_6.144 //
children.translated_text: "Dear child, I shall hold a blue lotus (<s>utpala</s>) and come to your assembly. // SvayambhuP_6.144 //

children.text: tena cihnena māṃ yāta saṃjānīṣva samāgataṃ /
children.translated_text: By that sign, know me as having arrived.

children.text: iti satyaṃ samādhāya dhṛtvānuśāsanaṃ mama // SvayambhuP_6.145 //
children.translated_text: Thus, establishing this truth, holding my teaching, // SvayambhuP_6.145 //
proceed to teach the true <s>Dharma</s>; may auspiciousness be yours."

children.text: iti śāstā samādiṣṭaṃ śrutvā sa yatirutsukaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.146 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction by the Teacher, that eager ascetic, // SvayambhuP_6.146 //
looking at that Teacher, bowing, spoke thus:
