"May the Lord Teacher be gracious; may you forgive my offenses. // SvayambhuP_6.147 //
By your grace, all my aspirations are accomplished.

children.text: tadanuśāsanaṃ dhṛtvā bhavatāṃ tatra jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_6.148 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, holding your teaching, for the welfare of the world there, // SvayambhuP_6.148 //
I now proceed to expound the <s>Nāmasaṅgīti</s>, O <s>Guru</s>."

children.text: iti saṃprārthya dharmmaśrī mitra saḥ saṃprāsāditaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.149 //
children.translated_text: Having thus entreated, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, having been blessed, // SvayambhuP_6.149 //
bowing at the lotus feet of that Teacher, set forth from there.
And bowing at the lotus feet of the female preceptors also, <s>Mokṣadā</s> and <s>Varadā</s> by name, // SvayambhuP_6.150 //
he set forth, delighted.

children.text: tataḥ sa sanmati dharmmaśrīmitraḥ sahasāvrajan // SvayambhuP_6.151 //
children.translated_text: Then that one of true wisdom, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, traveling swiftly, // SvayambhuP_6.151 //
quickly reaching his own hermitage, entered the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery).

children.text: tatra taṃ yatimāyātaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve 'pi sāṃghikāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.152 //
children.translated_text: There, seeing that ascetic arrived, all the members of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.152 //
bowing and asking after his welfare, led him into their dwelling.
Then, on the following day, having convened all the <s>Saṅghas</s>, that one of true wisdom, // SvayambhuP_6.153 //
took the assembly seat to expound the <s>Nāmasaṅgīti</s>.

children.text: taṃ sabhāsanamāsīnaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve 'pi sāṃdhikāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.154 //
children.translated_text: Seeing him seated in the assembly, all the members of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.154 //
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, kings, and others—all the people assembled.

children.text: tatra sarve 'pi te lokāḥ praṇatvā taṃ yati kramāt // SvayambhuP_6.155 //
children.translated_text: There, all those people, having bowed to that ascetic in order, // SvayambhuP_6.155 //
having circumambulated and placed him before them, attended on all sides.

children.text: tān sarvānsamupāsīnān dṛṣṭvā sa yatirātmavit // SvayambhuP_6.156 //
children.translated_text: Seeing all those assembled, that self-knowing ascetic, // SvayambhuP_6.156 //
expounding the <s>Nāmasaṅgīti</s>, he taught the purification.

children.text: tadā tatra manastasya jijñāsituṃ sa mañjuvāk // SvayambhuP_6.157 //
children.translated_text: Then, there, to test his mind, the eloquent <s>Mañjuvāk</s> (Mañjuśrī), // SvayambhuP_6.157 //
holding a lotus, with a deformed body, approached as a beggar.

children.text: tatra sa makṣikān kāye utpalena nivārayan // SvayambhuP_6.158 //
children.translated_text: There, waving away flies from his body with the lotus, // SvayambhuP_6.158 //
having arrived, he sat down at one side of the assembly, watching the people.

children.text: samāśritaṃ sa dharmmaśrīmitro dṛṣṭvātmanā guruṃ // SvayambhuP_6.159 //
children.translated_text: Having seen him seated, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s> recognized his <s>Guru</s> // SvayambhuP_6.159 //
by the lotus, and reflected in his mind thus:

children.text: aho nūnamayaṃ śāstā mano jijñāsituṃ mama // SvayambhuP_6.160 //
children.translated_text: "Ah, surely this is the Teacher, come here to test my mind, // SvayambhuP_6.160 //
holding a lotus in a wretched, unfortunate form.

children.text: tatkathamahamutthāya pratyuṅgamya na meya hi // SvayambhuP_6.161 //
children.translated_text: How then can I rise and go to meet him? Yet this should not be; // SvayambhuP_6.161 //
but then again, seeing him, how can I not pay homage to the <s>Guru</s>?
If I rise here and do not respectfully go to meet him, // SvayambhuP_6.162 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lokā ime māṃ dhikkuryuḥ sarve vicārataḥ /
children.translated_text: seeing this, all these people would censure me upon reflection.

children.text: ete na jñāyate yaṃ hi mañjuśrī ṛddhimānapi // SvayambhuP_6.163 //
children.translated_text: They do not know that this one is <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, possessing supernatural power; // SvayambhuP_6.163 //

children.text: īdṛgevāsya śāstā yaṃ miti me syād vihāsyatāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Is this what his teacher looks like?'—thus I would become an object of ridicule.

children.text: iti dhyātvā sa dharmmaśrīmitro lajjābhimohitaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.164 //
children.translated_text: Thus reflecting, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, overcome by shame and delusion, // SvayambhuP_6.164 //
having bowed mentally, he did not honor the Teacher outwardly.

children.text: tataḥ sa vimukhī bhūya paśyannapya vibhāvitaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.165 //
children.translated_text: Then, having turned away, though seeing him, he remained unrecognizing, // SvayambhuP_6.165 //
as if not knowing or not seeing, he taught only a fragment.

children.text: tataḥ sarve 'pi te lokāḥ śrutvā tatsaddharmmadeśanāṃ // SvayambhuP_6.166 //
children.translated_text: Then, all those people, having heard that teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.166 //
rising and bowing to that ascetic, went to their own homes.

children.text: tata loke gate dharmmaśrī mitraḥ sa samutthitaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.167 //
children.translated_text: Then, when the people had gone, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, having risen, // SvayambhuP_6.167 //
seeing that Teacher, approached to pay homage.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mañjudevo 'sau vandituṃ samupāgataṃ // SvayambhuP_6.168 //
children.translated_text: Seeing him approaching to pay homage, that <s>Mañjudeva</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.168 //
turning away, not looking, then set out and departed.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vimukhī bhūta dharmmaśrī mitra ātmanaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.169 //
children.translated_text: Seeing him turn away, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, remembering within himself // SvayambhuP_6.169 //
the great sin of his offense, fell to the ground.

children.text: nipatantaṃ tamālokya mañjuśrīḥ sa kṛpānidhiḥ // SvayambhuP_6.170 //
children.translated_text: Seeing him falling, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that treasure of compassion, // SvayambhuP_6.170 //
quickly catching him by the hand, raised him up and proceeded.

children.text: tatra sa utthito dharmmaśrī mitrastaṃ mahāmatiṃ // SvayambhuP_6.171 //
children.translated_text: There, having risen, <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, seeing that one of great wisdom // SvayambhuP_6.171 //
walking away, bowed and then spoke falsely:

children.text: bhagavanna mayā dṛṣṭo bhavānatra samāgataḥ // SvayambhuP_6.172 //
children.translated_text: "Lord, I did not see you when you arrived here. // SvayambhuP_6.172 //
Only afterwards, by the sign of the lotus, did I recognize your presence."

children.text: ityuktvā sa mṛṣāvādaṃ sāñjalistasya saṅguroḥ // SvayambhuP_6.173 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken this falsehood, with palms joined, at the lotus feet of that true <s>Guru</s>, // SvayambhuP_6.173 //
<s>Mañjudeva</s>, he bowed down, weeping again.

children.text: tatra tasya mṛṣā vaktuṃ rubhe 'pi nayane mukhāt // SvayambhuP_6.174 //
children.translated_text: Then, for speaking that falsehood, both his eyes fell from his face // SvayambhuP_6.174 //
at the tips of the lotus feet of the Teacher, onto the ground.
Then that fallen <s>Dharmaśrīmitra</s>, with a shattered mind, // SvayambhuP_6.175 //
having wept for a long time, rising, spoke to the Teacher thus:
"Lord, the offense that was committed by me through ignorance against the <s>Guru</s>— // SvayambhuP_6.176 //
May the teacher be pleased to forgive one of wicked mind."

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ tena mañjuśrīḥ sa kṛpānidhiḥ // SvayambhuP_6.177 //
children.translated_text: Thus entreated by him, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that treasure of compassion,
looking at that blind one with a compassionate gaze, spoke thus:

children.text: yadabhilajjayā karmma jñātvāpi duṣkṛtaṃ tvayā // SvayambhuP_6.178 //
children.translated_text: "The wicked deed that you did shamelessly, even knowing it—
having obtained this fruit of that, the consequence is indeed experienced.

children.text: tathāpi jñāna dṛṣṭvā tvaṃ sampaśya ddṛṣṭimān yathā // SvayambhuP_6.179 //
children.translated_text: Even so, with the eye of knowledge, see now as one who possesses sight.

children.text: jñānaṃ hi te 'sti yattena jñānaśrī mitra ucyase /
children.translated_text: You have knowledge indeed, and therefore you are called <s>Jñānaśrīmitra</s> (Friend of the Glory of Knowledge)."

children.text: ityuktyaiva sa mañjuśrīḥ kṣaṇādantarhita stataḥ // SvayambhuP_6.180 //
children.translated_text: Having said just this, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> instantly vanished from there,
and going through the sky like a bird, returned to his own hermitage.
Here, the entire account, in the presence of his two wives,
having narrated, that <s>Mañjuśrī</s> remained, bearing the welfare of the world.
From then on, that <s>Jñānaśrīmitra</s>, with the eye of knowledge,
seeing and proclaiming the true <s>Dharma</s>, practiced for the welfare of the world.

children.text: tadā maitreya tenāsya dharmadhātoḥ svayaṃbhuvaḥ // SvayambhuP_6.183 //
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Maitreya</s>, through him this <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the self-existent (<s>Svayambhū</s>),
became renowned as the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> called <s>Vāgīśvara</s> (Lord of Speech).

children.text: iti matvātra ye dharmadhātu vāgīśvara narāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.184 //
children.translated_text: Thus, understanding this, those people who worship the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> <s>Vāgīśvara</s>
with faith, according to the proper rites, having taken refuge—

children.text: abhiṣekaṃ ca saṃprāpya bodhicittā samāhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.185 //
children.translated_text: and having received <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration), with minds set on <s>Bodhicitta</s>, concentrated,
those who uphold the true <s>Dharma</s> <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, <s>vidyās</s>, and <s>mantras</s>—

children.text: te sarve vimalātmānaḥ pariśuddha trimaṇḍalāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.186 //
children.translated_text: they all, pure in soul, purified in the three spheres,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,

children.text: bhadraśrī sadguṇādhārāḥ sarva vidyā vicakṣaṇāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.187 //
children.translated_text: the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, skilled in all knowledge,
possessed of supernatural power, <s>siddhi</s>, and great <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), become practitioners of auspicious conduct.

children.text: āśuḥ sambodhi saṃbhāraṃ pūrayitvā yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.188 //
children.translated_text: Swiftly, having fulfilled the accumulations for perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>) in proper order,

body.text: arhantastrividhāṃ bodhiṃ prāpya yāyu jiṃnālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_6.189 //
body.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, they go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: iti matvābhivāchanti prāptuṃ ye saugataṃ padaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus, understanding this, those who desire to attain the state of a <s>Sugata</s>—

children.text: te 'tra bauddhālaye dharmmadhātu vāgīśvare sadā // SvayambhuP_6.190 //
children.translated_text: they should always, at this Buddhist shrine, the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> <s>Vāgīśvara</s>,
having performed worship with faith, having received <s>abhiṣeka</s> with reverence,
devoted to the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s> <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, <s>vidyās</s>, and <s>mantras</s>,
having worshipped according to the proper rites, with their purpose set on perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>),

children.text: bodhicaryā vrataṃ dhṛtvā saṃcarate jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_6.192 //
children.translated_text: having taken the vow of <s>Bodhicaryā</s> (enlightened conduct), should practice for the welfare of the world.
Swiftly they become pure in soul, purified in the three spheres,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, skilled in all knowledge,
possessed of supernatural power, <s>siddhi</s>, and great <s>abhijñā</s>, practitioners of auspicious conduct.
Then, having swiftly fulfilled the accumulations for perfect enlightenment in order,

children.text: arhantamtrividhāṃ bodhiṃ prāpya yāsyatha nivṛtiṃ // SvayambhuP_6.195 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, you shall reach <s>Nirvṛti</s> (liberation)."
Having heard this instruction given by the lord of sages, those assembled in the court,

children.text: sarve tatheti vijñāya prābhyanandan pravodhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_6.196 //
children.translated_text: all, understanding 'so be it,' rejoiced and were awakened.

body.text: itiśrī svayaṃbhū dharmmadhātu vāgīśvarābhidhāna prasiddha pravartano nāma ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'The Proclamation of the Renown of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> <s>Vāgīśvara</s> of the Glorious <s>Svayambhū</s>.'
Seventh chapter, named 'The Proclamation of the Concealment of the <s>Svayambhū Dharmadhātu Vāgīśvara</s>.'

children.text: atha bhūyaḥ sa maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then again that <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of great wisdom,
with palms joined, spoke thus to the Blessed One:
"O Blessed One, when was this <s>Dharmadhātu</s> covered with stone,

children.text: kenaiva hetunā stūpaṃ ko vyadhādīṣṭikāmayaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.2 //
children.translated_text: and for what reason did someone construct a <s>stūpa</s> of bricks?
O Blessed One, looking at all the curious people,
please instruct upon the cause of this to clear their doubts."
Thus entreated by <s>Maitreya</s>, that lord of sages,
the Blessed One, looking at the great being, instructed thus:
"Listen, <s>Maitreya</s>, as to who concealed this and made it manifest;
I shall tell the reason of this for the awakening of all the people.
When the fully awakened <s>Kanakamuni</s> had passed into <s>Nirvṛti</s>,

children.text: viṃśati varṣa sāhasra nṛrṇāmāyu yadā bhavet // SvayambhuP_7.6 //
children.translated_text: and the lifespan of humans was twenty thousand years,
then arose the Blessed Teacher, the King of <s>Dharma</s>, the lord of sages,
the omniscient one, <s>Arhat</s>, of great superknowledge, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
That fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>, at the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in the monastery,
at <s>Mṛgadāva</s> (the Deer Park), the abode of the <s>Jinas</s>, dwelt together with his assembly.
At that time, I was a <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Jyotirāja</s> (King of Light),
a lay devotee (<s>upāsaka</s>) who had taken refuge in <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the teacher of the world.
When that teacher <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the lord of the entire triple realm,
sat upon the assembly seat to teach the true <s>Dharma</s>,
all the people came to drink the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>:

children.text: brahmaśakrādayo devāḥ sarve lokādhipā api // SvayambhuP_7.11 //
children.translated_text: the gods headed by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, and all the lords of the worlds,
the planets, hosts of stars, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and <s>Apsarases</s>,

children.text: siddhāsādhyāśca rudrāśca yakṣa guhyaka kinnarāḥ // SvayambhuP_7.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>,
<s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Garuḍas</s>,
sages, ascetics, <s>Tīrthikas</s> (sectarian wanderers), and <s>brahmacārins</s>,
renunciants, <s>yogins</s>, and also other lay devotees,
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, kings and sovereigns,
<s>Vaiśyas</s>, counselors, ministers, servants, and hosts of army commanders,
artisans, merchants, caravan leaders, and other great people,
townspeople, countryfolk, villagers, townsfolk, and mountain dwellers,

children.text: tathonya deśikā lokā api sarvve samāgatāḥ // SvayambhuP_7.16 //
children.translated_text: and also people from other lands—all came.
There, beholding the fully awakened one, that lord of sages,

children.text: bhagavantaṃ samālokya sarve saṃghāḥ samāyayuḥ // SvayambhuP_7.17 //
children.translated_text: the Blessed One, seated on the assembly throne, all the assemblies gathered.
All the monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>), the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, renunciants, <s>yogins</s>,
the cloth-clad ones (<s>cailakas</s>), those observing vows, and all lay devotees (<s>upāsakas</s>),
likewise all the nuns (<s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>), the cloth-clad women, the female observers of vows,
female <s>Śrāvikas</s> (female disciples), and also others came.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, sages, <s>brahmacārins</s>,
<s>Tīrthikas</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, <s>Śaivas</s>, <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jain monks), and ascetics,
and also others arrived, eager for the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: sarve 'pi te munīndra staṃ dṛṣṭvā yayau pramoditāḥ // SvayambhuP_7.21 //
children.translated_text: All of them, seeing that lord of sages, were delighted.

children.text: tatra sarve 'pi te lokāstaṃ munīndraṃ yathākramaṃ /
children.translated_text: There, all those people, in proper order, that lord of sages,
having worshipped according to the rites and bowed, took their seats in the assembly.

children.text: tatra sarve 'pi te lokāḥ parivṛtya samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: There, all those people, surrounding him on all sides,
placing that lord of sages before them, gazed at him with concentration.
Eager to drink the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, like the thirsty toward the ocean,
with palms joined and serene faces, they stood in proper order.
Seeing all those people seated, all the assemblies, the gods,
and all the lords of the worlds, the Blessed One, the <s>Jina</s>,
beginning with the Noble Truths (<s>Āryasatya</s>), the means to the knowledge of perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>),

children.text: ādi madhyānta kalyāṇaṃ saddharmma samupādiśat // SvayambhuP_7.26 //
children.translated_text: taught the true <s>Dharma</s>, excellent in the beginning, middle, and end.
Having drunk that nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, all the people were awakened,

children.text: sadā bhadrasukhaṃ prāpnu samīcchire susaṃvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_7.27 //
children.translated_text: and wishing to attain auspicious happiness always, desired the good vow (<s>saṃvara</s>).

children.text: tataḥ sarve 'pi te lokāḥ saṃbuddha guṇavāñchinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those people, desiring the qualities of the fully awakened one (<s>Sambuddha</s>),

children.text: bodhicaryā vrataṃ dhṛtvā saṃcarire sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_7.28 //
children.translated_text: having taken the vow of <s>Bodhicaryā</s>, always practiced what is auspicious.

children.text: tadā sarvāṇi kāryāṇi kṛtvā vajrī sa yogavit /
children.translated_text: At that time, having accomplished all his tasks, that <s>Vajrin</s> (holder of the <s>Vajra</s>), the knower of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: mañjudevaḥ sa bhāryānte svayaṃ nirvṛtimāyayau // SvayambhuP_7.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mañjudeva</s>, together with his wives, himself attained <s>Nirvṛti</s> (liberation).

children.text: tato gatvā mahācīne sa mañjuśrī jināśrameṃ /
children.translated_text: Then, having gone to <s>Mahācīna</s> (Great China), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, at a Buddhist monastery,
assuming his own divine form, remained together with his wives.

children.text: atra teṣāṃ śarīrāṇi śiṣyāḥ sarve 'pi pāvake /
children.translated_text: Here, their bodies—all the disciples—in the sacred fire,
having cremated according to the rites, took the bones and purified them.
Then they, having deposited those bones in a receptacle according to the proper rites,

children.text: caityaṃ kṛtvā pratisthāpya samabhyarcya sadābhajana // SvayambhuP_7.32 //
children.translated_text: having made a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), established it, and worshipped and served it always.
Those who worship this <s>caitya</s> and serve it with faith always—
they shall attain the good qualities of the true <s>Dharma</s> of that <s>Mañjudeva</s>.
Understanding this, those who desire the good qualities of the <s>Dharma</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>—

children.text: atra mañjuśrī yaścaitya sarvadā prabhajantu te // SvayambhuP_7.34 //
children.translated_text: let them always worship this <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> here.
Having heard this instruction given by the lord of sages, those assembled people,
all, hearing 'so be it,' rejoiced and were awakened.
Then the Blessed One, <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>), the lord of sages, again
looking at <s>Maitreya</s> and the assembly, instructed thus:
"Then, after a long time had passed, in the kingdom of <s>Gauḍa</s>,
there arose a king named <s>Pracaṇḍadeva</s>, glorious, born of the lineage of <s>Vajradhara</s>.

children.text: sa rājā suciraṃ rājyaṃ nītidharmmeṇa pālayan /
children.translated_text: That king, governing the kingdom for a long time with righteous policy,
directing all the people toward the auspicious <s>Dharma</s>, made them practice it.
By the power of that <s>Dharma</s>, always there, in all directions,
prosperity, auspicious celebration, and freedom from calamity prevailed.
At that time, all those people, eager for the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
practiced the <s>Dharma</s> of their lineage, devoted to charity, morality, and vows,
steadfast in truthful assemblies, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,

children.text: kuleśabhajanaṃ kṛtvā prācaranta mitho hite // SvayambhuP_7.41 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped the lord of their lineage, practiced mutual welfare.
Seeing all the people seeking auspiciousness, that sovereign king,
delighted, addressed them and looking at them, instructed thus:

children.text: bho lokāḥ paurikāḥ sarve saddharma yadi vāñchatha /
children.translated_text: 'O people, all you citizens, if you desire the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: triratna bhajanaṃ kṛtvā carata bodhisamvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_7.43 //
children.translated_text: having performed worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), practice the <s>Bodhi</s> vow (<s>saṃvara</s>).
By that, you, of auspicious souls, purified in the three spheres,
shall become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, practitioners of the <s>Bodhi</s> path.
Then, pure in soul, free from affliction, with pure senses,
as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, you shall reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.'
Hearing this instruction by the king, all the people
acknowledged 'so be it,' rejoiced, and were awakened.

children.text: tataḥ sarve 'pi te lokā dhṛtvā rājñānuśāsanaṃ /
children.translated_text: Then all those people, upholding the king's instruction,
having performed worship of the Three Jewels, practiced auspicious conduct.
Seeing all those people devoted to the vow of <s>Bodhicaryā</s>,
with a soul pleased with great joy, he again reflected:
'My life and birth are fruitful, for all these people, devoted to my governance,

children.text: sarve 'lokāḥ samādhāya pracaranti sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_7.49 //
children.translated_text: practicing with concentration, always conduct themselves in auspiciousness.'
Then that <s>Pracaṇḍadeva</s>, seeing his kingdom in great celebration,
Having seen the misery in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence), he reflected with self-awareness:
"Here I am, afflicted by the flood of existence, I shall perish with worn-out senses;
then, overcome by disease too, I shall surely go to death.
So for how long shall I remain here, accompanied by happiness?

children.text: avaśyaṃ bhāvino bhāvā bhavanti bhavacāriṇāṃ // SvayambhuP_7.52 //
children.translated_text: Inevitable are the events that befall those who wander in existence.
Always in existence, auspiciousness comes only to those who practice the true <s>Dharma</s>;
suffering alone always comes to those who follow desires in the wandering of existence.
Therefore, I shall abandon the household life (<s>gṛhāśrama</s>), the abode of desires,

children.text: nirjane vana ekākī vihareyaṃ samāhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.54 //
children.translated_text: and dwell alone in a solitary forest, with concentration.
Remembering the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>), meditating, with a disposition fixed on <s>Sambodhi</s>,
holding the vow of the conduct of <s>Bodhi</s> (<s>Bodhicaryāvrata</s>), I shall conduct myself for the welfare of the world."

children.text: iti niścitya sa prājñaḥ pracaṇḍadeva ātmavit /
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, that wise one, <s>Pracaṇḍadeva</s>, the self-knower,
summoning all the royal ministers, instructed them thus:

children.text: bho sarva mantriṇo yūyaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ me vaco hitaṃ /
children.translated_text: "O all ministers, listen to my beneficial words.
What is proclaimed by me, you should accordingly carry out.
For I am old, overtaken by age, with worn-out senses;

children.text: tathā rogābhibhūto 'pi grasiṣye mṛtyunā dhruvaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.58 //
children.translated_text: and overcome by disease too, I shall surely be swallowed by death.

children.text: iti me trasyate cittaṃ durgati bhayaśaṃkitaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus my mind trembles, apprehensive with fear of bad destinies.
Inevitable are the events that befall those who wander in existence.
In existence, auspiciousness always comes to those who practice the true <s>Dharma</s>;
suffering alone always comes to those who follow desires in the wandering of existence.
The kingdom of misfortune, the enjoyment of sense objects, terrifying, agitated with the fear of serpents—

children.text: anityamasāreti vicintya tatra āgāramadhyāvasituṃ na rocate // SvayambhuP_7.61 //
children.translated_text: reflecting that it is impermanent and without essence, it does not please me to dwell in a house.
Understanding thus, I shall abandon the household life, the abode of desires,
and I now desire to dwell in the forest hermitage (<s>vanāśrama</s>), the beautiful grove.
Therefore, I shall install my own son, <s>Śaktideva</s>, upon the royal throne,

children.text: pratiṣṭhāpya nṛpaṃ kartumicchāmi sāṃprataṃ khalu // SvayambhuP_7.63 //
children.translated_text: and I wish to make him king now indeed.

children.text: tad bhavanto niśamyātra sarve 'pi mama śāsanaṃ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, all of you, having heard my command here,

children.text: abhiṣiṃcya nṛpaṃ kṛtvā bhajatainaṃ mamātmajaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.64 //
children.translated_text: consecrate him and make him king—serve this son of mine."

children.text: ityādiṣṭaṃ narendreṇa śrutvā te mantriṇo janāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction given by the king, those ministers and people
responded thus: "The command of our lord is our authority."
Then that king, summoning his son <s>Śaktideva</s>, spoke thus:
"Division, punishment, conciliation, and gifts—these are the four means of statecraft.
Here I am, overtaken by old age, surely with conquered senses;

children.text: tadā rogābhibhūte 'pi vajreyaṃ maraṇaṃ dhuvaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.67 //
children.translated_text: then, overcome by disease too, I shall surely go to death.
Therefore I desire the forest refuge, seeking the good with praiseworthy effort.

children.text: puro mṛtyu ripuṃ hanti gṛhasaṃraktameva vā // SvayambhuP_7.68 //
children.translated_text: Before one's eyes, the enemy Death slays even one attached to the household.
Therefore, my mind, frightened by <s>saṃsāra</s>, with manifold fear and apprehension,

children.text: nātra sthātuṃ manoreme gacchāmi nirjanaṃ vanaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.69 //
children.translated_text: does not delight in staying here—I go to the solitary forest.

children.text: tasmāt mayā yathā proktaṃ tathā caritumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, as I have instructed, you should accordingly conduct yourself.

children.text: prajānāṃ pālanaṃ kṛtvā dharmanītyā samācara // SvayambhuP_7.70 //
children.translated_text: Having protected the people, govern according to the law of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: lokān mā khekha yattāpaiḥ kuladharmma samācara /
children.translated_text: Do not oppress the people with punishments; practice the hereditary <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: pareṣvapi dayāyuktairdānaṃ hi śraddhayā kuru // SvayambhuP_7.71 //
children.translated_text: And with compassion toward others, give charity with faith.
Do not commit killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and the like;

children.text: mā mṛṣāvāda paiśūnyaṃ pāruṣyaṃ saṃbhinnameva ca // SvayambhuP_7.72 //
children.translated_text: do not commit false speech, slander, harsh words, or divisive talk.
Abandon the faults of covetousness, ill-will, and wrong views.

children.text: etāni tāni sarvāṇi dhāraya dṛḍhacetasā // SvayambhuP_7.73 //
children.translated_text: Hold firmly all these precepts with a steadfast mind.

children.text: pāpānāṃ mūla eṣo hi sugateneti deśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For this is the root of sins, as taught by the <s>Sugata</s>;

children.text: itthaṃ kṛte 'pi nṛpateritayo na bhaviṣyati // SvayambhuP_7.74 //
children.translated_text: when acting thus, O King, there will be no misfortune.

children.text: tatkasmāt dharmmeṇa prāpyate rājyaṃ dharmmeṇa dhanavarddhanaṃ /
children.translated_text: For by <s>Dharma</s> is a kingdom obtained, by <s>Dharma</s> is wealth increased,

children.text: dharmmeṇa dhanasādhyante dharmmeṇa kāma sidhyate // SvayambhuP_7.75 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Dharma</s> is wealth accomplished, by <s>Dharma</s> is desire fulfilled.

children.text: kāmasidhyena mokṣaṃ ca prāpyate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the fulfillment of desire, liberation too is obtained—there is no doubt in this.

children.text: anena jñānamārgeṇa saśāsa nṛpatiḥ sutaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.76 //
children.translated_text: By this path of knowledge, the king instructed his son.
Then that father-king, having consecrated <s>Śaktideva</s>, his own son,

children.text: abhiṣiṃcya pratisthāpya nṛpāsane nṛpaṃ vyadhāt // SvayambhuP_7.77 //
children.translated_text: having installed him, established him upon the royal throne and made him king.
Like an elephant restrained by the goad of knowledge and fear,

children.text: tatra sa janakaḥ sarva putrāya sarvamarppayet // SvayambhuP_7.78 //
children.translated_text: there that father entrusted everything to his son.
Having renounced all possessions, he spoke again thus:
"From today, you are the lord and master of all the people.
The instructor of all in <s>Dharma</s>, the bearer of the welfare of all beings."

children.text: namāma pitaraṃ tena śrutvā vākyaṃ rasāniva // SvayambhuP_7.80 //
children.translated_text: The son bowed to his father, having heard those words like nectar.

children.text: dhṛtvājñāṃ te yathā tāta prajānāṃ pratipālane /
children.translated_text: "I shall uphold your command, O Father, in the protection of the people."

children.text: iti praśāśya tato bhūpaḥ pracaṇḍadeva sanmatiḥ // SvayambhuP_7.81 //
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed, then King <s>Pracaṇḍadeva</s>, of true wisdom,
having exhorted his son, wife, and others, went alone to the forest hermitage.

children.text: tṛṇāsanasa tatra sa nirjaneraṇye vivikte utajāśraye // SvayambhuP_7.82 //
children.translated_text: There, in a solitary forest, in a secluded hermitage,
seated on a grass mat, he remained absorbed in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).

children.text: tatraikaṃ viharan kaṃcitkālaṃ sa ṛṣidharmmabhṛt // SvayambhuP_7.83 //
children.translated_text: There, dwelling alone for some time, that bearer of the <s>ṛṣi</s>'s <s>dharma</s>,
eager for the welfare of all beings, reflected thus in his mind:
"What is the use of meditating alone in a solitary forest, dwelling here?
To whom shall I teach the true <s>Dharma</s>, the means to <s>Bodhi</s>,
born of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>)?
The merit proclaimed by the lords of sages for the welfare of beings—

children.text: tadevaṃ nirjjane sthitvā kiṃ me dharmārthasādhanaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.86 //
children.translated_text: what means of <s>Dharma</s> is achieved by me while staying in solitude?
Without the purpose of benefiting beings, even austerity is meaningless;
what accomplishment is achieved here even by difficult austerity,
if it is merely for the sake of gaining happiness in a good destiny?
Without the purpose of benefiting beings, the means of accomplishment is fruitless.

children.text: tadatra nirjjane sthitvā tapasā niṣphalaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: Therefore, staying here in solitude, my austerity is fruitless,
compared to the achievement of <s>Dharma</s>, glory, and good qualities for the welfare of beings.
Knowledge, accomplishment, prosperity, energy, strength, and auspiciousness—

children.text: tat mamaitāni sarvāṇi saṃsiddhi saṃmitānyapi // SvayambhuP_7.90 //
children.translated_text: all these of mine, even equal to perfection,
without the purpose of benefiting beings, are meaningless, like those of an animal.
Therefore, abandoning this difficult vow, with a mind set on <s>Bodhi</s>,
holding the vow of the conduct of <s>Bodhi</s>, I shall conduct myself for the welfare of the world.

children.text: tasmāt tīrtheṣu tīrtheṣu pīṭheṣu puṇyabhūmiṣu // SvayambhuP_7.92 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, at sacred fords (<s>tīrthas</s>) after <s>tīrthas</s>, at sacred seats (<s>pīṭhas</s>), in holy lands,
teaching the true <s>Dharma</s> to beings, I shall wander forth."
"By this merit, purified in soul, purified in the three spheres,
swiftly attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, may I reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>."

children.text: iti niścitya sa prājñaḥ pracaṇḍadeva utthitaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.94 //
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, that wise <s>Pracaṇḍadeva</s> arose,
and then, for the welfare of beings, he set forth with concentration.

children.text: evaṃ saḥ pracaran dharmmamupadeśya samantataḥ // SvayambhuP_7.95 //
children.translated_text: Thus, wandering and teaching <s>Dharma</s> on all sides,
at sacred fields, <s>tīrthas</s>, and <s>pīṭhas</s>, he traveled with joy.

children.text: evaṃ bhraman sa sarvatra bhūtaleṣu yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.96 //
children.translated_text: Thus wandering everywhere on the surface of the earth, in due order,
gradually journeying, he arrived here at the <s>Himālaya</s>.

children.text: atrāyātaḥ sa saṃvikṣya sarvatra saṃpramoditaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.97 //
children.translated_text: Having arrived here and surveyed everything, he was greatly delighted:
"Oh! This is indeed a great sacred seat (<s>mahāpīṭha</s>)!" — so he spoke and rejoiced.

children.text: tataḥ sa idamālokya dharmmadhātuṃ jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.98 //
children.translated_text: Then, beholding this <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
in the form of light, with a serene soul, having bowed, he came here.

children.text: atra sa samupāgatya saṃmikṣyenaṃ jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.99 //
children.translated_text: Having approached here and beheld this abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
having worshipped according to the prescribed method, with faith, devotion, and a clear mind,
having performed many circumambulations, having praised with charming hymns,

children.text: aṣṭāṃgai praṇatiṃ kṛtvā dhyātvā japtvā bhajan mudā /
children.translated_text: having made prostration with the eight limbs (<s>aṣṭāṅga</s>), meditating, reciting, worshipping with joy.

children.text: tataścedaṃ sa saṃvīkṣya mañjudevasya nirmmitaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.101 //
children.translated_text: Then, beholding this creation of <s>Mañjudeva</s>,
having worshipped the <s>caitya</s>, praised it, sung hymns, bowed, and worshipped with joy.

children.text: tato 'sau ca mahādevī yonirūpāṃ khagānanāṃ // SvayambhuP_7.102 //
children.translated_text: Then, that great goddess in the form of the womb (<s>yoni</s>), bird-faced—
beholding her with a serene soul, he worshipped according to the prescribed method.

children.text: tatrāpi sa mahāsattva stutvā gītairmanoharaiḥ // SvayambhuP_7.103 //
children.translated_text: There too, that great being, having praised with charming hymns,
having made prostration with the eight limbs, circumambulated many times.

children.text: śraddhayā śaraṇaṃ gatvā smṛtvā dhyātvā samāhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.104 //
children.translated_text: Having gone to her as refuge with faith, remembering, meditating with concentration,
having recited her <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and <s>mantra</s>, he rejoiced.
Then that great being, beholding the <s>Vāgmatī</s> and the other
sacred fords, all of them, he rejoiced.

children.text: tata sa teṣu tīrtheṣu sarveṣvapi yathākramaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.106 //
children.translated_text: Then, at all those sacred fords, in due order,
having bathed, performed charity, vows, and the rest, he worshipped with delight.

children.text: tato 'ṣṭau vītarāgāṃśca dṛṣṭvā sa saṃpraharṣitaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.107 //
children.translated_text: Then, having seen the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> (passionless ones), he was greatly elated;

children.text: yathāvidhi samabhyarcya stutvā natvā bhajan kramāt /
children.translated_text: having worshipped according to the prescribed method, praised, bowed, and worshipped in order.

children.text: tataḥ pracaṇḍadevaḥ sa bodhisattvaḥ prasāditaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.108 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pracaṇḍadeva</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being pleased,
desired to remain here always, practicing his vow.

children.text: tataḥ sa vimalālokya himālaye samantataḥ // SvayambhuP_7.109 //
children.translated_text: Then he, beholding the pure <s>Himālaya</s> on all sides,
having enjoyed the supreme bliss of the true <s>Dharma</s>, desired the excellent cessation.

children.text: tataḥ sa mañjudevasya śiṣyaṃ śāsana sambhṛtaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.110 //
children.translated_text: Then he, approaching a disciple of <s>Mañjudeva</s>, one nurtured by the teaching,
a true <s>guru</s>, with humility requested thus:
"Venerable one, at this meritorious field, the great seat of the <s>Himālaya</s>,
I desire to hold the <s>pravrajyā saṃvara</s> (ordination vow) and remain here always.

children.text: tad bhavān kṛpayā mahayaṃ saṃbodhijñānasādhanaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.112 //
children.translated_text: May you, out of compassion, deign to bestow upon me
the <s>pravrajyā saṃvara</s>, the means to the knowledge of perfect awakening, for the welfare of the world."

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ tena niśamya sa guṇākaraḥ // SvayambhuP_7.113 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this request, that mine of good qualities,
looking upon that wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>, spoke thus:

children.text: ehi bhadra samīcchā te yadyasti bauddhasambare // SvayambhuP_7.114 //
children.translated_text: "Come, good one, if your wish exists for the Buddhist ordination vow (<s>Bauddha saṃvara</s>),
having taken the vow of renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>), wander forth with concentration."

children.text: ityuktvā sa mahābhijñaḥ pravrajitaṃ vidhāya taṃ // SvayambhuP_7.115 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that one of great supernatural knowledge, having performed his ordination,
having given him the vow of the conduct of <s>Bodhi</s>, set him forth for the welfare of the world.

children.text: tatra sa muṇḍitapātrī surakta cīvarāvṛtaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.116 //
children.translated_text: There he, shaven-headed, bearing a bowl, wrapped in a beautifully dyed robe,

body.translated_text: a celibate, an ascetic, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), free from afflictions, an <s>Arhat</s>, became one of great steadfastness.

children.translated_text: His name became <s>Śāntaśrī Bhikṣu</s> (the Monk of Peaceful Glory).

children.text: tataḥ sa sarvavicchāstā bodhisattvā hitārthadik // SvayambhuP_7.117 //
children.translated_text: Then he, the teacher of all knowledge, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, indicator of the path of welfare,
became venerable and worshipped even by the worlds of gods and <s>Asuras</s>.
From that time, <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, at the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
having performed worship of the Three Jewels, remained practicing the vow of <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: sa ekasmin dine cemaṃ jyotīrūpaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_7.119 //
children.translated_text: One day, seeing this form of light, radiant,
seated upon a jeweled lotus throne, he reflected thus:

children.text: aho hyayaṃ svayaṃ jāto jyotirūpo prabhāsvaraḥ // SvayambhuP_7.120 //
children.translated_text: Ah! This self-arisen one, in the form of light, resplendent, // SvayambhuP_7.120 //
seated upon a jewel-lotus throne, stands for the welfare of the world.
How long will this glorious <s>Dharmadhātu</s> <s>Jina</s> shrine // SvayambhuP_7.121 //
thus stand illuminating beings for the welfare of the world?

children.text: yataḥ kalau samayā te loka pañcakaṣāyite // SvayambhuP_7.122 //
children.translated_text: For in the <s>Kali</s> age, when the world is afflicted by the five corruptions, // SvayambhuP_7.122 //
all beings will become of wicked conduct and evil disposition,
intoxicated with pride, corrupt, greedy, acting according to desire, // SvayambhuP_7.123 //
envious, heedless, with minds agitated by jealousy,
blinded by the arrogance of afflictions and ego, without discrimination, negligent, // SvayambhuP_7.124 //
excessively attached to sensual pleasures, practitioners of the ten unwholesome deeds.

children.text: tadā kathamayaṃ śrīmān jyotīrūpaḥ prabhāsvaraḥ // SvayambhuP_7.125 //
children.translated_text: Then how will this glorious one, in the form of light, resplendent, // SvayambhuP_7.125 //
seated upon the jewel-lotus throne, remain for the welfare of the world?

children.text: nūnaṃ ye lobhino duṣṭāḥ kleśavyākulamānasāḥ // SvayambhuP_7.126 //
children.translated_text: Surely, those who are greedy, corrupt, with minds agitated by afflictions, // SvayambhuP_7.126 //

children.text: imaṃ caityaṃ pratikṣipya ratnāni saṃharet tadā /
children.translated_text: rejecting this <s>caitya</s>, will carry away its jewels.

children.text: duṣṭā ca tathānye 'pi duṣṭāḥ kleśābhimāninaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.127 //
children.translated_text: Those corrupt ones, and likewise others too, corrupt and proud of their afflictions, // SvayambhuP_7.127 //
will destroy this <s>caitya</s> in the form of light completely.

children.text: evaṃ tadā kalau kāle dhvaṃsite 'smin jinālaye // SvayambhuP_7.128 //
children.translated_text: Thus, at that time in the <s>Kali</s> age, when this <s>Jina</s> shrine is destroyed, // SvayambhuP_7.128 //
a great calamity born of great sin will surely occur.
Therefore, for the protection of this <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.129 //
I shall create a safeguard by covering it with stone, making a lofty <s>caitya</s>.

children.text: tadā sarve 'pi lokāste imaṃ stūpaṃ mahochritaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.130 //
children.translated_text: Then all those beings, seeing this lofty <s>stūpa</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.130 //
with faith and devotion, pleased, will worship it.
And by the power of that merit, always here and everywhere, // SvayambhuP_7.131 //
there will surely be abundance, auspicious celebration, and freedom from calamity.'

children.text: iti dhyātvā sa śāntaśrīḥ śāstāraṃ taṃ punarmudā // SvayambhuP_7.132 //
children.translated_text: Having thus reflected, <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, approaching the Teacher again joyfully, // SvayambhuP_7.132 //
bowing with joined palms, entreated him thus with devotion:
"Venerable one, O true <s>Guru</s>, O Teacher, I now wish here // SvayambhuP_7.133 //
to safeguard this <s>Dharmadhātu caitya</s> for its protection.
Covering it above with stone, with bricks raised high, // SvayambhuP_7.134 //
I am eager to make a <s>stūpa</s>, establish it, and make it enduring.

children.text: ityatra me bhavāñchāstā gupti kṛtvābhirakṣaṇe // SvayambhuP_7.135 //
children.translated_text: In this matter, may you, O Teacher, having made a safeguard for its protection, // SvayambhuP_7.135 //
deign to grant permission regarding the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the sustainer of the world."

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tena śāntaśriyā niśamya saḥ // SvayambhuP_7.136 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this entreaty by <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.136 //
that one of great wisdom, looking at that great being, spoke thus:
"O good one, if you wish to create a safeguard for this <s>Svayambhū</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.137 //

children.text: pratyekaṃ śrāvakaṃ yānaṃ muktvā mahati saṃśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: abandoning the vehicles of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> and the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, take refuge in the Great Vehicle (<s>Mahāyāna</s>).
Having received the <s>Vajrābhiṣeka</s> (diamond consecration), practice the <s>Vajra</s> vow again. // SvayambhuP_7.138 //
Then, having conquered the <s>Māras</s> and propitiated the Lord of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: saṃprārthya śilayācchādya kuru stūpaṃ samuchritaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.139 //
children.translated_text: having entreated, cover it with stone and make a lofty <s>stūpa</s>." // SvayambhuP_7.139 //

children.text: iti śāstā samādiṣṭaṃ niśamya sa pramoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction of the Teacher, he was delighted,

children.text: śāstāraṃ taṃ praṇatvā ca prārthayadevamādarāt // SvayambhuP_7.140 //
children.translated_text: and bowing to that Teacher, entreated him thus with devotion: // SvayambhuP_7.140 //
"May you, my true <s>Guru</s>, O Teacher, for the protection of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,

children.text: vajracaryāvrataṃ datvā cāraya māṃ jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_7.141 //
children.translated_text: having bestowed the <s>Vajracaryā</s> (diamond practice) vow, set me upon the path for the welfare of the world." // SvayambhuP_7.141 //

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tena śāntaśriyā niśamya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this entreaty by <s>Śāntaśrī</s>,
that one of great wisdom, looking at that great being, spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_7.142 //

children.text: yadi śraddhāsti te bhadra vajracaryā mahāvrataṃ /
children.translated_text: "If you have faith, O good one, in the great vow of the <s>Vajracaryā</s> (diamond practice),

children.text: yathāvidhi pradāsyāmi tad gṛhāṇa jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_7.143 //
children.translated_text: I shall bestow it according to the prescribed method; receive it for the welfare of the world." // SvayambhuP_7.143 //
Having said this, that great teacher gave to <s>Śāntaśrī</s> in due order
the <s>Vajracaryā</s> vow in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, together with the consecration. // SvayambhuP_7.144 //
<s>Śāntaśrī</s> was established as a <s>Vajrācārya</s> (diamond master), and at that moment, in the noble tradition, he attained supernatural knowledge.

children.text: tataḥ prāptābhiṣekaḥ sa śāntaśrī vajrayogavit // SvayambhuP_7.145 //
children.translated_text: Then, having received the consecration, <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, the knower of <s>Vajra</s>-yoga, // SvayambhuP_7.145 //

children.text: sa svātmā dakṣiṇāṃ tasmai gurave pradadau mudā /
children.translated_text: joyfully offered his own self as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual offering) to that <s>Guru</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sa vajradhṛg yogī mahābhijñaḥ susiddhimān // SvayambhuP_7.146 //
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Vajra</s>-bearing <s>Yogin</s>, of great supernatural knowledge, well-accomplished, // SvayambhuP_7.146 //
having propitiated his clan-lord, worshipped joyfully together with his retinue.

children.text: tataḥ sa vajradhṛg yogī mahābhijñaḥ susiddhimān // SvayambhuP_7.147 //
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Vajra</s>-bearing <s>Yogin</s>, of great supernatural knowledge, well-accomplished, // SvayambhuP_7.147 //
eager in the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>, became the lord of all knowledge.

children.text: tataḥ sāsturanujñāṃ sa samāsādya prasāditaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.148 //
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained the Teacher's permission, pleased, // SvayambhuP_7.148 //
having propitiated the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, he entreated thus with reverence:

children.text: bhagavan nātha sarvajña bhavatāṃ rakṣaṇāya yat // SvayambhuP_7.149 //
children.translated_text: "O Blessed One, O Protector, O Omniscient One, for your protection, // SvayambhuP_7.149 //
I am eager to cover the form of light and make a <s>caitya</s> here.

children.text: tad bhavān trijagannātha kṛpayā me prasīdatu // SvayambhuP_7.150 //
children.translated_text: May you, O Lord of the Three Worlds, be gracious to me with compassion. // SvayambhuP_7.150 //
And if there be any fault on my part in this, may you deign to forgive all of it."

children.text: iti saṃprārthya sa prājña jyotīrūpaṃ jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.151 //
children.translated_text: Having thus entreated, that wise one covered the <s>Jina</s> shrine in the form of light // SvayambhuP_7.151 //
together with the jewel-lotus, concealing it with stone.
Above that, with bricks, fashioning a lofty <s>caitya</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.152 //
having established it according to the prescribed method, he worshipped it always with great celebration.

children.text: tata idañca pucchāgraṃ mañjudevasya nirmmitaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.153 //
children.translated_text: Then this <s>caitya</s> at the tail-point, created by <s>Mañjudeva</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.153 //
he also covered with stone and made an excellent <s>stūpa</s>.

children.text: idaṃ stūpaṃ ca sa śāntaśrīḥ pratiṣṭhāpya yathāvidhi // SvayambhuP_7.154 //
children.translated_text: This <s>stūpa</s>, <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, having established according to the prescribed method, // SvayambhuP_7.154 //
always with faith and devotion, worshipped joyfully with great celebration.
Then that great teacher, having propitiated the five deities, // SvayambhuP_7.155 //
established them with their retinues in the five cities and always worshipped them.

children.text: tad yathā devatā pañca prathamaṃ vāyudevatā // SvayambhuP_7.156 //
children.translated_text: The five deities are thus: the first is the deity of Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>), // SvayambhuP_7.156 //
established in <s>Vāyupura</s> (Wind City); in <s>Vahnipura</s> (Fire City), the deity of Fire (<s>Agni</s>);

children.text: nāgapure ca nāgendro vasupure vasundharāṃ // SvayambhuP_7.157 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Nāgapura</s> (Serpent City), the lord of <s>Nāgas</s>; in <s>Vasupura</s> (Wealth City), <s>Vasundharā</s> (Earth Goddess); // SvayambhuP_7.157 //
in <s>Śāntipura</s> (Peace City), the glorious <s>Saṃvara</s> together with his retinue.

children.text: etān sarvān samārādhya sa ācārya yathāvidhi // SvayambhuP_7.158 //
children.translated_text: Having propitiated all of these, that teacher, according to the prescribed method, // SvayambhuP_7.158 //
having worshipped with great celebration, always worshipped them joyfully.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā sa ācārya śāntaśrīḥ kṛtakṛtyau maharddhikaḥ // SvayambhuP_7.159 //
children.translated_text: Having done thus, that teacher <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, his purpose fulfilled, of great supernatural power, // SvayambhuP_7.159 //
perfected in the auspicious <s>mantra</s>, became the lord of all knowledge.

children.text: tato bhūyaḥ sa ācāryo bodhisattvā mahāmatiḥ // SvayambhuP_7.160 //
children.translated_text: Then again that teacher, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of great wisdom, // SvayambhuP_7.160 //
eager for the welfare of all beings, meditating, reflected thus:
"Here, having propitiated all the gods according to the prescribed method, // SvayambhuP_7.161 //
having established and worshipped them, I worship joyfully with great celebration.
And likewise here, always, the <s>Dharmadhātu Vāgīśvara</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.162 //
remembering, meditating upon, and propitiating him, I shall remain for the welfare of the world."
Having thus reflected, <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, the teacher, bearing the threefold purpose, // SvayambhuP_7.163 //
for the welfare of all beings, remained there delighted.

children.text: evaṃ tā devatā bhaktyā bhajanti ye yathāvidhi // SvayambhuP_7.164 //
children.translated_text: Thus, those who worship those deities with devotion according to the prescribed method, // SvayambhuP_7.164 //
endowed with the qualities of auspicious glory, shall become practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: tad viśeṣaphalaṃ cāpi śṛṇu maitreya sāṃprataṃ // SvayambhuP_7.165 //
children.translated_text: "Now hear also the special fruit of that, O <s>Maitreya</s>. // SvayambhuP_7.165 //
For the enlightenment of all beings, I shall declare it here in brief.

children.text: tadyathā ye samārādhya sagaṇāṃ vāyudevatāṃ // SvayambhuP_7.166 //
children.translated_text: Those who, having propitiated the deity of Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>) together with its retinue, // SvayambhuP_7.166 //
worshipping according to the prescribed method, worship with devotion —

children.text: teṣāṃ vātamahotpātabhayaṃ kvāpi na vidyate // SvayambhuP_7.167 //
children.translated_text: for them, fear of great calamity from storms is nowhere found. // SvayambhuP_7.167 //
Health, endowment with <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), and desirable enjoyments shall always be theirs.

children.text: ye cāpyevaṃ samārādhya sagaṇāṃ vahnidevatāṃ // SvayambhuP_7.168 //
children.translated_text: And those who, having propitiated the deity of Fire (<s>Agni</s>) together with its retinue, // SvayambhuP_7.168 //
worshipping according to the prescribed method, worship with devotion —

children.text: teṣāṃ vahnimahotpātaṃ bhayaṃ kvāpi na vidyate // SvayambhuP_7.169 //
children.translated_text: for them, fear of great calamity from fire is nowhere found. // SvayambhuP_7.169 //
Nourished senses, health, and great happiness shall always be theirs.

children.text: ye cāpyevaṃ samārādhya sagaṇāṃ nāgadevatāṃ // SvayambhuP_7.170 //
children.translated_text: And those who, having propitiated the <s>Nāga</s> deity together with its retinue, // SvayambhuP_7.170 //
worshipping according to the prescribed method, always worship joyfully —

children.text: teṣāṃ na vidyate kvāpi durbhikṣotpātajaṃ bhayaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.171 //
children.translated_text: for them, fear of calamity arising from famine is nowhere found. // SvayambhuP_7.171 //
Wealth of auspicious jewels, and desirable enjoyments shall always be theirs.

children.text: ye cāpyevaṃ samārādhya sagaṇāṃ śrībasundharāṃ // SvayambhuP_7.172 //
children.translated_text: And those who, having propitiated the glorious <s>Vasundharā</s> (Earth Goddess) together with her retinue, // SvayambhuP_7.172 //
worshipping according to the prescribed method, worship with devotion —

children.text: teṣāṃ dāridrayaduḥkhādi bhayaṃ nāsti kadācana // SvayambhuP_7.173 //
children.translated_text: for them, fear of the suffering of poverty and such is never found. // SvayambhuP_7.173 //
Endowed with the good qualities of auspicious glory, great prosperity and happiness shall always be theirs.

children.text: ye cāpyevaṃ samārādhya sagaṇaṃ sambaraṃ jinaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.174 //
children.translated_text: And those who, having propitiated <s>Saṃvara</s>, the <s>Jina</s>, together with his retinue, // SvayambhuP_7.174 //
worshipping according to the prescribed method, always worship with devotion —

children.text: teṣāṃ mārāpasargga ca bhayaṃ kvāpi na vidyate // SvayambhuP_7.175 //
children.translated_text: for them, fear of the assaults of <s>Māra</s> is nowhere found. // SvayambhuP_7.175 //
Wealth of the jewel of the true <s>Dharma</s>, great sovereignty, and happiness shall always be theirs.

children.text: ye cedaṃ caityamārādhya mañjudevasya nirmmitaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.176 //
children.translated_text: Those who, having propitiated this <s>caitya</s> created by <s>Mañjudeva</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.176 //
worshipping according to the prescribed method, worship with devotion —

children.text: taddurbhbhagā durācārā duṣṭā syurna kadācana // SvayambhuP_7.177 //
children.translated_text: they shall never be unfortunate, of wicked conduct, or corrupt. // SvayambhuP_7.177 //
All shall become lords of <s>Dharma</s>, protectors, mines of glorious qualities.

children.text: ye cāpīdaṃ samārādhya dharmmadhātuṃ jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.178 //
children.translated_text: And those who, having propitiated this <s>Dharmadhātu Jina</s> shrine, // SvayambhuP_7.178 //
worshipping according to the prescribed method, worship with devotion —
all of them, of pure souls, endowed with the refuge of auspicious glory and good qualities, // SvayambhuP_7.179 //
shall become <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great supernatural knowledge, practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: ya etā devatāḥ sarvāḥ smṛtvā dhyātvāpi sarvadā // SvayambhuP_7.180 //
children.translated_text: Those who always remember and meditate upon all these deities, // SvayambhuP_7.180 //
and even uttering their names, worship with devotion —

children.text: te 'pi sarve na yāsyanti durggatiṃ ca kadācana // SvayambhuP_7.181 //
children.translated_text: they too shall never go to bad destinies. // SvayambhuP_7.181 //
Always born in good destinies, they shall become repositories of glorious qualities.
Then they, devoted to meritorious deeds, eager for the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>, // SvayambhuP_7.182 //
having taken refuge in the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), shall always conduct themselves in auspiciousness.
Then they, of pure souls, with purified senses and dispositions, // SvayambhuP_7.183 //
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, dwelling in the four <s>Brahma-vihāras</s>,
shall practice the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s> (Bodhisattva vow), bearing the welfare of all beings. // SvayambhuP_7.184 //
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulation for <s>Bodhi</s> in due order,
becoming lords of the ten <s>Bhūmis</s> (stages), shall become protectors, sons of the <s>Sugata</s>. // SvayambhuP_7.185 //
Then they, of pure souls, free from desire for the courses of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: arhantaḥ savala māraṃ nirjitya syurniraṃjanāḥ // SvayambhuP_7.186 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, having conquered <s>Māra</s> with his forces, shall become unstained. // SvayambhuP_7.186 //
Having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, luminaries of the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
for the welfare of all beings, they shall attain the state of a <s>Sambuddha</s>. // SvayambhuP_7.187 //
Those who, having heard of this greatness of qualities, greatly rejoice,
and likewise praise the greatness of that merit with devotion — // SvayambhuP_7.188 //
they too, all freed from blemish, purified in the three spheres,
glorious, endowed with good qualities, shall become of minds set on <s>Bodhi</s>. // SvayambhuP_7.189 //
they would never go to evil destinies, always born in good destinies;
having worked for the welfare of all beings, they would act for the welfare of the world. // SvayambhuP_7.190 //
Then they would become lords of all, fulfilling the goals of <s>Dharma</s> and wealth;
having fulfilled the accumulation for <s>Bodhi</s>, they would attain the state of a <s>Sambuddha</s>. // SvayambhuP_7.191 //

children.text: iti satyaṃ parijñāya bauddhaṃ padaṃ yadīcchatha /
children.translated_text: Thus, knowing this truth, if you desire the state of a <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: etān devān samārādhya bhajadhvaṃ sarvadā bhave // SvayambhuP_7.192 //
children.translated_text: having propitiated these deities, worship them always in existence. // SvayambhuP_7.192 //
By the power of this merit, you too shall become thus;

children.text: durggatiṃ naiva yāyāta kadācin kutracid dhruvaṃ // SvayambhuP_7.193 //
children.translated_text: you shall never go to evil destinies, anywhere, assuredly. // SvayambhuP_7.193 //
Always born in good destinies, abodes of auspicious glory and good qualities,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, you shall become practitioners of <s>Bodhi</s>. // SvayambhuP_7.194 //
Then, having fulfilled the accumulation for <s>Saṃbodhi</s> in proper order,
attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, you shall reach the state of a <s>Sambuddha</s>." // SvayambhuP_7.195 //

children.text: iti matvātra ye lokā rvāñchanti saugataṃ padaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus, those people in the world who, knowing this, desire the state of a <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: sa devān sagaṇāṃ sarvān samārādhya bhajantu te // SvayambhuP_7.196 //
children.translated_text: let them propitiate all those deities together with their retinues and worship them. // SvayambhuP_7.196 //
Having heard this instruction by the lord of sages, those assembled in the court,

children.text: sarve tatheti vijñapya prābhyanandan prabodhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_7.197 //
children.translated_text: all, saying 'so be it,' having been awakened, greatly rejoiced. // SvayambhuP_7.197 //
Then, as the abode of the <s>Jina</s> was concealed by <s>Śāntaśrī</s>,
the lord of sages, having so instructed, entered into <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) of single-pointed vision. // SvayambhuP_7.198 //

body.text: iti śrīsvayaṃbhūdharmmadhātuvāgīśvara guptikṛta pravarttano nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'The Concealment of the Glorious <s>Svayambhū Dharmadhātu Vāgīśvara</s>,' in the <s>Svayambhū Purāṇa</s>.
Eighth Chapter, named 'The Rain of Accomplishment, the Practice at the Hermitage of the <s>Svayambhū Caitya</s>.'

children.text: atha sa bhagavāñchāstā sa samādherutthitaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that Lord, the Teacher, having risen from <s>samādhi</s> again,

children.text: maitreyaṃ taṃ sabhāṃ cāpi samālokyaivamādiśat // SvayambhuP_8.1 //
children.translated_text: looking at <s>Maitreya</s> and the assembly, instructed thus: // SvayambhuP_8.1 //

children.text: śṛṇu maitreya bhūyo syā etad devānubhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Listen, <s>Maitreya</s>, there shall be more, by the power of these deities;
I shall speak also of the great power of accomplishment of the land of <s>Siddhas</s>. // SvayambhuP_8.2 //
Thus, here, in the abode of the <s>Siddha</s> world, the <s>Himālaya</s>,
in the land renowned as <s>Nepāla</s>, by the power of these deities, // SvayambhuP_8.3 //
there was always auspicious celebration, abundance, freedom from calamity,
endowed with all substances, thriving in prosperity. // SvayambhuP_8.4 //
Then, all the people everywhere, practitioners of the ten wholesome actions,
devoted to the worship of the Three Jewels, conducted themselves in auspiciousness. // SvayambhuP_8.5 //
Anointed with this merit, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
steadfast in auspicious glory and good qualities, they became practitioners of <s>Bodhi</s>. // SvayambhuP_8.6 //
Thus was their renown, bestowing supernatural power, accomplishment, qualities, and wealth;
prosperous, abundant, endowed with the refuge of auspicious <s>Śrī</s>, they shone. // SvayambhuP_8.7 //
Therefore, here, <s>yogins</s>, the wise, ascetics, and <s>brahmacārins</s>,

children.text: smṛtvā dhyātvā kuleśānaṃ samārādhya samāśrayan // SvayambhuP_8.8 //
children.translated_text: remembering and meditating upon <s>Kuleśa</s> (family deities), having propitiated them, took refuge. // SvayambhuP_8.8 //
Likewise, other virtuous people too, having come and been pleased,
worshipping this <s>Dharmadhātu</s> with devotion, took refuge. // SvayambhuP_8.9 //
And at all the <s>tīrthas</s>, having performed bathing, charity, and other observances,
they worshipped the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> and took refuge. // SvayambhuP_8.10 //
Having propitiated these five deities according to the proper rites,
worshipping them always with celebrations, they conducted themselves in concentration. // SvayambhuP_8.11 //
Then, having propitiated the goddess <s>Khagānanā</s> according to the proper rites,

children.text: bhajamānā mahotsāhaiḥ prācaranta sadā śubhaṃ // SvayambhuP_8.12 //
children.translated_text: worshipping her with great celebrations, they always conducted themselves in auspiciousness. // SvayambhuP_8.12 //

children.text: evamimaṃ ca pucchāgraṃ caityaṃ mañjuśriyāpi te /
children.translated_text: Thus also this <s>Caitya</s> at the tip of the tail (of the mountain), and <s>Mañjuśrī</s> too—

children.text: sarve lokāḥ samārādhya prābhajanta prasāditāḥ // SvayambhuP_8.13 //
children.translated_text: all the people, having propitiated them, worshipped with delight. // SvayambhuP_8.13 //
Thus all the people, delighting in the true <s>Dharma</s> with joy,

children.text: sadā bhadrāṇi karmmāṇi kṛtvātra sarvvadāśrayan // SvayambhuP_8.14 //
children.translated_text: always performing auspicious deeds, took refuge here always. // SvayambhuP_8.14 //
Thus, this great land of <s>Siddhi</s> (accomplishment), adorned with glory,
filled with many people, shone as the finest of all lands. // SvayambhuP_8.15 //
Then, after a passage of time, a king, the royal ascetic,
named <s>Śrī Guṇakāmadeva</s>, became the Teacher and lord of the world. // SvayambhuP_8.16 //

children.text: tadā sa nṛpatiḥ prauḍhā yuvā kāmātilālasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, that king, mature and youthful, excessively addicted to desire,

children.text: yathā kāmarasaṃ bhuktvā prācaran svecchayāraman // SvayambhuP_8.17 //
children.translated_text: having indulged in the pleasures of desire as he wished, roamed about at will. // SvayambhuP_8.17 //
Then that <s>Kṣatriya</s> too, deluded by the share of desire,
intoxicated by the qualities of women, became heedless of righteous policy and <s>Dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_8.18 //
Seeing a beautiful woman, even one forbidden, deluded,

children.text: balenāpi samākṛṣya vubhuje svecchayā mudā // SvayambhuP_8.19 //
children.translated_text: even by force he would seize and enjoy her at will with pleasure. // SvayambhuP_8.19 //
Thus, that king too, excessively addicted to the <s>Dharma</s> of desire,

children.text: mantriṣu sarva rājyāṅga niveśya svecchayā ramet // SvayambhuP_8.20 //
children.translated_text: entrusting all affairs of the kingdom to ministers, would sport as he wished. // SvayambhuP_8.20 //

children.text: tataḥ ste mantriṇaḥ sarve nṛpaṃ taṃ pramadā vaśe /
children.translated_text: Then, all those ministers, having established the king in the power of women,

children.text: pratiṣṭhāpya yathākāmaṃ bhuktvā caran yathecchayā // SvayambhuP_8.21 //
children.translated_text: indulging and acting as they wished, // SvayambhuP_8.21 //
likewise, servants and people too, all with minds afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements),
rejecting the true <s>Dharma</s>, conducted themselves as partakers of desire. // SvayambhuP_8.22 //
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> too, all of them, practitioners of the ten unwholesome actions,
having abandoned the righteous boundaries of their family <s>Dharma</s>, acted as they wished. // SvayambhuP_8.23 //
<s>Vaiśyas</s> (merchants) too, likewise greedy for the accumulation of wealth through <s>Dharma</s>,
having abandoned the livelihood of their family, indulged and acted as they desired. // SvayambhuP_8.24 //
Great people too, all of them, amassing wealth through injustice,
having abandoned the <s>Dharma</s> of their family, indulging, conducted themselves in pleasure. // SvayambhuP_8.25 //
Merchants too, all of them, striving for wealth through falsehood,
rejecting the <s>Dharma</s> of truth, they conducted themselves with deluded pride. // SvayambhuP_8.26 //
Artisans too, all of them, greedy for morsels of wages,
ignorant of proper methods, blinded by heedlessness, performed their work as they wished. // SvayambhuP_8.27 //
Likewise, women too, with dispositions of desire and defilement in their families,
having abandoned the <s>Dharma</s> of their family, conducted themselves as they desired. // SvayambhuP_8.28 //
Thus, all the people, attached to the ten unwholesome actions,
having abandoned the conduct of their family, acted as they wished. // SvayambhuP_8.29 //
The corrupted <s>Tīrthikas</s> too, seeing thus the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
reviling and abusing it, conducted themselves as they wished. // SvayambhuP_8.30 //

children.text: tadātra vahavo duṣṭā caurā dhūrttāḥ pragalbhikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, here, many corrupted ones—thieves, rogues, and bold ones,

children.text: sādhujanāḥ pratikṣipya ceru mattadvīpā iva // SvayambhuP_8.31 //
children.translated_text: rejecting virtuous people, roamed about like maddened elephants. // SvayambhuP_8.31 //
Even the virtuous and good people, following ignoble deeds,
having abandoned enthusiasm for the true <s>Dharma</s>, conducted themselves in low fashion, merely indulging. // SvayambhuP_8.32 //
Then, due to such sinful conduct, <s>Kali</s> (the age of strife) spread everywhere;

children.text: saddharmmo durvalī bhūto nīcavadvilayaṃ yayau // SvayambhuP_8.33 //
children.translated_text: the true <s>Dharma</s>, weakened, was dissolving like the base. // SvayambhuP_8.33 //
Then, here, as the powerful course of <s>Kali</s> was prevailing,
all the lords of the world, seeing it, became angry and turned away. // SvayambhuP_8.34 //
Then, having turned away, all the lords of the world,

children.text: dhignṛpamiti bā danto draṣṭumapi na cecchire // SvayambhuP_8.35 //
children.translated_text: saying 'Shame on the king!' in censure, did not even wish to look at him. // SvayambhuP_8.35 //
Then, when the benevolent gaze of the world-protectors ceased in celebration,
calamities began to approach and set in motion. // SvayambhuP_8.36 //

children.text: tato devā api krūrā ye duṣṭā mārapākṣikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, even the cruel gods who were corrupted, partisans of <s>Māra</s>,

children.text: sarve tatra rūpālokya mahotpātaṃ pracakrire // SvayambhuP_8.37 //
children.translated_text: all of them, looking upon that scene, wrought great calamity. // SvayambhuP_8.37 //
<s>Agni</s> (Fire) too, looking upon it thus, with an angered disposition like one corrupted,
burning with flame shrouded in smoke, wrought great calamity here. // SvayambhuP_8.38 //
<s>Dharmarāja</s> (Yama, Lord of Death) too became angry, merciless, even against the healthy,
and to slay all living beings, he sent forth a great plague. // SvayambhuP_8.39 //
<s>Nairṛtya</s> (the demon of the southwest), the lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, also, enraged and extremely merciless,
having entered everywhere here, always wrought great calamity. // SvayambhuP_8.40 //

body.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s>, the <s>Nāgarāja</s> (king of serpents) too, corrupted, with cruel gaze,

body.text: dṛṣṭvā vārivahān meghān sarvān vṛṣṭiṃ nyavārayet // SvayambhuP_8.41 //
body.translated_text: seeing the rain-bearing clouds, prevented all rain. // SvayambhuP_8.41 //

children.translated_text: <s>Marut</s> (Wind) too, seeing thus, angered, stood merciless;
acting incurably here, they wrought great calamity. // SvayambhuP_8.42 //

children.text: tathā yakṣāśca ye duṣṭāḥ kinnarā guhyakā api /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the corrupted <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Guhyakas</s> too,

children.text: gṛhe gṛhe praviśyāpi rogotpātaṃ pracakrire // SvayambhuP_8.43 //
children.translated_text: entering house after house, wrought calamity of disease. // SvayambhuP_8.43 //
Likewise, <s>Bhūtas</s> (ghosts), <s>Piśācas</s> (flesh-eating demons), <s>Vetālas</s> (vampires), <s>Kaṭapūtins</s> (stinking spirits),

children.text: ḍākiṇyaḥ pramathāścāpi śākinyaḥ sagaṇā api // SvayambhuP_8.44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ḍākinīs</s> (sky-going demonesses), <s>Pramathas</s> (tormentors), <s>Śākinīs</s> (power-wielding demonesses) with their retinues, // SvayambhuP_8.44 //

children.text: rudrā api sagandharvā kumbhāṇḍā garuḍā api /
children.translated_text: <s>Rudras</s> also, with <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Garuḍas</s> too,
roaming everywhere here, wrought great calamity. // SvayambhuP_8.45 //
All the <s>Mātṛkās</s> (mother goddesses) too, with their retinues, displeased,

children.text: suduṣṭavālokya sarvān stān drakṣituṃ na samāhire // SvayambhuP_8.46 //
children.translated_text: seeing all of them as exceedingly corrupt, did not even deign to look at them. // SvayambhuP_8.46 //
The planets and all the hosts of stars, hostile and displeased,
did not even wish to cast a favorable glance. // SvayambhuP_8.47 //
The <s>Kuleśas</s> (family deities) too, all the deities, displeased,

children.text: saṃtrāta samarthāstān paśyaṃtya eva tasthire // SvayambhuP_8.48 //
children.translated_text: though capable of protecting them, merely stood watching them. // SvayambhuP_8.48 //
Thus, other gods too, all turning away from protection,

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃdarśanaṃ kartumapi naiva vāṃchire // SvayambhuP_8.49 //
children.translated_text: did not even wish to grant them an audience. // SvayambhuP_8.49 //

children.text: teṣāṃ trātuṃ tadekāpi na śaśāka kathaṃcana /
children.translated_text: Not even one of them was able to protect them in any way;
thus, here, great calamity spread on all sides. // SvayambhuP_8.50 //
Thus, as great calamity was spreading everywhere here,

children.text: sarvakleśā hatātmānaḥ pracakru vigrahaṃ mithaḥ // SvayambhuP_8.51 //
children.translated_text: all, with selves ruined by defilements, engaged in mutual conflict. // SvayambhuP_8.51 //

children.text: tadevaṃ kalisaṃraktān sarvān lokān vilokya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing all the people steeped in <s>Kali</s> (strife) thus,

children.text: nṛpatiḥ suciraṃ dhyātvā manasaivaṃ vyacintayat // SvayambhuP_8.52 //
children.translated_text: the king, reflecting for a long time, pondered in his mind thus: // SvayambhuP_8.52 //

children.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ pāpajaṃ dhoraṃ jāyate 'trādhunā mama /
children.translated_text: "Alas, terrible is the misery born of sin that now befalls me here!
Who will bear the great-minded effort to quell that sin? // SvayambhuP_8.53 //
How shall this great suffering be brought to peace here?

children.text: paśyannevamupekṣyaiva rameyaṃ sāmprataṃ ca kiṃ // SvayambhuP_8.54 //
children.translated_text: Seeing thus, should I merely look on with indifference and enjoy myself now? // SvayambhuP_8.54 //

children.text: yo hi rājā prajāduḥkhamupekṣya ramate sukhaṃ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, a king who, ignoring the suffering of his subjects, enjoys happiness—

children.text: sa kiṃ rājā prabhurbhattāṃ duṣṭāhivadvigarhyate // SvayambhuP_8.55 //
children.translated_text: is he truly a king, a lord, a master? He is censured like a wicked serpent! // SvayambhuP_8.55 //
Where a king, ignoring the suffering of his subjects, does not deliberate,
and himself, having enjoyed happiness, roams about at will, // SvayambhuP_8.56 //
there all the subjects, with minds agitated by affliction,
abandoning the righteous conduct of truth and family <s>Dharma</s>, would act insolently. // SvayambhuP_8.57 //
Then those, steeped in sin, practitioners of the ten unwholesome actions,
shameless even in great sin, would conduct themselves as they wish. // SvayambhuP_8.58 //
All this great sinful consequence the king must surely bear;
thus has been truly declared by the great <s>Ṛṣis</s> wise in statecraft. // SvayambhuP_8.59 //
This ripening of sin must indeed be borne by me in existence;

children.text: tadatra kiṃ kariṣyāmi yadupāyaṃ na manyate // SvayambhuP_8.60 //
children.translated_text: what then shall I do here, when no remedy is conceived? // SvayambhuP_8.60 //

children.text: dhig janma me 'tra saṃsāre yasya rājye sadā kaliḥ /
children.translated_text: Cursed be my birth in this <s>Saṃsāra</s>, in whose reign <s>Kali</s> (strife) always prevails,
and famine and great calamity rage day and night! // SvayambhuP_8.61 //

children.text: dhanyāste puruṣā ye hi niḥkleśā vimalāśayā /
children.translated_text: Blessed are those men who, free from affliction, with pure dispositions,

children.text: vimukta bhava saṃcārā bhikṣavo brahmacāriṇaḥ // SvayambhuP_8.62 //
children.translated_text: freed from the wandering of existence, monks and <s>brahmacārins</s>.

children.text: kiṃ me 'tra janma saṃsāre sukulamapi prabhornṛṇāṃ /
children.translated_text: "What use is this birth to me in <s>saṃsāra</s>, even in a noble human family,

children.text: yadahaṃ paśuvad bhuktvā kāmameva rame gṛhe // SvayambhuP_8.63 //
children.translated_text: if I, like an animal, merely enjoy sensual pleasures and delight at home?
Thus I, stained by sin, with a mind troubled by afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>),

children.text: narakeṣu bhraman duḥkhaṃ bhuṃjīyāṃ vividhaṃ sadā // SvayambhuP_8.64 //
children.translated_text: wandering in the hells, would always suffer various miseries.

children.text: tadā ko me suhṛt mitraṃ saṃrakṣitumupācarat /
children.translated_text: Then who is my friend and companion who would come to protect me?

children.text: dharmameva tadā trāṇaṃ sarvaduḥkhāpahaṃ bhave // SvayambhuP_8.65 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> alone is the refuge in existence, the remover of all suffering.
The Buddhist <s>Dharma</s>, the supreme among all <s>Dharmas</s>, the remover of all fears,
the accomplisher of all purposes—it is proclaimed as proven and beneficial to the world.

children.text: ityahaṃ sāmprataṃ gatvā gośṛṅge parvate sthitaṃ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, I shall now go to <s>Gośṛṅga</s> mountain and approach
the great teacher <s>Śāntaśrī</s> who dwells there, with reverence.
He indeed, that great teacher, for the pacification of these calamities,

children.text: vidhānaṃ samupādiśya kuryānme 'tra hitaṃ sadā // SvayambhuP_8.68 //
children.translated_text: having instructed the proper methods, would always bring about my welfare here."
Having thus resolved, the king, together with the chief priest (<s>purohita</s>) and ministers,
and the great people and citizens, addressed them and instructed thus:
"O sirs, since such great calamity prevails here,
I wish now to perform the <s>Dharma</s> that brings about its pacification.
Therefore, the great teacher <s>Śāntiśrī</s>, of great superknowledge,

children.text: prārthayitvā tadā deśād dharttumicchāmi sadṛśaṃ // SvayambhuP_8.71 //
children.translated_text: having entreated him with reverence, I wish to bring him from that land.

children.text: iti sarve vayaṃ tatra gośṛṅge 'gre samādarāt /
children.translated_text: Thus, let us all go there to <s>Gośṛṅga</s> peak with reverence
to entreat the great teacher <s>Śāntaśrī</s>."
Hearing this instruction by the king, the chief priest and others,

children.text: sarve tatheti vijñapya prābhyanandan prabodhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_8.73 //
children.translated_text: all acknowledged 'so be it,' rejoiced, and were awakened.
Then that sovereign king, together with his ministers, people, and citizens,
placing the chief priest at the forefront, joyfully proceeded to <s>Gośṛṅga</s> peak.
There, seeing that teacher, the king was greatly delighted,
and approaching with palms joined, bowing, he sat at his lotus feet.
Likewise, all the people too, beholding him, were pleased,
and approaching, bowing at his feet, they attended upon him with joy.

children.text: tān sarvān samupāsīnān samīkṣya sa mahāmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing all of them seated, that one of great wisdom,
<s>Śāntaśrī</s>, looking at that king, instructed thus:

children.text: rājan sadāstu vo bhadraṃ sarvatrāpi nirantaraṃ /
children.translated_text: "O King, may auspiciousness always be yours, everywhere and without interruption.

children.text: kimarthamiha prāyāsi tat me 'gre vaktuṃmarhasi // SvayambhuP_8.78 //
children.translated_text: For what purpose have you come here? Please tell me."

children.text: iti śāntaśriyā prokte nṛpatiḥ sa kṛtāñjaliḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>Śāntaśrī</s> had spoken thus, that king, with palms joined,

children.text: praṇatvā taṃ mahācārya paśyannevaṃ nyavedayet // SvayambhuP_8.79 //
children.translated_text: bowing to that great teacher, looking at him, reported thus:
"O Glorious Teacher, for this purpose I take refuge in you;
for this purpose I entreat you—please instruct me.

children.text: yat me 'tra pāpato rājye mahotpātaṃ pravarttate /
children.translated_text: Because of sins, great calamity prevails in my kingdom;
please instruct the method for its pacification."

children.text: iti saṃprārthite rājñā śāntaśrī mantravit sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus entreated by the king, <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, the wise knower of <s>mantras</s>,
looking at that king, the great being, instructed thus:
"O King, because of sins, great calamity prevails here thus;
