children.text: tatpāpaśamanopāyaṃ vakṣāmi te śṛṇuṣva tat // SvayambhuP_8.83 //
children.translated_text: I shall tell you the method for subduing that sin—listen to it.
You, O King, the sovereign here, the protector of all <s>Dharmas</s>,
do not govern your subjects according to righteous policy.
Your ministers too, all of them, are averse to righteous policy,
and merely enjoying sensual pleasures, they conduct themselves as they please.
Likewise the servants, people, citizens, and great persons,
having abandoned the <s>Dharma</s> of their lineage, conduct themselves as they please.
Thus all the people, practicing the ten unwholesome actions,
rejecting the true <s>Dharmas</s>, conduct themselves heedlessly.
Therefore, this ripening of sin must indeed be experienced in existence;

children.text: yenaiva yatkṛtaṃ karmma bhoktavyaṃ tena tatphalaṃ // SvayambhuP_8.88 //
children.translated_text: whatever action has been done by anyone, its fruit must be experienced by that person.

children.text: evaṃ matvā nṛpaḥ svāmī svayaṃ nītyā vicārayan /
children.translated_text: Understanding this, O King, the sovereign himself, reflecting with righteous policy,

children.text: bodhayitvā prayatnena lokān saṃpālayat sadā // SvayambhuP_8.89 //
children.translated_text: having awakened the people with effort, should always protect them.

body.translated_text: But if the king here, without proper reflection, through heedlessness,
himself merely enjoys sensual pleasures and conducts himself as he pleases,

children.translated_text: then all the people too, following the king's conduct,
merely enjoying sensual pleasures, would conduct themselves as they please.

children.text: tadā tatra mahotpātaṃ pravarttat pāpato dhruvaṃ /
children.translated_text: Then great calamity would certainly prevail there because of sin;

children.text: pravarttite mahotpāta lokā syuḥ pāpaduḥkhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_8.92 //
children.translated_text: when great calamity prevails, the people would be afflicted by the suffering of sin.
If the king, watching them, remains indifferent and acts without compassion,

children.text: lokasaṃrakṣaṇe asaktaḥ sa sarvapāpabhāg bhavet // SvayambhuP_8.93 //
children.translated_text: being unattached to the protection of the people, he would share in all sins.
For indeed all sins committed by all the people
would fall before the king and give him their fruits.
This truth has been proclaimed by all the lords of sages.

children.text: natvā rājā svayaṃ nītyā vicārayan samācaret // SvayambhuP_8.95 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the king himself, reflecting with righteous policy, should conduct himself accordingly."
Having heard this instruction by <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, the wise counselor,
that king, with fear, his mind afflicted with burning anguish,
taking refuge in that teacher <s>Śāntaśrī</s>,
bowing at his lotus feet, again entreated with reverence:
"O Teacher, I shall always carry out your command upon my head;

children.text: tat me yaducitaṃ dharmma tat samādeṣṭumarhati // SvayambhuP_8.98 //
children.translated_text: please instruct me in the <s>Dharma</s> that is proper for me."

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ rājñā śrutvācāryaḥ sa satmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing this entreaty by the king, that teacher, the wise one,
looking at that king, the great being, instructed thus:
"O King, listen with concentration; I shall tell you the cause of auspiciousness.

children.text: yadyasti te kṛpā loka tat kuru yanmayoditaṃ // SvayambhuP_8.100 //
children.translated_text: If you have compassion for the people, then do what I say.
First, having bathed always at these <s>tīrthas</s> according to the proper rites,
with pure conduct and practice, concentrated, purified in the three spheres,
with a vow directed toward perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>), bearing the welfare of all beings,

children.text: triratnabhajanaṃ kṛtvā carasva poṣadhaṃ vrataṃ // SvayambhuP_8.102 //
children.translated_text: having performed worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), practice the <s>poṣadha</s> vow.
Then, this lord of the world, the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
having propitiated it according to the proper rites, worship it always with reverence.

children.text: tathā sarvā imā pañca devatāśca yathāvidhi /
children.translated_text: Likewise, all these five deities also, according to the proper rites,
having propitiated and worshipped them, serve them always with reverence.
And this <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> also, having propitiated it always,
having worshipped according to the proper rites, serve it with great celebration.
Likewise, the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> (dispassionate ones) also, having propitiated them according to the proper rites,
having worshipped with great enthusiasm, serve them always with reverence.
Likewise, the <s>Māheśvarī</s> goddess, the bird-faced one, with reverence,
having propitiated and worshipped her, serve her according to the proper rites.
All these deities indeed are lords and rulers of all the worlds,
and for the welfare of all beings, they have manifested of their own accord.
Therefore, here, among all these deities, always with faith,

children.text: vidhinā bhajanaṃ kṛtvā saṃcarasva jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_8.109 //
children.translated_text: having performed worship according to the rites, practice for the welfare of the world.
And having awakened all the people with effort,
at all these <s>tīrthas</s>, always bathing, giving charity, and the rest,
having caused great merit to be made, which bestows auspicious happiness to the world,
cause them to practice the <s>poṣadha</s> vow for the happiness of the good qualities of a <s>Sambuddha</s>.
And the worship of these deities, beginning with the Three Jewels, always
having caused to be done with great enthusiasm, guide them on the path of <s>Bodhi</s>.
Then, by the power of this merit, auspiciousness will prevail everywhere;

children.text: tadā sarvamahotpātaṃ sarvatra vilayaṃ vrajet // SvayambhuP_8.113 //
children.translated_text: then all great calamities will be dissolved everywhere.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s> of the immortals, and all the lords of the worlds,

children.text: sudṛśātra samālokya pālayeyuḥ sadā mudā // SvayambhuP_8.114 //
children.translated_text: looking upon this place with a favorable eye, would always protect it with joy.
Then, when this is protected by all those lords of the worlds again,
prosperity, glorious and auspicious celebration would always prevail.
Then all the people, free from disease, repositories of glorious virtues,

children.text: viramya pāpamārgebhyaḥ saṃcareran sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_8.116 //
children.translated_text: having turned away from sinful paths, would always conduct themselves in auspiciousness.

children.text: evaṃ dhṛtvā sadā rājan mahāpuṇya prabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, O King, upholding this always, by the power of great merit,
at last, attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, one would reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.
Thus, the supreme merit born from worship of the Three Jewels in existence—

children.text: vijñāyādau triratnānāṃ bhajasva śraddhayā smaran // SvayambhuP_8.118 //
children.translated_text: understanding this, first worship the Three Jewels with faith, remembering them.
Then, having bathed at all these <s>tīrthas</s>, with purified senses and disposition,

children.text: triratnaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatvā bhajasva poṣadhaṃ vrataṃ // SvayambhuP_8.119 //
children.translated_text: having gone to the Three Jewels as refuge, observe the <s>poṣadha</s> vow.
Then, all these deities, beginning with the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, always
having propitiated according to the proper rites, worship and serve them.
Having also awakened all the people with effort,
having had them bathe at all these <s>tīrthas</s> according to the proper rites,
establishing them in the refuge of the Three Jewels, which is the means to the knowledge of perfect enlightenment,
the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, have them observe the <s>poṣadha</s> vow.
Having also caused the worship of these deities to be performed always,
having established them on the path of <s>Bodhi</s>, guide and protect them in auspiciousness.
Having thus done, having obtained great merit, having become a repository of glorious good qualities,
one would certainly become a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a great being, of great superknowledge.
Then, having fulfilled the accumulations for perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>) in proper order,
as an <s>Arhat</s>, attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, you would reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>."

children.text: iti śāntaśriyā śāstā samādiṣṭaṃ niśamya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction given by the teacher <s>Śāntaśrī</s>,
the king acknowledged 'so be it' and wished to do accordingly.
Then that king, all the ministers, attendants, and people,
the citizens and great persons, he addressed and instructed thus:

children.text: bho mantriṇo janāḥ sarve 'mātyāḥ paurā mahājanāḥ /
children.translated_text: "O ministers, all you people, officers, citizens, and great persons—
as the teacher has instructed, so you should conduct yourselves.
I too, likewise upholding always the cause of auspiciousness,
having taken refuge in the Three Jewels, am eager to practice the vow."

children.text: ityādiṣṭaṃ narendreṇa śrutvā te mantriṇo janāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing this instruction by the king, the ministers and people,

children.text: paurā mahājanāḥ sarva tatheti pratiśuśruvuḥ // SvayambhuP_8.130 //
children.translated_text: the citizens and great persons—all agreed 'so be it.'
Then that king, together with all—the chief priest, ministers,
officers, attendants, citizens, and great persons—
having bathed at all these <s>tīrthas</s> according to the proper rites in sequence,

children.text: śuddhaśīlaḥ samādhāya prācarat poṣadhaṃ vrataṃ // SvayambhuP_8.132 //
children.translated_text: of pure conduct, having practiced concentration, observed the <s>poṣadha</s> vow.
Then those, of pure souls, having taken refuge in the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels),
having propitiated the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (essence of reality), worshipped and served it with joy. // SvayambhuP_8.133 //
Likewise, in <s>Vāyupura</s> (City of Wind), the <s>Vāyu</s> deity according to proper rites,
in <s>Agnipura</s> (City of Fire) the <s>Agni</s> deity, and in <s>Nāgapura</s> (City of Serpents) the lords of serpents, // SvayambhuP_8.134 //
in <s>Vasupura</s> (City of Wealth) <s>Vasundharā</s> (the Earth Goddess), bestower of the glory and qualities of the true <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: śāntapure maheśānaṃ sambaraṃ sagaṇaṃ kramāt // SvayambhuP_8.135 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Śāntapura</s> (City of Peace) <s>Maheśāna</s> (the Great Lord) <s>Saṃvara</s> together with his retinue, in order — // SvayambhuP_8.135 //
having worshipped according to proper rites, having taken refuge with faith,

children.text: tathā mañjuśrī yaścaityaṃ samabhyarcyābhajan sadā // SvayambhuP_8.136 //
children.translated_text: and also having always worshipped the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, // SvayambhuP_8.136 //
and likewise the eight dispassionate ones, and <s>Śrī Devī</s>, the bird-faced one,
having propitiated them according to proper rites, he always worshipped them. // SvayambhuP_8.137 //
Likewise, all those people too, following the conduct of the king,

children.text: snātvā sarveṣu tīrtheṣu śuddhaśīlā samādarāt // SvayambhuP_8.138 //
children.translated_text: having bathed at all the <s>tīrthas</s> (holy waters), of pure conduct, with reverence, // SvayambhuP_8.138 //
having taken refuge in the <s>Triratna</s>, practicing the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day) vow,
worshipped and served all the deities headed by the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. // SvayambhuP_8.139 //
Then, through the power of that merit, auspiciousness prevailed everywhere,

children.text: tataḥ sarva mahotpātaṃ krameṇa praśamaṃ yayau // SvayambhuP_8.140 //
children.translated_text: and all the great calamities gradually subsided. // SvayambhuP_8.140 //

children.text: tadā sarve 'pi te lokā nīrogāḥ puṣṭitendriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those people became free from disease, with nourished senses,

children.text: mahānandaṃ sukhaṃ prāpya babhūvu dharmmalālasāḥ // SvayambhuP_8.141 //
children.translated_text: and having attained great joy and happiness, became devoted to <s>dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_8.141 //

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā na nṛpo rājā pratyakṣaṃ dharmasatphalaṃ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the visible fruit of <s>dharma</s>, that king
exclaimed, 'Oh, the greatness of the true <s>dharma</s>!' and went about delighted. // SvayambhuP_8.142 //
But at that time, good rainfall did not occur here at all,

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā na nṛpaścāsīd durbhikṣaśaṃkitāśayaḥ // SvayambhuP_8.143 //
children.translated_text: and seeing that, the king became fearful in mind about famine. // SvayambhuP_8.143 //

children.text: tataḥ sa karuṇāviṣṭahṛdayaḥ sa nṛpaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that king, his heart filled with compassion,

children.text: śāntaśriyaṃ tamācārya natvaiva prāha sāñjaliḥ // SvayambhuP_8.144 //
children.translated_text: bowed to that <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) <s>Śāntaśrī</s> and spoke with joined palms: // SvayambhuP_8.144 //
"O <s>ācārya</s>, by your compassion, auspiciousness now prevails here,
and all the great calamities have subsided on all sides. // SvayambhuP_8.145 //
But good rainfall has not occurred even now;
please instruct the means for causing good rainfall." // SvayambhuP_8.146 //

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ rājñā śrutvācāryaḥ sa satmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this request of the king, that <s>ācārya</s> of righteous mind,
looking at that king, the great being, spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_8.147 //
"Well said, O king! Hear now the cause of perpetual good harvest;
I shall instruct the means for causing good rainfall right now. // SvayambhuP_8.148 //
Having drawn the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) of the <s>Nāga</s> kings according to proper rites,
invoke and propitiate all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s> there. // SvayambhuP_8.149 //
You, O great hero, be the practitioner and performer there;

children.text: yathā māyopadiṣṭāni tathā sarvāṇi sādhaya // SvayambhuP_8.150 //
children.translated_text: accomplish everything as I have instructed." // SvayambhuP_8.150 //
Having heard this instruction of the <s>ācārya</s>, that king, with joy,
assenting 'so be it,' wished to do accordingly. // SvayambhuP_8.151 //

children.text: tataḥ sa vajradhṛg vārā nāgapuraṃ yathāvidhi /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>vajra</s>-holder, at <s>Nāgapura</s>, according to proper rites,

children.text: likhitvā maṇḍalaṃ ramyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya samārccayat // SvayambhuP_8.152 //
children.translated_text: having drawn a beautiful <s>maṇḍala</s>, consecrated and worshipped it. // SvayambhuP_8.152 //
There, the <s>ācārya</s>, having propitiated all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s> in due order,
having invoked them, undertook to worship them. // SvayambhuP_8.153 //
There, all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s>, having come in due order,
took their respective seats and remained, with minds made serene. // SvayambhuP_8.154 //
<s>Karkoṭaka</s>, the king of serpents, alone did not come, out of shame;
observing this, <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, the great <s>ācārya</s> of great powers, // SvayambhuP_8.155 //
looking at that king, the great hero, great being, of great powers
and great supernatural knowledge, addressed and instructed him thus: // SvayambhuP_8.156 //
"O king, all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s> have come here now;

children.text: eka karkkoṭako nāgarāja eveha nāgataḥ // SvayambhuP_8.157 //
children.translated_text: only <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> king, has not come here. // SvayambhuP_8.157 //
'I am deformed; how can I go to the great assembly throne

children.text: gatvā tiṣṭheyamityevaṃ dhyātvā nāyāti lajjayā // SvayambhuP_8.158 //
children.translated_text: of the <s>Nāga</s> kings and stand there?' — thinking thus, he does not come, out of shame. // SvayambhuP_8.158 //

children.text: atastaṃ sahasā rājan gatvā tatra mahāhrade /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O king, go quickly to that great lake,
address <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, request him, and bring him here. // SvayambhuP_8.159 //
If even when requested that king of serpents does not come here,

children.text: tadā balena dhṛtvāpi sarvathā taṃ samānaya // SvayambhuP_8.160 //
children.translated_text: then, even seizing him by force, bring him here by all means." // SvayambhuP_8.160 //

children.text: ityācārya samādiṣṭaṃ śṛtvā sa nṛpatiḥ sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction of the <s>ācārya</s>, that wise king
reported thus to the <s>ācārya</s> <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, looking at him: // SvayambhuP_8.161 //
"O <s>ācārya</s>, how would I alone be able, going to that deep great lake,

children.text: gatvā balena nāgendraṃ dhṛtvā netuṃ praśaknuyāṃ // SvayambhuP_8.162 //
children.translated_text: to seize the lord of <s>Nāgas</s> by force and bring him?" // SvayambhuP_8.162 //

children.text: iti nivedya taṃ rājñā śrutvācāryaḥ sa mantravit /
children.translated_text: Having heard this report from the king, that <s>ācārya</s>, the knower of <s>mantras</s>,
looking at that king, the great hero, spoke thus: // SvayambhuP_8.163 //
"Mount a green horse and take a flower purified by <s>mantras</s>;

children.text: dhṛtvā braja praśaknoṣi mama mantrānubhāvataḥ // SvayambhuP_8.164 //
children.translated_text: you will be able to do it through the power of my <s>mantras</s>. // SvayambhuP_8.164 //

children.text: durvākuṇḍamidaṃ puṣpaṃ tatrādau kṣipa māṃ smaran /
children.translated_text: First, throw this <s>dūrvā</s>-grass flower-offering into the water there, remembering me;

children.text: bhraman yatra caren puṣpaṃ tat yathānusaran baja // SvayambhuP_8.165 //
children.translated_text: wherever the flower floats and goes, follow it and proceed. // SvayambhuP_8.165 //
Having thus instructed, he gave the <s>dūrvā</s> flower-offering, purified by <s>mantras</s>,
to the lord of men, and instructed again thus: // SvayambhuP_8.166 //

children.text: gatvaivaṃ nṛpate tatra nāgapure sametya taṃ /
children.translated_text: "Going thus, O king, arrive at <s>Nāgapura</s>,
address <s>Karkoṭaka</s> and convey to him my words thus: // SvayambhuP_8.167 //
'O <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, the purpose for which I have come here —

children.text: tadbhavānapi jānīyāt tathāpi vakṣyate mayā // SvayambhuP_8.168 //
children.translated_text: you too should know it; nevertheless, I shall state it: // SvayambhuP_8.168 //
At <s>Gośṛṅga</s>, the great <s>ācārya</s> <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, the <s>vajra</s>-holder, the accomplished one,
to bring about the cessation of famine and always cause good rainfall — // SvayambhuP_8.169 //
there in <s>Nāgapura</s>, all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s>, according to proper rites,
having propitiated and invoked them, he has undertaken to worship them. // SvayambhuP_8.170 //
All the lords of <s>Nāgas</s>, headed by <s>Varuṇa</s>, have come there;

children.text: tvameva nāgataḥ kasmāt sahasā gantumarhati // SvayambhuP_8.171 //
children.translated_text: why have you alone not come? You should come at once.' // SvayambhuP_8.171 //
If even when thus requested that king of serpents does not come,

children.text: valenāpi samākṛṣya sahasā nīyatāṃ tvayā // SvayambhuP_8.172 //
children.translated_text: then, even dragging him by force, let him be brought quickly by you." // SvayambhuP_8.172 //
Thus the teacher <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, having instructed with respect,
sent me for that purpose here — therefore you should come." // SvayambhuP_8.173 //
Thus having instructed, the <s>ācārya</s>, giving the flower purified by <s>mantras</s>

children.text: datvā taṃ nṛpatiṃ vīraṃ preṣayat tatra satvaraṃ // SvayambhuP_8.174 //
children.translated_text: to that heroic king, dispatched him there quickly. // SvayambhuP_8.174 //
Having heard this instruction of the <s>ācārya</s>, that great-minded one,
taking the <s>dūrvā</s> flower-offering, saying 'so be it,' set forth from there. // SvayambhuP_8.175 //

children.text: tataḥ sa nṛpatirvīraḥ śāstu rājñāṃ śirāvahan /
children.translated_text: Then that heroic king, carrying the command of the teacher upon his head,

children.text: haridaśvaṃ samāruhya saṃcaranstad hadaṃ yayau // SvayambhuP_8.176 //
children.translated_text: mounting the green horse, traveled and went to that lake. // SvayambhuP_8.176 //

children.text: tatra tīraṃ samāsādya paśyaṃ nṛpaḥ sa taṃ hadaṃ /
children.translated_text: There, having reached the shore, the king, looking at that lake,
bowing, remembering the <s>ācārya</s>, threw the <s>dūrvā</s> flower-offering into the water. // SvayambhuP_8.177 //
That offering, thrown into the deep water, floating, went to <s>Nāgapura</s>;
the king too, mounting his horse, followed that flower and went. // SvayambhuP_8.178 //

children.text: evaṃ nāgapure gatvā nṛpatiḥ sa vilokayan /
children.translated_text: Thus, having gone to <s>Nāgapura</s>, that king, looking around,

children.text: karkoṭaka mahīndraṃ taṃ sahasā samupācarat // SvayambhuP_8.179 //
children.translated_text: quickly approached <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, the great lord. // SvayambhuP_8.179 //
There, that hero, having met <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, the great lord,

children.text: yathācāryāya saṃdipṭaṃ tathā sarvaṃ nyavedayat // SvayambhuP_8.180 //
children.translated_text: reported everything just as instructed by the <s>ācārya</s>. // SvayambhuP_8.180 //

children.text: tat sanniveditaṃ sarva śrutvā nāgādhipāpi saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard all that was reported, that lord of <s>Nāgas</s>

children.text: kiñcidapyuttaraṃ naiva dadau tasmai mahībhuje // SvayambhuP_8.181 //
children.translated_text: did not give any reply whatsoever to that lord of the earth. // SvayambhuP_8.181 //

children.text: tataḥ sa nṛpatiścaivaṃ nivedya taṃ mahīśvaraṃ /
children.translated_text: Then that king, having thus reported to that great lord,
looking at him, addressing him, requested with respect: // SvayambhuP_8.182 //
"O lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, be pleased here; I carry the command of the teacher upon my head;

children.text: tvadāmantra na evāhaṃ prāgatastat samāvraja // SvayambhuP_8.183 //
children.translated_text: I have come here only to invite you — therefore please come." // SvayambhuP_8.183 //
Though thus requested, that <s>Nāga</s> king

children.text: kiñcitprāpyuttaraṃ naiva dadau tasmai mahībhuje // SvayambhuP_8.184 //
children.translated_text: gave no reply whatsoever to that lord of the earth. // SvayambhuP_8.184 //
Then that heroic king, as instructed by the teacher,
having reported everything before him, spoke again thus: // SvayambhuP_8.185 //

children.text: nāgendra nāparādhaṃ me yattvayā na śrutaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: "O lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, do not hold it against me that my words were not heeded by you;

children.text: tanme śāstrā yathādiṣṭaṃ tathā nūnaṃ careya hi // SvayambhuP_8.186 //
children.translated_text: for I must indeed carry out what the teacher has instructed." // SvayambhuP_8.186 //

children.text: ityuktepi narendreṇa karkoṭako hi yo 'pi saḥ /
children.translated_text: Though thus spoken to by the lord of men, that <s>Karkoṭaka</s>

children.text: kiñcidapyuttaraṃ naiva dadau rājñe mahībhṛte // SvayambhuP_8.187 //
children.translated_text: still gave no reply whatsoever to the king, the lord of the earth. // SvayambhuP_8.187 //
Then that heroic king, carrying the command of the teacher upon his head,
seized him, dragged that serpent, and went forth as if carrying a heavy burden. // SvayambhuP_8.188 //
Then, brought from the horse, by <s>Guṇakāmadeva</s>,

children.text: ānīte tena mārgeṇa vaśikācala ucyate // SvayambhuP_8.189 //
children.translated_text: the path by which he was brought is called <s>Vaśikācala</s> (Mountain of Subjugation). // SvayambhuP_8.189 //

children.text: evaṃ dhṛtvā samākṛṣya sa vīrastaṃ mahīśvaraṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having seized and dragged that great lord, that hero

children.text: sahasā nāgapure nītvā śāsturagre samācarat // SvayambhuP_8.190 //
children.translated_text: quickly brought him to <s>Nāgapura</s> and came before the teacher. // SvayambhuP_8.190 //
"O <s>ācārya</s>, by your command, <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, the king of serpents,
has been seized, dragged, and brought by me — behold him and be pleased." // SvayambhuP_8.191 //
Having heard this report of the king, the <s>ācārya</s>, concentrated,
looking at that king, the great hero, instructed thus: // SvayambhuP_8.192 //
"Well done, O king, great hero! Since the king of serpents has been brought by you,
take him to his seat and establish him there in due order." // SvayambhuP_8.193 //
Having heard this instruction of the <s>ācārya</s>, that king accordingly
addressed that <s>Nāga</s> king and seated him on his throne. // SvayambhuP_8.194 //
Having seen him seated on his throne, the <s>ācārya</s>, according to proper rites,

children.text: nāgendrān stān samāvāhya samārādhya samārcayat // SvayambhuP_8.195 //
children.translated_text: having invoked and propitiated those lords of <s>Nāgas</s>, worshipped them. // SvayambhuP_8.195 //

children.text: tataḥ sa vrajadhṛkājña ācāryaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>vajra</s>-holding king, by command of the <s>ācārya</s>,
having praised all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s>, requested them thus with respect: // SvayambhuP_8.196 //
"O lords, great <s>Nāga</s> kings, all of you before me
have been propitiated, invoked, and worshipped according to proper rites. // SvayambhuP_8.197 //
Therefore, be pleased with me always and deign to grant what is desired;
I propitiate you only for the welfare of all beings, and for no other reason. // SvayambhuP_8.198 //
Because of the accumulation of sins here, famine now prevails,

children.text: tena sarve 'pi duḥkhārttā lokaścaranti pātakaṃ // SvayambhuP_8.199 //
children.translated_text: and therefore all the people, afflicted by suffering, commit sinful acts. // SvayambhuP_8.199 //
For the pacification of that famine and the cause of perpetual good harvest,
I perform this rite for causing good rainfall, for the welfare of the world. // SvayambhuP_8.200 //
All of you lords, for the protection of all beings,
should cause good rainfall here always." // SvayambhuP_8.201 //
Having heard this request made by <s>Śāntaśrī</s>,
all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s> assented to him, saying 'so be it.' // SvayambhuP_8.202 //
Having heard that promise of 'so be it' from the <s>Nāga</s> kings,
<s>Śāntaśrī</s> requested those <s>Nāga</s> kings thus with respect: // SvayambhuP_8.203 //

children.text: bhavanto me prasīdantu yadahaṃ prārthaye punaḥ /
children.translated_text: "May you be gracious to me, for what I entreat again —
for the welfare of all beings, may you deign to grant the wish." // SvayambhuP_8.204 //
Having heard this entreaty by <s>Śāntaśrī</s>,
all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s> replied to him, 'So be it.' // SvayambhuP_8.205 //
Having heard the promise given by all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s>,
the teacher entreated those serpent lords thus with devotion: // SvayambhuP_8.206 //

children.text: bhavantaḥ śrūyatāṃ vākyaṃ yat mayā prārthyate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: "May you hear the words that I entreat once more.

children.text: tadbhavadbhiḥ pratijñātaṃ saṃdhātavyaṃ tathā sadā // SvayambhuP_8.207 //
children.translated_text: That which is promised by you must always be upheld. // SvayambhuP_8.207 //
When, due to the course of sin, drought surely occurs here,
then let the means for accomplishing good rainfall be employed. // SvayambhuP_8.208 //

children.text: tadyathā bhavatāṃ paṭṭe likhitvā maṇḍalaṃ śubhaṃ /
children.translated_text: To that end, having drawn an auspicious <s>maṇḍala</s> on your banner-cloth,
I am eager to establish and consecrate it according to the prescribed method. // SvayambhuP_8.209 //
Whenever drought should occur here, then this banner-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
having been spread out, worshipped according to the ritual, invoked, and honored — // SvayambhuP_8.210 //
thus, when this banner is spread out and worshipped according to the prescribed method,
good rainfall must be sustained by you for the welfare of the world." // SvayambhuP_8.211 //
Having heard this entreaty by <s>Śāntaśrī</s>,
all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s> replied to him, 'So be it.' // SvayambhuP_8.212 //
Then that wise knower of <s>mantras</s>, with the consent of all the lords of <s>Nāgas</s>,

children.text: likhitvā maṇḍalaṃ paṭṭe pratiṣṭhāpya yathāvidhi // SvayambhuP_8.213 //
children.translated_text: having drawn the <s>maṇḍala</s> on the banner-cloth and established it according to the prescribed method, // SvayambhuP_8.213 //
afterward, when drought occurred, for the accomplishment of good rainfall,
he placed it in <s>Nāgapura</s>, safeguarding it from being burned. // SvayambhuP_8.214 //

children.text: tato vajrī sa ācāryaḥ sarvān stān bhujagādhipān /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Vajra</s>-bearing teacher, having entreated all those lords of serpents,

children.text: saṃprārthya vinayaṃ kṛtvā visasarjja vinodayan // SvayambhuP_8.215 //
children.translated_text: having shown them respect, dismissed them, delighting them. // SvayambhuP_8.215 //

children.text: tataḥ sarve 'pi te nāgarājāḥ svasvālayaṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those <s>Nāga</s> kings returned to their respective abodes,
and raising banks of clouds, they rained everywhere. // SvayambhuP_8.216 //
Then, due to the course of good rainfall, the famine was dispelled,
and abundance, auspicious celebration commenced everywhere. // SvayambhuP_8.217 //
Then all those beings, delighted with great joy,

children.text: triratnabhajanaṃ kṛtvā prācaranta sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_8.218 //
children.translated_text: performing worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), always conducted themselves in auspiciousness. // SvayambhuP_8.218 //

children.text: tataḥ sa nṛpati rājā dṛṣṭasatyaḥ prasāditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that king, having seen the truth, pleased,
having worshipped the teacher <s>Śāntaśrī</s> according to the prescribed method, // SvayambhuP_8.219 //
bowing with the eight limbs, with a pleased mind, and having made circumambulations,
with palms joined in salutation, gazing at him, he entreated thus with devotion: // SvayambhuP_8.220 //
"O Blessed One, O great teacher, by the power of your <s>Dharma</s>,
all calamity has been pacified and good rainfall has commenced. // SvayambhuP_8.221 //
Therefore, here always, certainly, free from calamity everywhere,
may there be unceasing celebration of auspicious <s>Dharma</s> glory. // SvayambhuP_8.222 //

children.text: evaṃ sadā kṛpā dṛṣṭayā saṃpaśyan viṣaye mama /
children.translated_text: Thus, always looking with compassionate gaze upon my realm,
may you deign to always make it free from calamity and auspiciously celebrated. // SvayambhuP_8.223 //

children.text: sāmprataṃ saphalaṃ janma saṃsārajīvitaṃ ca me /
children.translated_text: Now fruitful is my birth and my life in <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: yallokāśca sukhībhūtāḥ saṃcaranta sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_8.224 //
children.translated_text: since the beings have become happy and always conduct themselves in auspiciousness. // SvayambhuP_8.224 //
Therefore I, O Teacher, now bearing your command upon my head,
taking refuge in the hermitage of my kingdom, shall rule and protect the world. // SvayambhuP_8.225 //
Therefore, bestowing your favor upon me, graciously pleased,

children.text: saṃbodhisādhane cittaṃ sa sthitiṃ karttumarhati // SvayambhuP_8.226 //
children.translated_text: may you deign to establish my mind steadfastly in the means to <s>Saṃbodhi</s>." // SvayambhuP_8.226 //

children.text: iti vijñapya bhūpālasta sya śāstuḥ padāmbuje /
children.translated_text: Having thus informed the king, bowing at the lotus feet of that Teacher,

children.text: natvānujñāṃ samāsādya mahotsāhaiḥ puraṃ yayau // SvayambhuP_8.227 //
children.translated_text: and having obtained permission, he went to the city with great celebration. // SvayambhuP_8.227 //

children.text: tatra sa nṛpa āśritya samantri sacivo mudā /
children.translated_text: There, that king, taking refuge with his ministers and counselors, joyfully,

children.text: bodhicaryāvrataṃ dhṛtvā tasthau kurvan sadā śubhaṃ // SvayambhuP_8.228 //
children.translated_text: holding the vow of the practice of <s>Bodhi</s>, remained always doing auspicious deeds. // SvayambhuP_8.228 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter, named 'The Accomplishment of the Name of the <s>Svayambhū Caitya</s> Hermitage, and the Bringing of Good Rainfall.'

body.text: navama adhyāyaḥ śrīmahācārya śāntikaraguṇasaṃsiddhimahātmyānubhāva prakathanapravartano nāma
body.translated_text: Ninth chapter, named 'The Narration of the Greatness of the Power and Qualities of the Glorious Great Teacher <s>Śāntikara</s>.'

children.translated_text: Then <s>Maitreya</s>, looking up, rising with joined palms,
bowing to that Blessed One, entreated him thus with devotion: // SvayambhuP_9.1 //

children.text: kadā śāntikaraṃ nāma tasyābhavat kathaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: "When did the name <s>Śāntikara</s> (peacemaker) come to be his, and how?
I wish to hear the cause of that; please instruct us." // SvayambhuP_9.2 //

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tena maitreyeṇa sa sarvavit /
children.translated_text: Thus entreated by <s>Maitreya</s>, that omniscient one,
the Blessed One, looking at that great being, instructed him thus: // SvayambhuP_9.3 //
"Listen, O <s>Maitreya</s>, I shall declare the great quality of <s>Śāntaśrī</s>,
his enthusiasm for the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>, bearing the purpose of auspicious glory and good qualities. // SvayambhuP_9.4 //
That king, a great being, eager for the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
having renounced the pleasures of the kingdom, undertook a pilgrimage to the <s>tīrthas</s>. // SvayambhuP_9.5 //

children.text: sa sarveṣvapi tīrtheṣu snātvā dānaṃ vidhāya ca /
children.translated_text: He, having bathed at all the <s>tīrthas</s> and performed giving,
practiced the three <s>samādhis</s> and observed the <s>Poṣadha</s> vow. // SvayambhuP_9.6 //
Thus, wandering to all the sacred seats, with a mind set on the true <s>Dharma</s>,
holding the vow of <s>Yogacaryā</s> (practice of yoga), he traveled about in concentration. // SvayambhuP_9.7 //
Wandering through all the fields of merit, he came here,

children.text: dṛṣṭvaimaṃ maṇḍalaṃ ramye vismitaṃ samupāyayau // SvayambhuP_9.8 //
children.translated_text: and seeing this beautiful <s>maṇḍala</s>, he was filled with wonder. // SvayambhuP_9.8 //
Here, seeing from afar this <s>Dharmadhātu Jina</s> shrine,
bowing joyfully with the eight limbs, he quickly approached to behold it. // SvayambhuP_9.9 //
Arriving, that great being, having seen this <s>Jina</s> shrine in the form of light,
this <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, bowing, took shelter in it. // SvayambhuP_9.10 //
Then that king, rising with enthusiasm, here in beautiful <s>Nepāla</s>,

children.text: sarvatrāpi ca saṃdraṣṭuṃ pracacāra vilokayan // SvayambhuP_9.11 //
children.translated_text: traveled about everywhere, looking and beholding. // SvayambhuP_9.11 //

children.text: teṣu sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snātvā datvā yathepsitaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having bathed at all those <s>tīrthas</s>, having given as desired,

children.text: yathāvidhi samādhāya vrataṃ cara samāhitaḥ // SvayambhuP_9.12 //
children.translated_text: he settled according to the prescribed method and observed the vow in concentration. // SvayambhuP_9.12 //
Then, having seen the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> (passionless ones), he was delighted,
and having propitiated them according to the prescribed method, worshipped and always served them. // SvayambhuP_9.13 //
Then he propitiated the great goddess, the supreme lady with a bird's face,
and having worshipped her according to the prescribed method, served her joyfully. // SvayambhuP_9.14 //
Then, having beheld the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, he was delighted,
and having worshipped it according to the prescribed method, he served it reverently. // SvayambhuP_9.15 //
Then, by the power of those great merits, <s>Śāntaśrī</s>, his senses purified,

children.text: pravajyā saṃvaraṃ dhṛtvā brahmacārī babhūva saḥ // SvayambhuP_9.16 //
children.translated_text: having taken the vow of renunciation (<s>pravrajyā saṃvara</s>), became a <s>Brahmacārin</s> (celibate practitioner). // SvayambhuP_9.16 //
Because his six senses were beautifully adorned with supreme peaceful glory,

children.text: taṃ nanāma prasiddhaṃ ca śāntaśrīrityabhūdyataḥ // SvayambhuP_9.17 //
children.translated_text: he was bowed to, and became well-known as '<s>Śāntaśrī</s>' (Peaceful Glory). // SvayambhuP_9.17 //
Then that one of true wisdom, the discerning <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the welfare of the world,
having received the <s>Vajracaryā</s> (diamond practice) vow, traveled about in concentration. // SvayambhuP_9.18 //
Then, having covered this <s>Dharmadhātu Jina</s> with stone,
fashioning a great <s>stūpa</s> with bricks, he concealed it. // SvayambhuP_9.19 //
Then five deities were established in the five cities here,
and this <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> was also greatly made by him. // SvayambhuP_9.20 //

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvātra kāryāṇi sarvāṇi sa mahāmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus accomplished all the tasks here, that one of great wisdom,
a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of great supernatural knowledge, conducted himself for the welfare of the world. // SvayambhuP_9.21 //
Then, having pacified the great calamity everywhere,
<s>Śāntaśrī</s> always established the celebration of auspicious glory. // SvayambhuP_9.22 //
Then that one of great supernatural knowledge, when drought occurred,
having propitiated the <s>Nāga</s> kings, brought about good rainfall. // SvayambhuP_9.23 //
Thus, he of threefold supernatural knowledge, the pacifier of great calamities,

children.text: śubhaṃkara sadā tena śāntikare iti smṛtaḥ // SvayambhuP_9.24 //
children.translated_text: always doing good — by that he was known as '<s>Śāntikara</s>' (peacemaker). // SvayambhuP_9.24 //
Such a <s>mantrin</s> (master of mantras), of great supernatural knowledge, a <s>Vajrācārya</s> of great wisdom,

children.text: samṛddhisiddhisaṃpannā na bhūtā na bhaviṣyati // SvayambhuP_9.25 //
children.translated_text: endowed with prosperity and accomplishment — neither has existed nor shall exist. // SvayambhuP_9.25 //
Having thus established everywhere a calamity-free, auspicious celebration,
that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śāntaśrī</s> became honored in the three worlds. // SvayambhuP_9.26 //
Thus, understanding his great merit, the means to the virtues of auspicious glory,

children.text: vijñāya śaraṇaṃ gatvā savitavyaṃ śubhārthibhiḥ // SvayambhuP_9.27 //
children.translated_text: having gone to his refuge, seekers of auspiciousness should serve him. // SvayambhuP_9.27 //
If, having gone to his refuge and approached with faith,

children.text: yathāvidhi samārādhya bhajeyuḥ sarvadā mudā // SvayambhuP_9.28 //
children.translated_text: they worship according to the prescribed method, always joyfully — // SvayambhuP_9.28 //
they all, of pure souls, free from afflictions, with conquered senses,
shall attain the wealth of the qualities of auspicious glory, prosperity, and accomplishment. // SvayambhuP_9.29 //

children.text: ye ca tasya sadā smṛtvā dhyātvāpi ca samāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those who, always remembering and meditating upon him with concentration,

children.text: nāmāpi ca samuccārya bhajeyuḥ śraddhayā sadā // SvayambhuP_9.30 //
children.translated_text: and even uttering his name, worship always with faith — // SvayambhuP_9.30 //
they too, all freed from blemish, purified in the three spheres,
endowed with his qualities and glory, shall become practitioners of the path to <s>Bodhi</s>. // SvayambhuP_9.31 //
Thus, understanding his great merit, those who desire his qualities,

children.text: tasyaiva śaraṇaṃ gatvā bhajantu te sadā mudā // SvayambhuP_9.32 //
children.translated_text: having gone to his refuge, should worship always joyfully. // SvayambhuP_9.32 //
Thus instructed by the great sage, all those assembled in the court,
the beings, acknowledging 'so be it,' were delighted and enlightened. // SvayambhuP_9.33 //

body.translated_text: Thus that great being, bearing the purpose of auspicious glory and good qualities,

body.text: sarvasattvahitaṃ kṛtvā saṃtasthe suciraṃ tathā // SvayambhuP_9.34 //
body.translated_text: having done what was beneficial for all beings, remained thus for a long time. // SvayambhuP_9.34 //

children.translated_text: Then, when time had passed, the king, old, with decrepit senses,
free from afflictions, dispassionate, meditating, reflected thus: // SvayambhuP_9.35 //
"I am old, with limbs exceedingly decrepit; how long shall I remain thus?

children.text: avaśyaṃ daivayogeṇa yāsyāmi maraṇaṃ dhruvaṃ // SvayambhuP_9.36 //
children.translated_text: Surely, by the force of destiny, I shall inevitably meet death. // SvayambhuP_9.36 //
Therefore I should now give this kingdom, together with its consecration,
to my young son for the protection of the people." // SvayambhuP_9.37 //
Having thus reflected, that lord of the earth consecrated his son <s>Narendradeva</s>,
making him king, and enlightening him, he instructed thus: // SvayambhuP_9.38 //
"O king, my son, having settled and conducting yourself by the law of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: triratnabhajanaṃ kṛtvā saṃcarasva sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_9.39 //
children.translated_text: performing worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), always conduct yourself in auspiciousness. // SvayambhuP_9.39 //
From today, you are the lord and ruler of all beings,
the instructor in all <s>Dharma</s>, and the bearer of the welfare of all beings. // SvayambhuP_9.40 //
Therefore, protecting all beings here by the law of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: triratnabhajanaṃ kṛtvā saṃcaraṃsva sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_9.41 //
children.translated_text: performing worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), always conduct yourself in auspiciousness." // SvayambhuP_9.41 //
Having thus instructed his son, that father, free from desire for worldly existence,
having renounced all possessions, took to the forest-dwelling life. // SvayambhuP_9.42 //
Dwelling there, that one of great supernatural knowledge, purified in the three spheres,
with his mind established in <s>samādhi</s>, he practiced the <s>Brahma</s> vow. // SvayambhuP_9.43 //

children.text: tataḥ kāle gate mṛtyusamaye sa samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, when time had passed, at the moment of death, he, composed,

children.text: triratnaṃ sa smaraṃstyaktvā dehaṃ yayau sukhāvatīṃ // SvayambhuP_9.44 //
children.translated_text: remembering the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), having abandoned the body, went to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Pure Land of Bliss). // SvayambhuP_9.44 //

children.text: tataḥ sa nṛpatī rājā narendradeva indravat /
children.translated_text: Then that lord of men, King <s>Narendradeva</s>, like <s>Indra</s>,
awakening the people with effort, protected all the worlds.
That king too, of purified soul, devoted to the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: śāntikaraṃ tamācārya sametya śaraṇaṃ yayau // SvayambhuP_9.46 //
children.translated_text: approached the teacher <s>Śāntikara</s> and went to him for refuge.
There, having taken refuge, bearing the teacher's command upon his head,

children.text: triratnabhajanaṃ kṛtvā prācarat sarvadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_9.47 //
children.translated_text: having performed worship of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), he always conducted himself in auspiciousness.

children.text: sadā sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi /
children.translated_text: Always at all the sacred fords (<s>tīrthas</s>), having bathed according to the prescribed method,
he gave <s>piṇḍa</s> (offering) to the ancestors, and to supplicants as they desired.
Likewise, the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> (passionless ones) and also the lords of the <s>Kṣatra</s> world,

children.text: yathāvidhi samārādhya samārcayat sa parvasuḥ // SvayambhuP_9.49 //
children.translated_text: having propitiated and worshipped according to the prescribed method, he honored them on festival days.
Likewise the glorious great goddess, the bird-faced one, according to the prescribed method,
having propitiated and worshipped, he served with great enthusiasm and joy.
Likewise at the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, approaching its foremost seat,
having propitiated and worshipped according to the prescribed method, he always served.
Likewise at <s>Vāyupura</s> (City of Wind), the <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) deities together with their retinues,
having propitiated and worshipped according to the prescribed method, he always served.
Likewise at <s>Vahnipura</s> (City of Fire), the <s>Vahni</s> (Fire) deities together with their retinues,
having propitiated and worshipped according to the prescribed method, he always served.
Likewise at <s>Nāgapura</s> (City of Nāgas), the <s>Nāga</s> deities together with their retinues,
having propitiated and worshipped according to the prescribed method, he always served.
Likewise at <s>Vasupura</s> (City of Wealth), the goddess <s>Vasudhārā</s> together with her <s>maṇḍala</s>,
having propitiated and worshipped according to the prescribed method, he always served.
Likewise at <s>Śāntipura</s> (City of Peace), the glorious <s>Saṃvara</s>, the <s>Jina</s>, together with his retinue,
having propitiated and worshipped according to the prescribed method, he always served.

children.text: tathā tasya dharmadhātoḥ sa narendraḥ samupāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, that lord of men, having taken refuge at that <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
having propitiated according to the prescribed method, always worshipped and served.
Thus that lord of men, the king, devoted to the virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: triratnabhajanaṃ kṛtvā saṃprācarat sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_9.58 //
children.translated_text: having performed worship of the Three Jewels, always conducted himself in auspiciousness.
Thus that king, in these rites of pilgrimage to <s>tīrthas</s> and the rest,

children.text: bodhayitvā prayatnena sarvān lokān yayā jayat // SvayambhuP_9.59 //
children.translated_text: having awakened all the people with effort, went forth victoriously.

children.text: tathā sarve 'pi te lokā dhṛtvā nṛpānuśāsanaṃ /
children.translated_text: Likewise all those people too, upholding the king's instruction,
engaged in these rites of pilgrimage to <s>tīrthas</s> and the rest.
Likewise the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s>, the bird-faced goddess too,

children.text: pañcaitā devatāścāpi caityaṃ mañjuśriyo 'pi ca // SvayambhuP_9.61 //
children.translated_text: and also these five deities, and the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> too,
the lord of the world, the protector of the world, the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>—

children.text: yathāvidhi samabhyarcya prābhajanta sadā mudā // SvayambhuP_9.62 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped according to the prescribed method, they always served with joy.
By the power of this <s>Dharma</s>, always auspiciousness here,
free from calamity, with great enthusiasm, prevailed on all sides.

children.text: evaṃ sa nṛpatī rājā narendra deva ātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus that lord of men, King <s>Narendradeva</s>,

children.text: bodhicaryāḥ vrataṃ dhṛtvā saṃpracara jagaddhite // SvayambhuP_9.64 //
children.translated_text: holding the vow of the conduct of <s>Bodhi</s>, conducted himself for the welfare of the world.

children.text: parānapi tathā sarvān lokān yatnena bodhayan /
children.translated_text: Awakening all the others, all the people, with effort,
having joined them to the path of <s>Bodhi</s>, he set them forth for the welfare of the world.

children.text: evaṃ sa indravad rāja bodhisattvā jagatprabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus that king, like <s>Indra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, lord of the world,

children.text: sarvasattvahitaṃ kṛtvā tasthau ciraṃ śubhe raman // SvayambhuP_9.66 //
children.translated_text: having done what benefits all beings, remained long, delighting in auspiciousness.

children.text: tataḥ śrīmān sa ācāryaḥ śāntikaro maharddhikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the glorious teacher <s>Śāntikara</s>, of great supernatural power,
having accomplished his purpose, though advanced in age, did not desire to pass into <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.
Desiring the welfare of all beings, below the summit of <s>Śāntipura</s>,
in a splendid meditation chamber, of the measure of one sacrificial ground,
having raised the great banner of <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (Wish-fulfilling Jewel) upon a glorious great blaze,

children.text: sa prājñaḥ sa mahāsattvo bodhisattvā jinātmajaḥ // SvayambhuP_9.69 //
children.translated_text: that wise one, that great being, <s>Bodhisattva</s>, son of the <s>Jina</s>,
absorbed in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>dhāraṇī</s>, <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>yoga</s>, and <s>dhyāna</s>,
holding the aspiration for perfect awakening (<s>Sambodhipraṇidhi</s>), remained with a steadfast mind.
When the true <s>Dharma</s> declines here, and the world is afflicted by the five degenerations (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>),

children.text: tadotthāya samādheḥ sa saddharmma deśayiṣyati // SvayambhuP_9.71 //
children.translated_text: then he will arise from <s>samādhi</s> and teach the true <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: yadā yadātra satmitraḥ śāstrā vidyādhipā na hi /
children.translated_text: Whenever there is no true spiritual friend, teacher, or lord of knowledge here,

children.text: tadā tadā na sanmitraḥ śāstrāvidyādhipobhavan // SvayambhuP_9.72 //
children.translated_text: then and then he will become the true friend, teacher, and lord of knowledge.
Having turned all people away from the path of evil, with effort,
having established them on the path of <s>Bodhi</s>, he will set them forth in the true <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: evaṃ dhyātvā sa ācāryaḥ śāntikaraḥ samādhibhṛt /
children.translated_text: Thus, having meditated, that teacher <s>Śāntikara</s>, bearing <s>samādhi</s>,
for the welfare of all beings, remained absorbed in <s>yoga</s>.
Thus that teacher of the three virtues, bearing the welfare of all beings,
a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of great supernatural knowledge, abides there for the welfare of the world.

children.text: ye tasya śaraṇaṃ gatvā smṛtvā dhyātvā samādarāt /
children.translated_text: Those who go to him for refuge, remembering and meditating with respect,

children.text: nāmāpi ca samuccāryaṃ bhajanti śraddhayā sadā // SvayambhuP_9.76 //
children.translated_text: and even uttering his name, worship with faith always—
they too, all of great supernatural knowledge, discerning <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,
endowed with the qualities of auspicious glory, shall always be so in every existence.
Then they, of pure souls, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
holding the vow of the conduct of <s>Bodhi</s>, shall conduct themselves for the welfare of the world.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,

children.text: arhanto bodhimāsādya prāpsyanti saugataṃ padaṃ // SvayambhuP_9.79 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, shall reach the state of a <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: ye ca tadguṇamāhātmyaṃ śṛṇvanti śraddhayā mudā /
children.translated_text: And those who hear of the greatness of his qualities with faith and joy—

children.text: te 'pi tadguṇa saṃpatti saṃsiddhiṃ samavāpnuyuḥ // SvayambhuP_9.80 //
children.translated_text: they too shall attain the accomplishment of the wealth of those qualities.
Thus, understanding this, whoever desires the wealth of his qualities,
they should listen to the greatness of his good qualities with respect.
Having heard this instruction given by the lord of sages, all those assembled in the court,
the people, affirming 'so be it,' rejoiced, being awakened.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter, named 'The Declaration of the Greatness and Power of the Accomplishment of the Qualities of the Glorious Great Teacher Śāntikara.'
Tenth Chapter: named 'The Well-Spoken Sūtra of the Greatness of the Dharma of the Origin of the Glorious Dharmadhātu Svayambhū.'

children.text: athāsau bhagavān bhūyo maitreyaṃ taṃ mahāmatiṃ /
children.translated_text: Then that Blessed One, again, addressing <s>Maitreya</s>, that one of great wisdom,
and looking upon the assembly, summoned them and instructed thus:
"Listen, <s>Maitreya</s>, I shall tell of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the teacher of the world—
the greatness of the qualities of the true <s>Dharma</s>, bestowing the knowledge of perfect awakening.
Here, this nun <s>Cūḍā</s>, of good conduct, a practitioner of <s>brahmacarya</s>,

children.text: idaṃ mañjuśriyaṃ ścaityaṃ śraddhayā samupāśritā // SvayambhuP_10.3 //
children.translated_text: has approached this <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> with faith.
Always having worshipped with pure blue lotus garlands according to the prescribed method,

children.text: smṛtvā dhyātvā samārādhya sabhaktyā śraddhayā sadā // SvayambhuP_10.4 //
children.translated_text: remembering, meditating, propitiating, with devotion and faith always,

children.text: ādyāṃ cale cule vande svāheti navamākṣaraṃ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ādyāṃ cale cule vande svāhā</s>'—these nine syllables,

children.text: dhāraṇī paramāvidyāṃ paṭhantī bhajane sadā // SvayambhuP_10.5 //
children.translated_text: the supreme <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) <s>dhāraṇī</s>, she recites in worship always.
By the power of this merit, this nun <s>Cūḍā</s>, a virtuous one,
shall surely become endowed with the five supernatural powers (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>) within twelve years.
Then she, of great supernatural knowledge, the abode of the wealth of glorious qualities,
having done what benefits all beings, shall practice the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s> (Bodhisattva vow).
Then, as a female <s>Arhat</s>, of great wisdom, purified in the three spheres,
having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, she shall reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.
Thus, other people too, at the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> in the three times,

children.text: paṭhantī dhāraṇīmenāṃ bhajanti śraddhayā sadā // SvayambhuP_10.9 //
children.translated_text: reciting this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, worship with faith always—
they too, all freed from blemish, purified in the three spheres,
the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> with conquered senses,
having attained the state of the five supernatural powers, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
bearing the welfare of all beings, shall practice the <s>Bodhisaṃvara</s>.
Then they, having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in proper order,

children.text: jitvā māragaṇān sarvān niḥkleśā vimalendriyāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.12 //
children.translated_text: having conquered all the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, free from afflictions, of pure senses,
as <s>Arhats</s> too, of great supernatural knowledge, devoted to the practice of perfect awakening,
having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, would reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.
You too, understanding this, at the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> likewise,
reciting this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, worship with minds set on <s>Bodhi</s>.
Anointed by this merit, purified in the three spheres,

children.text: yūyamapi tathā sarve bhaveta sugatātmajāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.15 //
children.translated_text: you too, all of you likewise, shall become sons of the <s>Sugata</s>.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the abode of auspicious glory and good qualities,
of great supernatural knowledge, lords of the world, you shall become practitioners of auspicious conduct.
Then, having fulfilled the accumulations for perfect awakening in proper order,
having conquered all the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
as <s>Arhats</s>, having attained the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, you shall become <s>Buddhas</s>.

children.text: iti satyaṃ parijñāya yadi saṃbodhimicchatha // SvayambhuP_10.18 //
children.translated_text: Having truly understood this, if you desire perfect awakening,
at this <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, worship always with joy."

children.text: ityādiṣṭaṃ munīndreṇa niśamya te sasāṃdhikāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.19 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction given by the lord of sages, those together with the assembly,
all the people, saying 'so be it,' rejoiced, being awakened.

children.text: tataḥ sarve 'pi te lokā brahmāśakrādayo 'marāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.20 //
children.translated_text: Then all those people, the immortals led by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>,
and all the lords of the worlds too, together with their attendants, joyfully,

children.text: bhagavantaṃ munīndraṃ taṃ sasaṃgha saṃprasāditāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.21 //
children.translated_text: being pleased with that Blessed One, lord of sages, together with his <s>Saṅgha</s>,

children.text: natvā pradakṣiṇī kṛtvā svasvālayaṃ mudā yayuḥ /
children.translated_text: having bowed and circumambulated, went joyfully to their own abodes.
All the mortals, kings and others, together with ministers, people, and townsmen,

children.text: sasāṃdhikaṃ munīndraṃ taṃ natvā svasvālayaṃ yayuḥ /
children.translated_text: having bowed to that lord of sages with his assembly, went to their own abodes.
<s>Hārītī</s>, the <s>Yakṣiṇī</s> too, together with her children, the protectress of the Buddhists,
having performed worship of the Three Jewels, took refuge at the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sa bhagavāṃścāpi samutthāya sasāṃdhikaḥ // SvayambhuP_10.24 //
children.translated_text: Then that Blessed One too, rising, together with his assembly,
illuminating the world with his radiance, went to the hermitage of <s>Jaṭodyāna</s>.

children.text: tatra sa trijagannātho vihāre sahasāṃdhikaiḥ // SvayambhuP_10.25 //
children.translated_text: There, that lord of the three worlds, at the monastery with his assembly,
having taught the true <s>Dharma</s>, dwelt for the welfare of the world.

children.text: iti te guruṇādiṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ mayā tathocyate // SvayambhuP_10.26 //
children.translated_text: "Thus what was taught by my <s>Guru</s>, I heard, and so it is told.
Having heard this, O great king, rejoice with faith."

children.text: iti śāstrārhatādiṣṭaṃ niśamya sa narādhipaḥ // SvayambhuP_10.27 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction given by the worthy teacher, that lord of men,
being pleased, having bowed to that <s>Arhat</s>, spoke thus with respect:

children.text: bhadantohaṃ samicchāmi saṃdraṣṭuṃ taṃ svayaṃbhuvaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.28 //
children.translated_text: "Venerable one, I desire to see that <s>Svayambhū</s> (the Self-Existent).
Therefore I shall go to <s>Naipāla</s> (Nepal)—grant me your permission."

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ rājñā śrutvā sorhanyatirmudā // SvayambhuP_10.29 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this request from the king, that <s>Arhat</s> ascetic, with joy,
looking upon that king, that great being, instructed thus:

children.text: sādhu rājan samicchā te yadyasti taṃ svayambhuvaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.30 //
children.translated_text: "Well done, O King! If your desire exists to see that <s>Svayambhū</s>,
go, having propitiated, worship with faith.

children.text: sarvatīrtheṣu ca snātvā datvā dānaṃ yathepsitaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.31 //
children.translated_text: Having bathed at all the sacred fords, having given charity as desired,
having propitiated and worshipped the <s>Vītarāgas</s> with respect—
the goddess <s>Dharmodayā</s>, the great goddess, the bird-faced queen of the <s>Jinas</s>,
having approached with faith, having worshipped, serve her with reverence.
The five deities established in the five cities, according to the proper rites,
having propitiated and worshipped, serve them with devotion and reverence.

children.text: mañjudevasya caityaṃ ca samālokya yathāvidhi // SvayambhuP_10.34 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjudeva</s>, having beheld it according to the proper rites,
having propitiated and worshipped, serve it reciting the <s>dhāraṇī</s>.
And the teacher seated in the cave, established in the meditation of <s>samādhi</s>,
having meditated upon, propitiated, worshipped, and bowed to, serve him with reverence.
Likewise other great beings, devotees of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,
having propitiated and worshipped all of them, bow down before them.
Purified in soul by this merit, a repository of auspicious glory and good qualities,
you shall become a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a great being, the protector of the world.
Then, having fulfilled the accumulations for perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>) in proper order,
as an <s>Arhat</s>, attaining <s>Sambodhi</s>, you shall reach the state of a fully awakened <s>Sambuddha</s>.

children.text: iti satyaṃ parijñāya saṃbodhi yadi vāñchasi // SvayambhuP_10.39 //
children.translated_text: Thus, knowing this truth, if you desire perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>),
go there and with great enthusiasm, behold that <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,
having propitiated it according to the proper rites, serve it, having taken refuge.

children.text: gaccha te maṅgalaṃ bhuyāt sidhyatu te samīhitaṃ /
children.translated_text: Go! May auspiciousness be yours! May your desire be fulfilled!
Having seen as you wish, return delighted."

children.text: iti śāstrā samādiṣṭaṃ śrutvā sa nṛpatirmudā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction given by the teacher, that king joyfully,
bowing to that <s>Guru</s> with palms joined, having received permission, was delighted.
Then that sovereign king, together with ministers, people, and citizens,
set out with royal splendor and auspicious enthusiasm, proceeding joyfully.

children.text: tatra mārge sa rājendraḥ sarvān lokān prasādayan /
children.translated_text: On the way, that chief of kings, pleasing all the people,
proceeding with great enthusiasm, quickly arrived at <s>Naipāla</s> (Nepal).

children.text: tatra prāptaḥ samālokya dūrāt taṃ śrīsvayaṃmbhuvaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having arrived there, beholding from afar that glorious <s>Svayambhū</s>,

children.text: sāñjali praṇatiṃ kṛtvā pramanāḥ sahasā caret // SvayambhuP_10.45 //
children.translated_text: making a prostration with palms joined, he went forward eagerly, with a joyful mind.
There, seeing everywhere the auspicious celebration that was taking place,
that king, amazed and delighted, approached.

children.text: tatra sarveṣu tīrtheṣu krameṇa sa narādhipaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, at all the <s>tīrthas</s> in sequence, that lord of men,

children.text: snātvārthibhyo yathākāmaṃ dadau dānaṃ caran vrataṃ // SvayambhuP_10.47 //
children.translated_text: having bathed, gave charity to supplicants as desired, practicing the vow.
Then, beholding the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> (dispassionate ones), that king was delighted,
and having propitiated them according to the proper rites, worshipped and served them duly.
Then, proceeding joyfully, beholding the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
having propitiated and worshipped it according to the proper rites, he served it in due order.
Then at <s>Vāyupura</s> (the City of Wind), the deity of <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) together with its retinue, joyfully,
having propitiated according to the proper rites, he worshipped and served it.
Then at <s>Agnipura</s> (the City of Fire), the deity of <s>Agni</s> (Fire) together with its retinue also,
having propitiated according to the proper rites, he worshipped and served it with reverence.
Then at <s>Nāgapura</s> (the City of Serpents), the <s>Nāga</s> deity together with its retinue also,
having propitiated according to the proper rites, he worshipped and served it with joy.
Then at <s>Vasupura</s> (the City of Wealth), the goddess <s>Śrī Vasundharā</s> (Earth Goddess) together with her retinue,
having propitiated according to the proper rites, he worshipped and served her with reverence.
Then at <s>Śāntipura</s> (the City of Peace), the glorious <s>Saṃvara</s> together with his retinue likewise,
having propitiated according to the proper rites, he worshipped and served him with joy.
Then the <s>Śāntikarācārya</s> (the Peace-Making Teacher), established in the meditation of <s>samādhi</s>,
having meditated upon, propitiated, and worshipped him, he served him with great delight.
Then the goddess <s>Dharmodayā</s>, the bird-faced <s>Maheśvarī</s>,
having propitiated and worshipped according to the proper rites, he served her with joy.
"I bow to the fully awakened one, the lotus-eyed, the omniscient, the abode of compassion,
the teacher <s>Samantabhadra</s>, <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>).
I bow to <s>Śrīghana</s> (Dense with Glory), <s>Śrīmān</s> (the Glorious), the supreme, the mass of virtue, the maker of auspiciousness,

children.text: śrīmantaṃ śrīkaraṃ śāntaṃ śāntimūrti namāmyaham // SvayambhuP_10.58 //
children.translated_text: the glorious, the maker of glory, the peaceful, the embodiment of peace.
I bow to the lion who teaches the doctrine of <s>Nairātmya</s> (non-self), the faultless, the one without outflows (<s>nirāśrava</s>),
the knower of right conduct, the pure in soul, the spotless.
I bow to the one beyond duality, free from ego, beyond conceptualization, the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
who has shaken off all afflictions, the one beyond elaboration.
I bow to the lord of the universe, the distinguished, the one of universal form, the guide (<s>Vināyaka</s>),
complete with all the marks of the universe, the <s>Vītarāga</s> (dispassionate one).
I bow to the one endowed with the supreme method, the lord of all, of pure radiance,
of subdued impulse, pure, free from delusion.
I bow to the tamer of the difficult to tame, the peaceful, the pure, the abode of the five <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: sugatiṃ suśrutaṃ saumyaṃ śubhrakīrtti namāmyahaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.63 //
children.translated_text: the one of good destination, well-heard, gentle, of bright fame.
I bow to the lord of <s>yogins</s>, possessed of the ten powers, the knower of the world, worshipped by the world,
the teacher of the world, the embodiment of the world, the protector of the world.
I bow to the one freed from blemish, the enemy of desire, the sole one of all arts, the bearer of arts,
of beautiful form, the vessel of compassion, of golden radiance."
Then, having approached the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjuśrī</s> and the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,
having propitiated and worshipped according to the proper rites, he served it with bowing.

children.text: tato mudā caran vīkṣya dharmadhātuṃ jinālayaṃ /
children.translated_text: Then, proceeding joyfully, beholding the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,
having propitiated and worshipped it according to the proper rites, he served it with joy.
With supreme devotion he praised the abode of the <s>Jina</s>, the self-existent (<s>Svayambhū</s>):

children.text: jyotīrūpāya caitanyaṃ rūpāya bhavate namaḥ // SvayambhuP_10.68 //
children.translated_text: "Homage to you, who are of luminous form, of conscious form.
Homage to you, the destroyer of <s>Mura</s> and others, the bestower of <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), of the form of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ),
of the form facing all directions, O you who are affectionate to devotees.
Homage to you, the creator of the elements beginning with earth, venerated by the world;

children.text: jagatsraṣṭe jagatpātre jagaddhartre namo namaḥ // SvayambhuP_10.70 //
children.translated_text: salutation upon salutation to the creator of the world, the vessel of the world, the sustainer of the world.
To the one attainable through meditation, the object of meditation, the bestower of the four goals (<s>caturvarga</s>)."

children.text: evaṃ stutvā aśokaḥ sa punaḥ kṣamāpanaṃ vyadhāt // SvayambhuP_10.71 //
children.translated_text: Having thus praised, <s>Aśoka</s> then made a prayer of forgiveness.
Thus that king, having worshipped all the devotees of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,
the great beings, he honored them and made them content.
Thus that sovereign king, having taken refuge in the glorious <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,
having performed worship of the Three Jewels, practiced the <s>Bodhi</s> vow (<s>saṃvara</s>).
Then that delighted king, together with ministers, people, and citizens,
having bowed and circumambulated the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, proceeded joyfully.
Then, proceeding, that lord of the earth, with great enthusiasm and delight,
quickly arrived at the city and approached the monastery.
There, having come to that <s>Arhat</s> <s>Upagupta</s> together with his assembly,
beholding him, bowing with palms joined, he took a secluded seat in the assembly.
Seeing him arrived, that <s>Arhat</s> teacher, with a pleased gaze,
asked the king: 'Welcome! Is all well?'

children.text: tacchutvā sa mahīpālaḥ śāstāraṃ taṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king, with palms joined to the teacher,
bowing, with a supremely serene face, looking at him, spoke thus:
"I have returned, O Teacher, by the power of your compassion.

children.text: kuśalaṃ me kathaṃ na syāt sarvatrāpi sadāpi hi // SvayambhuP_10.79 //
children.translated_text: How could I not be well, everywhere and always?
By the power of your compassion, I went joyfully in <s>Nepāla</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snātvā dānaṃ yathepsitaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.80 //
children.translated_text: and having seen and bathed at all the <s>tīrthas</s>, I gave charity as desired.
Likewise, having beheld the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s>, delighted,
having propitiated according to the proper rites, I worshipped and served them in due order.
Then, beholding that glorious <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the self-existent (<s>Svayambhū</s>),
having propitiated and worshipped it according to the proper rites, I served it with joy.
Then at <s>Vāyupura</s>, the <s>Vāyu</s> deity was worshipped by me;
then at <s>Agnipura</s>, the <s>Agni</s> deity too was worshipped by me.
Likewise at <s>Nāgapura</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> kings were worshipped by me;

children.text: tathā tathā vasupure devī vasundharāṃ samarccitā // SvayambhuP_10.84 //
children.translated_text: likewise at <s>Vasupura</s>, the goddess <s>Vasundharā</s> was worshipped by me.
Then at <s>Śāntipura</s>, the glorious <s>Saṃvara</s> was worshipped;
then the <s>Śāntikarācārya</s>, having been beheld, was worshipped by me.
The bird-faced goddess too, having been propitiated, was worshipped;

children.text: mañjudevasya caityaṃ ca yathāvidhi samarcitaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.86 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjudeva</s> was worshipped according to the proper rites.
Thus, O Venerable One, there at <s>Upachandoha</s>, the meritorious sacred land,
all the deities were worshipped by me according to the proper rites.
This merit was obtained by me through the power of your compassion;

children.text: tadatra janmasāphalyaṃ jīvitaṃ cāpi me 'dhunā // SvayambhuP_10.88 //
children.translated_text: therefore my birth and life now have become fruitful.
And always, O Teacher, I shall remember the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: smṛtvā nāma samuccārya dhyātvā bhajeya mā bhavaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.89 //
children.translated_text: uttering its name, meditating, and worshipping it throughout existence."

children.text: iti rājñā samākhyātaṃ śrutvā so 'rha prasāditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this account by the king, that <s>Arhat</s>, pleased,

children.text: nṛpati taṃ samālokya punarevaṃ samādiśat // SvayambhuP_10.90 //
children.translated_text: looking at that king, again instructed thus:
"Blessed are you, O great king, that you wish to remember, meditate upon, and worship

children.text: smṛtvā dhyātvāpi saṃbhaktuṃmicchase 'tra sadā bhaja // SvayambhuP_10.91 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the abode of the <s>Jina</s>. Always serve it here.
Purified in soul by this merit, a repository of auspicious glory and good qualities,
you shall become a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a great being, lord of all <s>Dharma</s>.
Then, having fulfilled the accumulations for perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>) in proper order,
as an <s>Arhat</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, you shall certainly obtain the state of <s>Buddhahood</s>.
By merely hearing the origin narrative of that <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the self-existent (<s>Svayambhū</s>),
one would obtain great merit, the means to perfect enlightenment (<s>Sambodhi</s>).
Therefore, understanding this, the origin narrative of that <s>Svayambhū</s>,

children.text: satkṛtya śraddhayā martyāḥ śrotumarhanti sarvathā // SvayambhuP_10.95 //
children.translated_text: mortals should hear it in all ways, with respect and faith.
Those people who hear the origin narrative of that <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the self-existent,

children.text: śṛṇvanti ye narā bhaktyā satkṛtya śraddhayā mudā // SvayambhuP_10.96 //
children.translated_text: with devotion, with respect, with faith, and with joy—

children.text: durgatiṃ te na gacchanti kutrāpi hi kadācan /
children.translated_text: they never go to bad destinies, nowhere, never;
always born in good destinies, they are repositories of auspicious glory and good qualities.
Devoted to the vow of <s>Bodhicaryā</s>, established in the welfare of all beings,
of great superknowledge, lords of the world, they shall become sons of the <s>Sugata</s>.
Having fulfilled the accumulations for <s>Bodhi</s> in due order for the welfare of the world,

children.text: arhantatrividhāṃ bodhiṃ prāpyeyuḥ saugataṃ padaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.99 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Arhats</s>, attaining the threefold <s>Bodhi</s>, they shall reach the state of a <s>Sugata</s>.
Understanding this, O great king, one should hear with faith and reverence
the greatness of the qualities of <s>Svayambhū</s>, which is rare and sought by those who desire <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: śṛṇvanti ye narā bhaktyā satkṛtya śraddhayā mudā /
children.translated_text: Those people who hear with devotion, respect, faith, and joy
the greatness of the qualities of <s>Svayambhū</s>, which bestows the glorious virtues of the true <s>Dharma</s>—
they too shall not go to bad destinies, always associated with good destinies.
endowed with auspicious glory and good qualities, shall become attainers of <s>bodhi</s>. // SvayambhuP_10.102 //
Therefore, having heard of this great merit, having meditated always with reverence,

children.text: smṛtvā nāma samuccārya saṃbhaktavyaṃ svayaṃbhuvaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.103 //
children.translated_text: having remembered and uttered even the name, one should worship <s>Svayambhū</s>. // SvayambhuP_10.103 //
I too, O king, in former times, having heard of the account of the good qualities
of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> <s>Svayambhū</s>, became greatly delighted. // SvayambhuP_10.104 //
Then I quickly went there to <s>Nepāla</s>,

children.text: snātvā sarveṣu tīrtheṣu dadau dānaṃ yathepsitaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.105 //
children.translated_text: and having bathed at all the <s>tīrthas</s> (holy waters), gave charity as desired. // SvayambhuP_10.105 //
I propitiated and worshipped those eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> (dispassionate ones),

children.text: devīṃ khagānanāṃ cāpi samārādhya samarcitā // SvayambhuP_10.106 //
children.translated_text: and also propitiated and worshipped the <s>Devī</s> (goddess) with the bird-face. // SvayambhuP_10.106 //
I propitiated and worshipped the <s>caitya</s> of <s>Mañjudeva</s>,

children.text: pañca purā sthitā pañca devatāśca samarcitāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.107 //
children.translated_text: and the five deities established in the five cities were also worshipped. // SvayambhuP_10.107 //
Likewise, the <s>ācārya</s> <s>Śāntikara</s> was beheld and worshipped,
and then, having taken refuge at the <s>dharmadhātu</s> <s>Svayambhū</s>, // SvayambhuP_10.108 //

children.text: satkṛtya śraddhayā nityaṃ samārādhya mudā bhajaṃ /
children.translated_text: honoring it, always with faith, having propitiated it, I worshipped with joy;
thus, always taking refuge there as a devotee of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, // SvayambhuP_10.109 //
performing worship of the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels), I practiced the <s>bodhisaṃvara</s> (vow of enlightenment).
Purified in soul by this merit, with the three spheres completely purified, // SvayambhuP_10.110 //
I have now attained <s>bodhi</s> and become a son of the <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: iti vijñāya mānuṣyā vāñchanti ye sunirvṛtiṃ // SvayambhuP_10.111 //
children.translated_text: Thus, knowing this, those humans who desire supreme <s>nirvṛti</s> (liberation), // SvayambhuP_10.111 //

children.text: dharmadhātuṃ samārādhya bhajantu te sadā mudā /
children.translated_text: let them propitiate the <s>dharmadhātu</s> and worship always with joy,

children.text: smṛtvā dhyātvā ca nāmāpi samuccārya samādarāt // SvayambhuP_10.112 //
children.translated_text: having remembered, meditated, and even uttered the name with reverence, // SvayambhuP_10.112 //
having beheld and bowed, let them worship that abode of the <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: ye bhajanti sadā smṛtvā dhyātvā natvā jinālayaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.113 //
children.translated_text: Those who always worship, having remembered, meditated, and bowed to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>, // SvayambhuP_10.113 //
shall quickly attain <s>saṃbodhi</s> (perfect enlightenment) and reach the state of a <s>Saṃbuddha</s>.

children.text: iti satyaṃ samākhyātaṃ sarvairapi munīśvaraiḥ // SvayambhuP_10.114 //
children.translated_text: Thus has the truth been declared by all the lords of sages; // SvayambhuP_10.114 //
having heard and rejoiced, remembering that <s>dharmadhātu</s>, let them worship abundantly.
Those too who, having heard this well-spoken teaching, rejoice in their hearts, // SvayambhuP_10.115 //
remembering and meditating upon the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, worship always —
they too, by the great merit of this, with the three spheres completely purified, // SvayambhuP_10.116 //
the foundation of auspicious glory and good qualities, abiding in the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes),
<s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, of great supernatural knowledge, with auspicious senses, // SvayambhuP_10.117 //
shall quickly attain <s>saṃbodhi</s> and reach the state of a <s>Saṃbuddha</s>.

children.text: iti me guruṇādiṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ mayā tathocyate // SvayambhuP_10.118 //
children.translated_text: Thus was it instructed by my <s>guru</s>, heard by me, and so it is told. // SvayambhuP_10.118 //
You too, having always made the people hear this, rejoice.
By the power of this merit, everywhere and always for you, // SvayambhuP_10.119 //
there shall surely be freedom from calamity and auspicious zeal, O lord of men."

children.text: iti tenārhatādiṣṭaṃ śrutvāśoko nṛpo mudā // SvayambhuP_10.120 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction of the <s>arhat</s>, King <s>Aśoka</s>, with joy, // SvayambhuP_10.120 //
assenting 'so be it,' rejoiced with his assembly.

children.text: tataḥ sarve 'pi te lokā niśamyaitatsubhāṣitaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.121 //
children.translated_text: Then all those people too, having heard this well-spoken teaching, // SvayambhuP_10.121 //
rejoicing, with great zeal, always conducted themselves in auspiciousness.
Then, by the power of that merit, everywhere and always there, // SvayambhuP_10.122 //
freedom from calamity and auspicious zeal prevailed without interruption.

children.text: ityādiśya mahābhijño jayaśrīḥ sa mahāmatiḥ // SvayambhuP_10.123 //
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed, <s>Jayaśrī</s>, that one of great supernatural knowledge and great wisdom, // SvayambhuP_10.123 //
looking upon all those companions, instructed again thus:
