"Wherever this sacred discourse on <s>dharma</s> is set forth, even in the <s>Kali</s> age, // SvayambhuP_10.124 //
whoever speaks it, hears it, causes others to hear it, or propagates it —

children.text: eteṣāṃ tatra sarveṣāṃ saṃbuddhāḥ sakalāḥ sadā // SvayambhuP_10.125 //
children.translated_text: for all of them, always, all the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s>, // SvayambhuP_10.125 //
looking upon them with compassionate eyes, shall bring about auspiciousness until the end of existence.

children.text: sarvā pāramitā devyasteṣāṃ tatra sadā śivaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.126 //
children.translated_text: All the <s>Pāramitā</s> (Perfection) goddesses shall always bring them welfare, // SvayambhuP_10.126 //
and fulfill their accumulations for <s>saṃbodhi</s> in due order.
All the <s>bodhisattvas</s> too, and the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), // SvayambhuP_10.127 //
and the <s>arhats</s> and yogins shall always bring them auspiciousness.

children.text: sarve lokādhipāścāpi sarve cāpi maharṣayaḥ // SvayambhuP_10.128 //
children.translated_text: All the lords of the worlds too, and all the great sages, // SvayambhuP_10.128 //

children.text: tatra teṣāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ kuryuḥ samīkṣya maṅgalaṃ /
children.translated_text: shall always, looking upon all of them, bring auspiciousness.
All the lords of the <s>devas</s> too, and all the lords of <s>daityas</s> (demons), // SvayambhuP_10.129 //
likewise all the <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians) and all the lords of <s>yakṣas</s>,
<s>garuḍas</s>, <s>Nāga</s> kings, and lords of <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd-shaped spirits) as well, // SvayambhuP_10.130 //

children.text: samīkṣya sarvadā teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kuryuḥ samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: shall always, looking upon them, provide protection on all sides.

children.text: sarvāśca mātṛkā devyaḥ sabhairavagaṇā api // SvayambhuP_10.131 //
children.translated_text: All the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (Mother) goddesses, together with the <s>Bhairava</s> hosts, // SvayambhuP_10.131 //

children.text: kṛtvā rakṣāṃ sadā teṣāṃ kuryurbhadraṃ samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: providing them protection always, shall bring auspiciousness on all sides.

children.text: sarve grahāśca tārāśca siddhā vidyādharā api // SvayambhuP_10.132 //
children.translated_text: All the planets, stars, <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings), and <s>vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-bearers), // SvayambhuP_10.132 //
and the <s>sādhyas</s> too, always looking upon them, shall bring great auspiciousness.
<s>Bhūtas</s> (spirits), <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>piśācas</s> (fiends), and even the wicked hosts of <s>Māra</s>, // SvayambhuP_10.133 //

children.text: vīkṣya teṣāṃ prasannāste rakṣāṃ kuryuḥ sadā mudā /
children.translated_text: looking upon them, with serene minds, shall always provide protection with joy.
Whoever with joy writes down this account of the greatness of <s>Svayambhū</s>'s qualities, // SvayambhuP_10.134 //
by that, all the well-spoken <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) teachings are written.
And whoever has caused this well-spoken teaching of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> to be written, // SvayambhuP_10.135 //

children.text: tenāpi sakalaṃ sūtraṃ lekhāpitaṃ bhaved dhruvaṃ /
children.translated_text: by that, the entire <s>sūtra</s> has surely been caused to be written.

children.text: likhitaṃ cāpi yecedaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yathāvidhi // SvayambhuP_10.136 //
children.translated_text: And those who, having written this, establish it according to proper rites, // SvayambhuP_10.136 //
placing it in a clean place or house, always worshipped with offerings —

children.text: tenārhanto jināḥ sarve pratyekasugatā api // SvayambhuP_10.137 //
children.translated_text: by that, the <s>arhats</s>, all the <s>Jinas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, // SvayambhuP_10.137 //
together with the <s>saṃgha</s> and the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, are indeed worshipped.

children.text: yaścāpīdaṃ svayaṃ dhṛtvā parebhyo 'pi samādiśat // SvayambhuP_10.138 //
children.translated_text: And whoever, having taken up this teaching, also instructs others, // SvayambhuP_10.138 //
contemplating it constantly, remembering, meditating, and bowing with joy —

children.text: tasya sarvamunīndro hi pratyekasugatā api // SvayambhuP_10.139 //
children.translated_text: for that person, all the lords of sages, and the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, // SvayambhuP_10.139 //
<s>arhats</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, pleased, shall grant what is desired.
Whoever, having worshipped the preacher of this teaching and all the listeners, // SvayambhuP_10.140 //
according to proper rites, satisfies them with offerings —

children.text: tena sarve 'pi saṃbuddhāḥ pratyekasugatā api // SvayambhuP_10.141 //
children.translated_text: by that, all the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, // SvayambhuP_10.141 //
<s>arhats</s>, all the <s>bhikṣus</s>, yogins, celibate practitioners,

children.text: bodhisattvāśca sarve 'pi vratino yatayo 'pi ca // SvayambhuP_10.142 //
children.translated_text: and all the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, those observing vows and ascetics as well, // SvayambhuP_10.142 //
are worshipped, fed, pleased, and gratified.

children.text: kimevaṃ vahunoktena sarve buddhā munīśvarāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.143 //
children.translated_text: Why say much? All the <s>Buddhas</s>, lords of sages, // SvayambhuP_10.143 //
all the <s>Tārā</s> goddesses, and all the <s>saṃghas</s>, sons of the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: nityaṃ teṣāṃ kṛpā dṛṣṭayā samālokyānumoditāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.144 //
children.translated_text: shall always look upon them with compassionate eyes, and being pleased, // SvayambhuP_10.144 //

body.text: rakṣāṃ vidhāya sarvatra varaṃ dadyuḥ samīhitaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.145 //
body.translated_text: providing protection everywhere, shall grant the desired boon. // SvayambhuP_10.145 //

children.translated_text: All the lords of the worlds too, all the <s>devas</s> and lords of the gods,

children.text: rakṣāṃ kṛtvā varaṃ dadyusteṣāṃ saddharmasādhane // SvayambhuP_10.146 //
children.translated_text: providing protection, shall grant them boons in the practice of the true <s>dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_10.146 //
Kings too shall always protect them and, being pleased,
granting whatever is desired, shall guard them always with reverence. // SvayambhuP_10.147 //
Ministers too shall always be their helpers, together with counselors, attendants, and followers,
with servants, soldiers, and officers — they shall be their benefactors. // SvayambhuP_10.148 //
All <s>vaiśyas</s> (merchants) too shall be providers of all wealth, dear friends,
and all the eminent ones and great people shall be their benefactors. // SvayambhuP_10.149 //
Even enemies shall become servants, and upon seeing them shall become well-intentioned;
thus other people too, all shall become of friendly disposition. // SvayambhuP_10.150 //
Animals, birds, all insects, and creatures

children.text: naiva teṣāṃ viruddhā syuḥ bhaveyurhitaśaṃsina // SvayambhuP_10.151 //
children.translated_text: shall never be hostile to them and shall be well-wishers. // SvayambhuP_10.151 //
Thus, everywhere in all worlds, for those practitioners of the true <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: nirutpātaṃ śubhotsāhaṃ saumāṅgalyaṃ sadā bhavet // SvayambhuP_10.152 //
children.translated_text: there shall always be freedom from calamity, auspicious zeal, and good fortune. // SvayambhuP_10.152 //
Thus, the most excellent merit arising from the abode of <s>Svayambhū</s> —

children.text: natvā taṃ trijagannāthaṃ bhajadhvaṃ sarvadā mudā // SvayambhuP_10.153 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to that lord of the three worlds, worship always with joy. // SvayambhuP_10.153 //

children.text: ye tasya śaraṇe sthitvā smṛtvā dhyātvā samāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, abiding in his refuge, having remembered and meditated with concentration,

children.text: nāmāpi ca samuccārya bhajanti śraddhayā sadā // SvayambhuP_10.154 //
children.translated_text: even uttering the name, worship always with faith — // SvayambhuP_10.154 //
for them, all three jewels, always well-disposed,

children.text: kṛpā dṛṣṭayā samālokya kṛtvā deyuḥ sadā śubhaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.155 //
children.translated_text: looking upon them with compassionate eyes, shall always grant auspiciousness. // SvayambhuP_10.155 //
Thus was it instructed by the teacher <s>Jayaśrī</s> and heard —

children.text: jineśvarī pramukhāḥ saṃghā sarve nandanprabodhitāḥ // SvayambhuP_10.156 //
children.translated_text: the communities headed by <s>Jineśvarī</s>, all were delighted and awakened. // SvayambhuP_10.156 //
The entire <s>Sarvāvatī</s> assembly too, having heard this, with serene minds,
assenting 'so be it,' rejoiced, being awakened. // SvayambhuP_10.157 //
Then all those people, rising up, with serene minds,

children.text: jayaśriya sasaṃghaṃ taṃ natvā svasvāśramaṃ yayuḥ // SvayambhuP_10.158 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to <s>Jayaśrī</s> together with his assembly, went to their respective hermitages. // SvayambhuP_10.158 //
There, always coming with great devotion, together with the assembly and sons of the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: snātvā sarveṣu tīrtheṣu dhṛtvā vrataṃ yathāvidhi // SvayambhuP_10.159 //
children.translated_text: having bathed at all the <s>tīrthas</s>, having undertaken vows according to proper rites, // SvayambhuP_10.159 //
then the eight <s>Vītarāgas</s> and also the <s>Devī</s> with the bird-face,
and the five deities too, were worshipped according to proper rites. // SvayambhuP_10.160 //
Likewise, the <s>caitya</s> of <s>ācārya</s> <s>Śāntikara</s> and also of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>,
having propitiated the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, meditating and worshipping, he always served it. // SvayambhuP_10.161 //
Then, by the power of that merit, in that land, always,
freedom from calamity and auspicious zeal prevailed on all sides. // SvayambhuP_10.162 //
Then that <s>Jayaśrī</s>, of great supernatural knowledge, a son of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: sarvānstān sāṃdhikān paśyan punarevaṃ samādiśat // SvayambhuP_10.163 //
children.translated_text: looking upon all those companions, instructed again thus: // SvayambhuP_10.163 //
"Wherever this sacred discourse on the <s>dharma</s> of <s>Svayambhū</s> is propagated,
there, by the power of that merit, may auspiciousness always prevail. // SvayambhuP_10.164 //
All the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> there, and the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,

children.text: arhanto bodhisattvāśca kurvantu maṃṅgalaṃ sadā // SvayambhuP_10.165 //
children.translated_text: <s>arhats</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, may they always bring auspiciousness. // SvayambhuP_10.165 //
All the lords of the worlds too, and all the great sages,

children.text: samālokya sadā tatra prakurvantu sumaṅgalaṃ // SvayambhuP_10.166 //
children.translated_text: looking upon it always, may they bring great auspiciousness there. // SvayambhuP_10.166 //
May the clouds rain in due season, and may the earth be rich with crops;

children.text: nirutpātaṃ subhikṣyaṃ ca bhavantu tatra sarvadā // SvayambhuP_10.167 //
children.translated_text: may there always be freedom from calamity and good harvest there. // SvayambhuP_10.167 //
May the king be righteous, may the ministers follow justice,
and may all the people be of good conduct, practitioners of <s>dharma</s>. // SvayambhuP_10.168 //
May all beings be of good conduct, with minds set on <s>saṃbodhi</s>,

children.text: triratnabhajanaṃ kṛtvā saṃcarantāṃ sadā śubhe // SvayambhuP_10.169 //
children.translated_text: and performing worship of the <s>Triratna</s>, may they always conduct themselves in auspiciousness." // SvayambhuP_10.169 //
Having heard this instruction of <s>Jayaśrī</s>, all the companions,
saying 'so be it,' rejoiced with serene minds. // SvayambhuP_10.170 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth chapter of the <s>Śrī Dharmadhātu Svayambhūtpatti Dharma Māhātmya Subhāṣita Sūtra</s> (the Well-Spoken Sūtra on the Greatness of the Dharma of the Arising of the Self-Existent Dharmadhātu).

children.text: ye dharmmā hetuprabhāvā hetu steṣāṃ tathāgataḥ hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and the cessation of these—thus speaks the great ascetic.

body.translated_text: May there be auspiciousness!

body.text: deyadharmo 'yaṃ pravaramahāyāyinaḥ śrīmatrudravarṇṇamahāvihārāvasthitaḥ paramopāsakaśrīśākyavaṃśodbhavaḥ śrīrāmānandena likhito 'gamat saṃpūrṇṇa //
body.translated_text: This religious gift belongs to the foremost great <s>Mahāyāna</s> practitioner, residing in the glorious <s>Rudravarṇa Mahāvihāra</s>, the supreme lay devotee born of the glorious <s>Śākya</s> lineage, written by the glorious <s>Rāmānanda</s>; it has been completed.
May there always be auspiciousness!

children.translated_text: In the Nepal era, in the year endowed with serpent-sage-taste (= 670),

children.text: cāṣāḍhe kṣīnacandre tu pañcamyāñca tithau śubhe // 1 //
children.translated_text: in the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, on the dark moon, on the auspicious fifth <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), // 1 //
it was completed at that time, written by the glorious <s>Rāmānanda</s>;
whether pure or impure, let it be corrected by the wise. // 2 //
Whatever merit is spoken of in writing, and whatever merit in reciting,
by that merit, may all the world attain the supreme <s>Bodhi</s> (enlightenment). // 3 //

body.text: śrīrāmānandayā pustaka juro / śubhaṃ / upasargga / maharādaharāścaiva śītarāpūṭaloka vā / upasarggī mahāmārī saptaite lokahārakaḥ // saṃvat 934 śrāvaṇa śukla // samāptam //
body.translated_text: The manuscript of the glorious <s>Rāmānanda</s>. Auspiciousness! Calamity: great drought, cold, epidemic of the people, or calamity, great plague—these seven are the destroyers of the world. // <s>Saṃvat</s> 934, <s>Śrāvaṇa Śukla</s> (bright half of Śrāvaṇa). Completed. //
